The more imperial the family, the stricter the rules. Sleeping in late was something Jiang Xuening could do at the manor, but Shen Zhiyi could hardly do it in the palace. After many years of palace life, when the time came to rise, she did not even need palace maids to wake her. She opened her eyes on her own, got up, and had palace attendants serve her while washing and dressing—clearly long accustomed to it all.

Probably because she had cried and vented last night, when she woke this morning, apart from somewhat swollen eyes, she had actually recovered her usual vitality.

Not only did she wash up on her own, but she also directed the palace attendants to serve Jiang Xuening.

Jiang Xuening had not slept well the night before last, and after last night’s ordeal, she appeared even more exhausted. But seeing that Shen Zhiyi had actually recovered her cheerful appearance, she could not very well show it and let her notice anything amiss, spoiling her precious good mood. So she forcibly ignored the throbbing tightness from both temples, hung a smile on her lips, and conversed with Shen Zhiyi while accepting the palace attendants’ service.

The palace attendants in Yangzhi Study did not serve their daily needs.

But Jiang Xuening had been Empress in her previous life, so being served by palace attendants did not make her uncomfortable. Only when she extremely naturally passed the brocade handkerchief back into that palace attendant’s hand and subconsciously waved for them to withdraw did a chill suddenly shoot up from the soles of her feet, making her shudder with cold.

Shen Zhiyi still had not noticed anything unusual.

The female official serving in the sleeping hall glanced at Jiang Xuening but asked somewhat awkwardly, “Your Highness, you kept Study Companion Jiang in the hall on a whim last night, but the palace attendants have not yet gone to Yangzhi Study to fetch Study Companion Jiang’s usual dresses. I wonder now…”

What should she wear?

Shen Zhiyi also turned to look. At this moment, Jiang Xuening stood there wearing only snow-white undergarments, her beautiful face bare without makeup. Perhaps because she had just woken up, she had a rather sickly, languid air, much like those beauty-afflicted ladies with lightly furrowed brows in scholars’ paintings.

She was truly too beautiful.

Her eyes could not help but light up. She immediately said to the female official, “Ningning’s figure is about the same as mine. Having her wear mine would naturally be best! Come, Ningning, I am going to pick out the most beautiful outfit for you!”

Jiang Xuening: ???

She had just been thinking about those pampered and privileged habits she had developed in Kunning Palace, not paying attention at all to what they were saying. Before she could react, she was already pulled by Shen Zhiyi to sit before the dressing mirror.

Next, she heard Shen Zhiyi calling out orders left and right.

One moment summoning this palace maid to powder her face and draw her brows, the next moment having that palace maid fetch a different set of palace attire, and then personally opening her own cosmetic box, comparing red ruby drop earrings and cloisonné bracelets against Jiang Xuening’s body.

For a moment, Jiang Xuening did not know whether to laugh or cry. She only felt that Shen Zhiyi was like a little girl who had suddenly acquired a doll, determined to dress her up beautifully before she’d be satisfied.

She was somewhat tired, so she did not have the energy to stop her.

She simply stood up and sat down intermittently, allowing her to manipulate as she pleased.

Shen Zhiyi changed to another pair of drop earrings to compare against her earlobes, only feeling that this pale purple glass-like misty clouds could only be supported by such a slender neck and snow-white complexion. It looked so beautiful that she could not bear to look away.

But as she watched, her previously spirited eyes drooped.

Jiang Xuening caught a glimpse and asked, “Does it not look good?”

Shen Zhiyi lowered her hand. Her gaze never left Jiang Xuening, but now held little drops of heartache. “It looks good, but it is just too beautiful. I cannot help but think that, with your nature of not competing or fighting, you still get schemed against in the palace. If later Yan Lin is also gone, who will be there to protect you?”

Jiang Xuening was speechless.

But Shen Zhiyi began thinking unusually seriously. Her eyes rolled around, then suddenly brightened. She actually asked, “What do you think of my Royal Brother?”

Shen Jie?!

Jiang Xuening’s eyelid twitched. She immediately recalled the trajectory of her fate in her previous life. Without thinking, she immediately said, “Many thanks for Your Highness’s regard. Prince Linzi is naturally refined and magnanimous. Xuening, being of humble birth, only wishes for a peaceful life. You must not joke about such things.”

Shen Zhiyi was very puzzled. “What’s wrong with my Royal Brother?”

In her heart, Jiang Xuening thought, “Your Royal Brother is fine in every way, just not suitable for me.”

Thinking of this idea made Shen Zhiyi very excited. The palace was full of her people, so she was not afraid of being overheard by others. She squatted directly before her and said, “Really, Ningning, I heard from Mother and Imperial Brother that soon they will be selecting a consort for my Royal Brother. If you could become my Royal Brother’s princess consort, then in the future, my Royal Brother will most likely be named Crown Prince by my Imperial Brother, and later will also live in the palace. That way, you’d also live in the palace. Would we not be able to live together every day, see each other constantly, eat together, play together, and sleep together?”

Her eyes were both sparkling bright.

Jiang Xuening recalled that in this life, Shen Zhiyi had been extremely sincere toward her. She wanted to refuse directly, but facing such a gaze, when the words reached her lips, she found them rather difficult to speak.

But if she did not make it clear…

The matter of entering the palace as a study companion through unexpected circumstances, even though her name had not been submitted, surfaced in her mind once more, immediately followed by everything she had experienced since entering the palace, as well as everything that would happen in the future.

She was truly afraid and weary.

Having experienced the prosperity of her previous life, Jiang Xuening truly did not want to repeat the same mistakes.

She suddenly used an unprecedentedly serious gaze to look back at Shen Zhiyi, gently taking that string of purple glass drop earrings from her hand and placing them back in the cosmetic box, saying, “Xuening was exceptionally summoned into the palace by Your Highness. The great efforts involved, Your Highness surely understands better than I. Then Your Highness should also understand that the person the Jiang manor initially reported for palace entry was not me. To receive Your Highness’s favor, be summoned by imperial decree to enter the palace, and receive Your Highness’s abundant care while serving—to know Your Highness, Xuening is also very happy. But palace life is not what Xuening enjoys. Xuening is of humble birth, without great ambitions, and only wishes to return to the countryside of childhood, to give free rein to my heart…”

Shen Zhiyi froze.

She had not expected Jiang Xuening to say such words.

The string of purple glass was gone from her hand, replaced by her palm with its faint warmth.

But a surge of anger rose from the bottom of her heart.

Shen Zhiyi wanted to say, “I’ve treated you so well; how dare you think of leaving?” but upon touching Jiang Xuening’s warm and sincere gaze, the anger that had just risen was pressed down like being suppressed by gently flowing water, slowly extinguished, transforming instead into a bit of loneliness and pitifulness.

She said, “You do not like the palace?”

Jiang Xuening said, “The days here are very unpleasant.”

Shen Zhiyi held her breath. “Then you tell me—whoever makes you unhappy, I will give them all a quick end so you can be happy!”

Such a childish temper.

Her eyes widened greatly, her fine brows raised up. Though there was an old scar beneath the corner of her eye, it did not diminish her noble bearing as a Princess. Only her cheeks puffed out on both sides, her lips pressed tightly together, clearly unwilling to let the matter rest.

Jiang Xuening was utterly helpless.

She immediately feared that if this topic continued, it would instead provoke her temper, and she’d give herself a “might as well go all in” situation, secretly arranging for her to marry Shen Jie. Then there’d be nowhere to seek justice. So she sighed and wanted to change the subject, saying, “Let’s still look at what to wear today. The drop earrings are also quite pretty…”

But Shen Zhiyi was not so easily fooled.

She simply liked Jiang Xuening as a playmate.

While dressing her up, she racked her brains, exhausting her wits trying to pry information from her mouth, asking, “Are the palace attendants at Yangzhi Study not treating you well? Did those dogs from the Imperial Household Department mistreat you with rations? Did that one called You Yue bully you again? Just tell me—exactly who made you unhappy? Ningning…”

This stance—clearly, if Jiang Xuening named one person, she’d go eliminate that person!

Cold sweat broke out on Jiang Xuening’s forehead.

But Shen Zhiyi’s questions came one after another, each guess more outlandish than the last.

Her mouth suddenly chattered on endlessly, just like a garrulous mynah bird.

Jiang Xuening looked up to the heavens and sighed.

For the first time, she so badly wanted to give herself a big slap across the face: if she had known, she could have directly told Shen Zhiyi, “I would rather be Your Highness’s study companion than Your Highness’s imperial sister-in-law.” Most likely, Shen Zhiyi would have been delighted to immediately abandon the idea of having her marry Shen Jie. Why would she need to be interrogated over and over like now?

Sincere feelings got struck by lightning!

Finally, after Shen Zhiyi voiced her twenty-third outlandish guess, Jiang Xuening could not withstand the test of temptation and tentatively said, “Since Your Highness cares so much about whether I am happy or not, then I will…just say it. Actually, leaving the palace would make me happy…”

Shen Zhiyi gave her a sweet smile. “Ningning, you are dreaming.”

Jiang Xuening: “…”

Shen Zhiyi hung the string of purple glass earrings on her, very cheerfully coaxing her, “Pick another one, pick another one—this Princess will definitely make it happen for you!”

Jiang Xuening silently shed tears in her heart. After pondering for a long time, a bold-as-brass idea suddenly popped into her head: “Then what makes me most unhappy is learning the zither. Teacher Xie keeps dragging me off to learn the zither every other day, and his requirements are extremely strict…”

Shen Zhiyi: “…”

Jiang Xuening blinked. “You said you’d definitely make it happen.”

Shen Zhiyi: “…”

This time, it was Shen Zhiyi’s turn to silently shed tears in her heart. All the civil and military officials knew Teacher Xie’s standing in scholarship. One should know that her studying in the palace caused widespread criticism throughout the court. If Teacher Xie had not approved, it probably could not have happened. Moreover, with Teacher Xie’s usual teaching manner, even if she had a hundred times more courage, she would not dare act presumptuously before him or forbid him from dragging Jiang Xuening off to learn the zither!

But anything could be lost—Grand Princess Leyang’s face could not be lost!

Shen Zhiyi forcibly suppressed her guilty conscience and said with stern righteousness, “For Teacher Xie to be so earnest in teaching you, when court affairs keep him so busy, yet he still takes most of an hour every day to teach you the zither—this is something others would envy but cannot have. How can you dislike Teacher Xie for being strict? Too excessive!”

Jiang Xuening wanted to speak, “But—”

Shen Zhiyi cut in, “If you say one more word, I will tell Teacher Xie that you dislike learning the zither!”

Jiang Xuening: “…”

I never knew before that you’d actually threaten people with tattling?!

She was dumbfounded.

But Shen Zhiyi coughed once and said without blushing or her heart racing, “Oh my, this Princess is not omnipotent. Besides these two things, if there’s anyone else who makes you unhappy, speak up. This Princess will definitely uphold justice for you!”

After thinking for a long while, Jiang Xuening managed to squeeze out, “There’s nothing else.”

Only when fully dressed and made up, eating breakfast together with Shen Zhiyi, did she look at the pastry in her bowl with rose filling formed into half an orchid flower, pick it up, take a small bite, and then slowly lower her eyelids.

Shen Zhiyi asked, “What’s wrong?”

Jiang Xuening’s gaze flickered slightly. Looking at that small piece of pastry, she only said, “It’s nothing. I just suddenly remembered that my elder sister at home also makes such pastries. For a moment, I miss her a bit…”

After saying this, she changed the subject and continued eating.

But Shen Zhiyi lowered her eyes in thought for a moment, seriously committing this sentence to memory.

After breakfast, the two went to Fengchen Hall to study.

When they arrived, the others were already there early.

Everyone was talking when they heard Grand Princess Leyang was coming, and all turned to look.

But who would have expected that with this look, their gazes could not be withdrawn—

Only these gazes did not fall on Grand Princess Leyang but fell on Jiang Xuening!

Having been in the palace for some time, the study companions mostly wore the clothes they had brought when they came.

Jiang Xuening’s usual attire tended even more toward plain elegance—somewhat willfully relying on her good foundation to be lazy about dressing up. But today she came from Mingfeng Palace, wearing palace attire that the palace attendants had spent a long time selecting from what Shen Zhiyi had worn in the past.

Snow-white fabric was pressed with layer upon layer of fine gold thread.

Dark blue crane-and-cloud patterns climbed up from the hem of the dress. The flowing water patterns on both wide sleeves were like piled brocade. A piece of exquisite white jade pendant hung at her waist. Only the moon-white embroidered peony sachet was her own.

Her face was even more exquisite and dazzling.

Her complexion was already fair. With drawn brows and painted eyes, lips touched with vermilion, with every glance her spirit seemed to fly—every frown and smile appeared soul-stirring.

But what was even more surprising was the feeling she gave.

There was none of the discomfort or unsuitability of a young girl secretly wearing splendid garments. Wearing this palace attire, her originally careless, frivolous casualness seemed to unconsciously restrain itself by two parts. Supporting herself on a palace attendant’s hand as she approached step by step, she actually displayed a kind of stern nobility belonging to one dwelling in the nine-layered palace.

Xiao Shu looked at her for quite a while without reacting.

But Grand Princess Leyang happily showed off to everyone—this was the result of her morning’s work.

Seeing Jiang Xuening’s bearing and her countenance after such elaborate dressing, everyone was shocked in their hearts and also felt somewhat sour, but on the surface, they had to chime in with praise. For a moment, it was all as complicated as if five-flavor bottles had been knocked over.

Before leaving Mingfeng Palace, Jiang Xuening had also looked in the mirror. She only felt that this luxurious palace attire worn on her body was beautiful, certainly beautiful, but it was like a nightmare. Looking through the dressing mirror, what she saw was not herself but the Empress from her previous life who could neither advance nor retreat, whose eyes were dazzled by prosperity.

She had wanted to change outfits.

But seeing it was almost time for class, and there was no time to change again, she had no choice but to wear this outfit to Fengchen Hall.

She had not slept all night, and her thoughts were also in turmoil. She attended the class absent-mindedly. Not until the class ended and she saw everyone place zithers on the zither tables did she suddenly remember that the next class was Xie Wei teaching zither.

So she pinched the space between her brows, which woke her up a bit.

That Jiao’an was still placed in the side hall. After leaving the hall, Jiang Xuening headed toward the side hall.

Unexpectedly, today, Xie Wei was actually in the side hall very early.

The young eunuch at the hall entrance looked at her with some surprise. After announcing through the door, he opened it to let her in.

Jiang Xuening entered.

Xie Wei had no court lectures this morning and did not want to stay in the Grand Secretariat arguing with that bunch of old men, so he had come to the side hall to handle official documents. At this moment, he was rising to take down his own “Emei” from the wall. Turning his head to see Jiang Xuening, he also froze for a moment.

Jiang Xuening greeted him, “Teacher Xie, good day.”

But Xie Wei’s gaze lingered on her for a long time, examining her clothing and makeup. His brows gradually furrowed tightly, and he only said, “Not good-looking.”

After saying this, he cradled Emei at an angle and walked toward the hall entrance.

“…”

Jiang Xuening stood in place, practically with a head full of grievances.

What was wrong with this person?

Although she herself also felt this outfit was very unlikeable, hearing these words came from Xie Wei’s mouth—why did it sound so grating? What did a stinking man know about the depths and subtleties of a young lady’s makeup and clothing that he dared to comment?

Moreover, how could she possibly…Not! Look! Good!?

That Xie fellow deserved his usual reading of Buddhist scriptures and Daoist texts. In his previous life, he did not even touch women—he probably was not liked by young ladies to begin with! He deserved not being able to get a wife!

CONTENT END 79

chapters.title: Fell Asleep
chapters.content:
Recently, the zither lessons had basically been teaching right-hand finger techniques. After learning each technique, they were given corresponding zither pieces to practice. Xie Wei’s requirements were very strict—no one dared to be careless.

Even Shen Zhiyi was very well-behaved in class.

Only Jiang Xuening, during today’s class, stared with her eyes wide open. Since she was not allowed to touch the zither anyway, she simply sat in the corner of the back third row, coldly eyeing Xie Wei, as if wanting to bore a hole through him with her gaze.

For a moment, Xie Wei did not understand what she was trying to do.

Fortunately, Jiang Xuening had not rested well for two nights in a row. Her eyes felt somewhat sore. After glaring at him for a while, drowsiness surged up. Before long, she could not hold on anymore and yawned. Being able to persist without closing her eyes and collapsing onto the desk to sleep already required tremendous willpower—she could not muster any more energy to glare at him.

Another class passed in a daze.

When class ended, everyone already knew that Jiang Xuening’s learning the zither always meant being dragged along by Teacher Xie. No one wanted to stay here and spend more time with him, so they all scattered in a flash.

But Jiang Xuening could not escape.

Xie Wei walked down from the hall carrying his zither and asked, “Why were you glaring at me?”

Jiang Xuening had finally made it through class and was just about to yawn when hearing these words. She had no choice but to forcibly hold it back and defend herself, “How could that be? You must have seen wrong. How would this student dare do such a thing?”

Xie Wei said flatly, “Not only dare to do it, but now dare to lie about it too.”

Jiang Xuening forced a smile. “Then it must be that this student was earnestly listening to your lecture, momentarily engrossed, harboring such admiration for you that I stared blankly.”

Xie Wei remained unmoved. “Is that so?”

Seeing his indifferent manner, Jiang Xuening grew irritated. She immediately recalled how this person had frowned earlier, saying she “did not look good,” and so secretly harbored some vengeful thoughts. Smiling exceptionally sweetly, she said, “It could also be that Teacher Xie’s lecture today was dry and boring, extremely poor, so this student listened in complete confusion and unconsciously could only stare at you.”

Xie Wei: “…”

Dry and boring, listened in complete confusion!

If previously his entire person had maintained a composed manner, after hearing these two sentences from Jiang Xuening, his expression immediately darkened, and even the temperature in his eyes dropped several degrees.

No one had ever evaluated him this way—

Since returning to the capital four years ago and presiding over court lectures at the Wenyuan Pavilion, whether teachers or students, whether colleagues or the Emperor, everyone praised him highly. This was the first time he had encountered such a troublemaker as Jiang Xuening, who could lie with her eyes wide open.

His heart caught for a moment. Xie Wei’s thin lips pressed into a flat, straight line. For an instant, he wanted to lose his temper.

But when his gaze fell back on Jiang Xuening, though the impulse came, he restrained it.

He said unperturbed, “Spacing out and nearly falling asleep yourself, unable to understand, yet blaming the teacher for not knowing how to teach—that is quite a skill.”

Jiang Xuening’s smile did not change. “You are right.”

Almost shameless in flavor—whatever Xie Wei said, that was what it was.

Xie Wei was too lazy to quibble with her, so he walked toward the hall entrance.

But unexpectedly, the moment he turned around, Jiang Xuening lightly gritted her teeth behind his back and muttered in a small voice, “A crude fellow who cannot even get himself a wife, with no appreciation—yet still has the gall to say I do not look good! How capable you are!”

“What did you say?”

Xie Wei’s footsteps halted. He directly turned his head back to look at her.

The back of Jiang Xuening’s neck went cold. She hurriedly clutched her zither and caught up, as if the person who had just been muttering was not her at all. Extraordinarily obsequious, she walked to Xie Wei’s side and said, “This student said she herself is just a crude fellow who does not know how to appreciate anything. Fortunately, Teacher Xie is kind-hearted and willing to give me extra guidance. Let’s go learn zither now.”

“…”

Did she really think he was hard of hearing?

Xie Wei stared at her for quite a while, feeling this student had a bit of that “if you do not discipline for three days, she will tear the roof tiles off” restless energy. Recalling the various domineering rumors about her in the marketplaces over the years, he only felt he should restrain her a bit, lest she think him easy to get along with and become increasingly presumptuous.

But when about to lose his temper, he saw her looking at him with bright, sparkling eyes.

This appearance was truly the picture of obedience.

The reprimanding words reached Xie Wei’s lips, but could not be spoken. In the end, he swallowed them back, only flicked his wide sleeve, and said, “As long as you know who is teacher and who is student, that is good. Let’s go.”

He turned around.

Jiang Xuening stuck her tongue out at his back before following.

They arrived once more at the side hall of Fengchen Hall.

Xie Wei placed Emei on another zither table, only saying, “These past days, the teaching has all been right-hand finger techniques. Having finished teaching today, you should by rights have a slight understanding of right-hand techniques and be able to play the corresponding zither pieces. When I played the zither in the hall, you sat very far away and probably could not see the finger techniques clearly. So now I will play once more. You must carefully observe the details of the finger techniques. After I finish playing, you will practice and play it once for me to hear.”

Jiang Xuening immediately felt overwhelmed.

But Xie Wei only asked her, “Did you understand?”

Jiang Xuening sat before her own zither table and very sincerely nodded, saying, “I understood.”

The Way of the zither, for Xie Wei, came as easily as breathing.

He played “Colorful Clouds Chasing the Moon,” which he had demonstrated for everyone in the main hall of Fengchen Hall today.

The zither music flowed like gurgling water.

This kind of zither piece, suitable for practicing finger techniques, had a simple and light rhythm, like water droplets bouncing on clear spring water or like bamboo leaves drifting down along a stream. It was not complex—when played by Xie Wei, it already had a flavor of returning to simplicity.

When playing the zither, he was always single-mindedly focused.

When the music finally ended, he slowly lowered both palms, pressing down the lingering notes of this leisurely piece, raised his head, and said, “Did you see clea—”

The next syllable, “rly,” got stuck in his throat, abruptly cutting off.

Xie Wei’s expression suddenly became extremely poor—

At the zither table beside him, Jiang Xuening, who had been sitting upright when they first came in and who moments ago had opened her eyes wide and answered, “I understood,” had at some unknown point collapsed entirely.

The zither table was only so big.

After her face collapsed onto it, the Jiao’an ancient zither resting on top was squeezed askew to one side. Her two arms were raised to pillow under her head, her eyes had long since closed, and even her breathing had become even.

She had actually fallen directly asleep!

Xie Wei’s fingers, still pressed on the zither strings, suddenly became somewhat heavy. Fearing he might accidentally snap a string if not careful, he slowly lifted his fingers.

His expression also slowly became blank.

There was no disciplinary ruler in the side hall, but on the writing desk was today’s sheet music. He stood up, picked up that music book, rolled it along its spine in his palm into a cylinder, and walked toward Jiang Xuening, wanting to wake her.

Only when he walked over, stood beside her, and raised that music book rolled into a tube shape, wanting to “invite” her to wake up, for some reason, he paused.

Palace attire was complex—it looked splendid, but wearing it was heavy.

Yet the young lady’s figure was very slender.

When standing or sitting, with spine held straight, eyes glancing about brilliantly, it did not seem like much. But at this moment, pillowing her own arms, collapsed like this, sleeping on the narrow zither table, she naturally curled herself into a small bundle.

This splendid palace attire thus suddenly seemed like a suit of hard armor.

But hidden inside…

Was only a fragile little thing.

The young lady must have been extremely tired. Even beneath the powder dusted under her eyelids, one could see traces of weary, pale blue.

Eyes closed, fine brows lowered.

Some of the bright lip rouge had smudged onto the palace attire’s sleeve due to her collapsed position, looking like several fallen flower petals or like a dropped paintbrush that had randomly streaked across paper.

A string of fine purple glass drop earrings rested beside her ear against her cheek.

The light from outside was not very bright. Passing through that translucent purple glass, it refracted several strands of gentle and brilliant light, reflecting onto her snow-white skin.

These past days, when he lectured in the hall, Jiang Xuening had always listened with ears perked.

Even when called to this side hall to practice, she had always been obedient without complaint.

But today, the moment he was not paying attention, she had collapsed and fallen asleep.

Xie Wei’s gaze fell on her curled and thick eyelashes and also on her slightly furrowed brows. He only wondered if she was having some nightmare. After a long while, he ultimately withdrew the sheet music that was just about to tap her head. But standing beside the deeply sleeping young lady, for a moment, he did not quite know what to do.

Such a troublesome student…

This really was the first time teaching one.

If he had known it would be like this, why give himself this trouble? Whether Jiang Xuening learned badly or not—what did it have to do with him anyway…

He sneered inwardly.

Though he could not help wondering if this little girl had played and made noise too late last night without knowing to rest, which was why she was so sleepy today, ever since experiencing that incident with “Admonitions for Women” and misunderstanding her once, he would never again rashly jump to conclusions so easily.

After standing beside her for quite a while, Xie Wei could not resist—he shook his head and smiled soundlessly.

He actually did not plan to wake her, letting her sleep.

Only he had not expected that the moment he turned around, preparing to take advantage of this time to continue handling some official documents, someone outside knocked on the door, saying to those inside, “Teacher Xie, His Majesty is in Qianqing Palace currently in conference and requests you come over.”

It was a somewhat deep eunuch’s voice.

Probably completely not expecting someone might be sleeping inside, the voice was somewhat loud, without any attempt to lower it.

Xie Wei frowned as soon as he heard and subconsciously turned his head to look at Jiang Xuening.

Jiang Xuening was in a dream, barefoot in the water, catching shrimp. Just as she was happily occupied, she heard “Qianqing Palace” and froze. That big shrimp thus slipped out of her hands. She grew anxious, lunged forward forcefully, her head following with a nod forward, and immediately woke up.

Her whole person still had not reacted.

She sat up abruptly, only shouting, “My fish! My shrimp!”

Then, looking up, she met Xie Wei’s eyes that had suddenly become complex and indescribable.

Jiang Xuening: “…”

The zither lay before her, and Xie Wei stood before her.

She suddenly felt her heart go ice cold through and through, and she herself also went ice cold through and through.

Recalling how he had earlier suspected she was having a nightmare, Xie Wei suddenly felt he had been somewhat excessively benevolent lately. At this moment, he only looked at her quietly and smiled slightly, “You have your fish, you have your shrimp. How about I go to the Imperial Kitchen and request a chef for Young Lady Ning’er to prepare a feast of delicacies from land and sea?”

CONTENT END 80

chapters.title: Satisfaction
chapters.content:
What fish, what shrimp!

Even if you gave Jiang Xuening a hundred times the courage, she would not dare to eat them now!

However…

The moment food was mentioned, she could not help but think of those peach pastries. If it were this man before her who personally served them and told her to eat, well, that might not be unacceptable?

No, no, no—she had to dismiss such dangerous thoughts quickly!

Xie Wei was already wary of her knowing things about him that others did not know. If she accidentally let something slip, heaven knew where his mind would go, and if her words truly brought disaster upon herself, that would be terrible.

With this thought, Jiang Xuening’s face broke into an awkward smile. Her heart uneasy, she carefully defended herself, “Last night I slept in Grand Princess’s bedchamber. I was not quite accustomed to it, so that is why I was drowsy today…”

Xie Wei’s brow moved slightly. “At the Grand Princess’s?”

Jiang Xuening nodded with unusual sincerity, then raised her arm. The wide, exquisite palace dress sleeves unfurled as she said, “Really, look, even these clothes were found for me by the Grand Princess.”

The young woman’s gaze toward him still showed some timidity, as though she knew she had committed a grave error. But there was no intention to argue or deny it—though she did offer reasons for herself…

Xie Wei looked at her palace attire, his furrowed brow not relaxing.

But when he spoke, his voice was much calmer than before, “If you did not sleep well, go back and take a nap. I happen to have matters to attend to today anyway.”

Jiang Xuening was delighted, not expecting Xie Wei to be so reasonable. She was about to heap praise on him, “Teacher Xie is truly understanding and reasonable…”

But before she could finish, Xie Wei calmly added, “Today’s missed lesson will be made up tomorrow.”

Jiang Xuening: “…”

She should have known! This person, surnamed Xie, would naturally be this unforgiving! She had gotten happy too soon!

Xie Wei watched with his own eyes as the smile forming on the young woman’s lips froze, and the brightness that had just appeared on her face instantly dimmed. The gloom that had been piled up in his heart somehow dispersed a little. He said, “The fingering techniques I taught today, you must know them by tomorrow. If you do not…”

Jiang Xuening immediately nodded vigorously like a pecking chicken, “I will, I will, I definitely will!”

Xie Wei suppressed a smile, flatly hummed an acknowledgment, and strode out of the side hall first, heading toward the Qianqing Palace together with the eunuch who had come earlier to announce His Majesty’s summons.

Only after watching him walk away did Jiang Xuening slowly breathe a sigh of relief. “That scared me to death!”

*

At this very moment in the Jiang residence, someone else had also received a fright.

This afternoon, Lady Meng was taking Jiang Xuehui to Hanshan Temple to pray for blessings.

Before departing, they sat in the room drinking tea and talking.

Lady Meng recalled how Jiang Boyou’s words had defended Jiang Xuening, and she sighed softly, saying, “Originally, the name submitted for the study companion position from our household was yours, but somehow Ning’er ended up going instead. She follows Wan-niang and has learned an intolerant temperament. I fear that in the future, she will only make things harder for you. Now that the Yongyi Marquis household has met with disaster and Prince Linzi is soon to select a consort, I only hope that today you can draw a good fortune lot and have some good luck.”

Jiang Xuehui sat below her but did not speak.

Her gaze lowered, falling only on the embroidered handkerchief on her lap. Even now, she could not quite fathom the meaning behind Jiang Xuening’s words that day.

Just then, the household steward suddenly rushed in to announce, “Madam, a eunuch from the palace has arrived!”

Lady Meng and Jiang Xuehui both stood up almost simultaneously.

Lady Meng’s face went pale, her voice trembling. “Is it court business? Has something happened to the master? Or has Ning’er caused trouble in the palace again?”

How would the steward know?

It was just that everyone in the Jiang household knew their Second Young Lady had experienced an extremely dangerous encounter in the palace some days ago. With recent unrest at court as well, now that someone from the palace had come, they could not help but think the worst.

But unexpectedly, the eunuch who entered had a face full of smiles. He bowed and said, “Greetings, Madam. Greetings, Eldest Young Lady. This servant has come from the palace on Grand Princess Leyang’s orders to specifically summon the Elder Young Lady Jiang to enter the palace as a study companion. Please, Eldest Young Lady, make some brief preparations and accompany this servant to the palace. Her Highness the Grand Princess is waiting most anxiously.”

The visitor was Huang Renli, who served at Shen Zhiyi’s side.

However, neither Lady Meng nor Jiang Xuehui recognized him. Upon hearing these words, both were momentarily shocked and uncertain.

Lady Meng could hardly believe it. “Out of the blue, why would Her Highness the Grand Princess summon our eldest daughter to the palace?”

At this point, she was even somewhat fearful.

She only said, “Could it be that our household’s second daughter has caused some trouble?”

Huang Renli had just come from the palace and was completely clear about last night’s events when Jiang Xuening was kept overnight by Her Highness the Grand Princess. Hearing Lady Meng’s words, he raised his eyebrows with some surprise, and the smile on his face faded somewhat as he said, “Madam need not worry excessively. Our Highness is extremely fond of Second Young Lady Jiang. She even kept Second Young Lady overnight in the palace last night. It was just that this morning, when the Second Young Lady was having pastries, she mentioned thinking of the pastries made by the Eldest Young Lady. Our Highness took this to heart, guessing that she missed her family. That is why she sent this servant to fetch the Eldest Young Lady to the palace, to also keep Her Highness company as a study companion. This way, seeing each other daily, she will not think about leaving the palace.”

“…”

Lady Meng choked and immediately fell silent.

Grand Princess Leyang was having Jiang Xuehui enter the palace, but it was not because she liked Jiang Xuehui, nor because Jiang Xuehui’s talents were particularly outstanding—it was simply because Jiang Xuening casually mentioned something while having pastries this morning!

Jiang Xuehui was even more astonished.

She herself knew clearly how much Jiang Xuening had detested her since returning to the capital, unwilling to even give her a pleasant expression. Yet now she had actually told Grand Princess Leyang that she thought of the pastries she made…

Jiang Xuehui indeed knew how to make pastries.

But heaven knew she had once presented them to Jiang Xuening, only to have Jiang Xuening dump all the desserts she had made on the ground right in front of her! Then she smiled somewhat awkwardly and said to her, “I am sorry; I was not careful and spilled them. What a waste of your kind intentions.”

But her reaction was extremely quick.

Lady Meng’s hesitation had already caused Huang Renli to furrow his brow slightly.

Jiang Xuehui immediately bowed and said, “To receive Her Highness the Grand Princess’s favor, Xuehui thanks Her Highness for this grace. I will prepare immediately and accompany the eunuch.”

Huang Renli thought to himself that this young lady was rather clever, so he nodded, his expression relaxing somewhat.

*

Having barely escaped disaster under Xie Wei’s hand, Jiang Xuening returned from Fengchen Hall’s side hall to Yangzhi Study. Without even eating lunch, she dove straight into her bed, closed her eyes, and slept soundly.

It was not until the afternoon when palace servants came to wake her that she finally arose.

It turned out that Grand Princess Leyang had recently developed a playful mood and had called the palace servants from her own palace to play pitch-pot together. She had also come to Yangzhi Study to call the study companions to join them.

Everyone had entered the palace primarily to accompany Shen Zhiyi in her studies and secondarily to be her good playmates.

When Shen Zhiyi extended an invitation, who would dare not go?

Jiang Xuening had slept just the right amount, so she quickly got up to wash and dress, then went with everyone to Mingfeng Palace.

Shen Zhiyi was playing wildly with people, and the palace servants, who rarely saw her happy, were accompanying her in play.

The moment Jiang Xuening stepped into the hall, the corner of her mouth twitched.

She did not know where Shen Zhiyi had learned such tricks, but some palace servants had long paper strips stuck to their faces, and some even had their faces painted with ink brushes, looking rather dejected—clearly they had lost and received “punishment.”

As soon as the study companions arrived, they were immediately pulled into the game by her.

Naturally, some were eager to seize this opportunity to curry favor with Shen Zhiyi and were therefore very enthusiastic.

But not Jiang Xuening.

She had not eaten at noon and was feeling somewhat hungry. Seeing that there were still some candied fruits and pastries displayed in the hall, she did not rush forward. Instead, she slacked off and muddled through. While everyone played and frolicked in front, she sat in the back eating first.

Shen Zhiyi naturally spotted her at a glance, but seeing her sitting there eating, she thoughtfully did not call her over.

Everyone first played a round of pitch-pot.

Shen Zhiyi held arrows in her hand and usually hit the target with each throw. She was quite skilled, often winning everyone’s applause. Jiang Xuening cheered along from afar.

But someone could not stand seeing her so leisurely and called out to her, “Is Second Young Lady Jiang not going to play? I heard you used to frequent the marketplaces often. Games like pitch-pot—you must be most skilled at them, right? Would you not come show us your skills?”

Jiang Xuening looked up and saw it was Chen Shuyi.

This young lady from a great family had a faint smile at the corner of her mouth, gazing at her with meaningful eyes, her expression looking mocking no matter how you viewed it.

Jiang Xuening had just taken a small bite of the candied fruit in her hand. She gently set it down and was about to speak.

Unexpectedly, Shen Zhiyi furrowed her brow and directly said to Chen Shuyi, “Can you not see Ningning is eating? She will come play when she’s finished eating. Why are you being so nosy?”

These words were far too impolite!

Everyone was stunned!

Chen Shuyi herself had not expected this. Her mouth opened slightly, momentarily at a loss for what to do.

One must know that Chen Shuyi was, after all, the precious daughter of Grand Scholar Chen. Her status was quite noble, and she usually played with Xiao Shu. Who in the palace would not give her some face?

Even Shen Zhiyi had always been pleasant and agreeable toward her in the past.

Yet now, just for asking Jiang Xuening one question, she was directly reprimanded?

Chen Shuyi’s face could not maintain its composure, turning red then white. She hesitantly tried to defend herself, “Your Highness, I did not…”

Shen Zhiyi’s face showed no expression, coldly saying, “If that was not your intention, then shut your mouth.”

The hall instantly fell silent.

Jiang Xuening also stared at Shen Zhiyi in a daze.

Anyone with eyes could see that Grand Princess Leyang’s mood did not seem very good, and her words were completely defending Jiang Xuening. She was not willing to give even half a face to someone like Chen Shuyi, a young lady from such a distinguished family.

Just what ability did Jiang Xuening possess to bewitch people like this?

You Yue had formed a great enmity with Jiang Xuening during the rest period and hated her to the bone. But she no longer dared speak out or make any moves, fearing she would fall into Jiang Xuening’s trap. So at this moment, she could only use her eyes to express her contempt and indignation toward Jiang Xuening.

Then…

Before she could even think about what expression she should make when Jiang Xuening turned her gaze over—what look would provoke the other party’s displeasure and anger—Shen Zhiyi had already caught her eye.

Shen Zhiyi stared at her for a moment, then raised her eyebrow. “What do you mean by looking at Ningning with that kind of expression?”

You Yue: ??????

She was completely dumbfounded.

Not daring to speak was one thing, not being able to act was another, but now she could not even use her eyes?!

You Yue was so frightened she immediately withdrew her gaze, trembling, “I…I…”

Shen Zhiyi did not listen at all. “If you look at Ningning with that kind of expression again, I will have someone gouge out your eyeballs!”

You Yue shuddered, cold sweat breaking out on her forehead. Her face instantly turned deathly pale. She was practically ready to kneel on the ground to beg forgiveness. Now she did not even dare raise her head once, only repeatedly saying, “Yes, yes.”

First, Chen Shuyi was immediately scolded for doing nothing, then You Yue received a terrifying threat for just one glance. The other study companions all sensed something was wrong with the atmosphere.

Most people did not dare speak.

But Yao Xi glanced at Chen Shuyi, then at You Yue, and gently spoke, trying to mediate, “Sister Shuyi probably meant no harm, and Second Young Lady You only glanced once. Perhaps Your Highness the Grand Princess has misunderstood?”

“Misunderstood?”

Shen Zhiyi had not truly wanted to play pitch-pot today when she called them here. This morning’s words from Jiang Xuening about “these days here have not been comfortable”—she had not forgotten. Previously, she had not paid close attention, but now, secretly observing with care, she had seen many telltale signs.

She let out a cold laugh.

She was still holding the brush used earlier to paint the faces of palace servants who had lost. She slowly paced over to Yao Xi and looked her up and down, saying, “Young Lady Yao is quite compassionate toward heaven and merciful toward people. How about I report to my Imperial Brother and simply send you to Baiyun Convent to become a nun so that your compassionate heart can have some place to be useful?”

Yao Xi had not shown any malice toward Jiang Xuening at all—she had merely stood up to speak a word on behalf of Chen Shuyi and You Yue!

Yet she was threatened with being sent to become a nun!

What young lady could face such a thing?

Everyone gasped.

Yao Xi even less expected that speaking a word of fairness would get her rebuked. A mix of hatred and fear rose in her heart. The fingers hanging at her side quietly clenched. Her situation became extremely awkward, yet she did not dare to say another word.

The candied fruit was still in Jiang Xuening’s mouth, carrying a sweet-and-sour taste.

But now she was so shocked she could not swallow it.

Her gaze wandered among everyone, then fell back on Shen Zhiyi. She had no idea what madness this noble princess was exhibiting, attacking everyone she saw.

Although she felt…

This was absolutely satisfying!

As Shen Zhiyi turned her eyes and caught her gaze, which held a trace of admiration, a flush of red immediately flew across her face. She felt as if she were floating on clouds, about to fly away. So she pretended to casually avoid that gaze.

But when she turned to face the others, her face was completely ice-cold.

She actually proclaimed loudly, “I’ve said before that whoever dares offend Ningning should not blame me for being impolite. I never thought some people would treat my words as wind passing by their ears. Do not think I called you here today to have fun. I called you here precisely to warn you all—as long as it is something this Princess can manage, whoever makes Ningning uncomfortable, I will make her ten times, a hundred times more uncomfortable!”

The arrows for pitch-pot still lay on the table.

The palace servants’ faces still had paper strips stuck to them, painted with ink marks.

But the earlier playfulness and laughter had been completely swept away.

All the study companions finally understood at this point—today’s summons was to establish authority!

All for Jiang Xuening alone!

For a moment, everyone harbored their own thoughts, but after hearing Shen Zhiyi’s earlier rebukes, not a single person dared open their mouth to object or speak up for anyone. Without exception, all were trembling with fear.

Xiao Shu remained relatively composed.

She merely quietly withdrew her gaze from Jiang Xuening. When she lowered her head, she could not help but feel additional wariness and displeasure. Because Shen Zhiyi’s warning undoubtedly included her as well.

However, her status was different after all.

With Empress Dowager Xiao present, she did not particularly fear Shen Zhiyi’s words, nor was she as foolish as those other few.

“Reporting to Your Highness, the person has been brought.”

Just at this moment, Huang Renli entered the hall with a joyful smile on his face, holding his whisk. He bowed and paid respects to Shen Zhiyi, reporting thus.

Everyone could not help but look at him.

They were quite puzzled for a moment: A person had been brought—who?

Shen Zhiyi’s expression immediately relaxed, as if she too became happy. She actually walked to Jiang Xuening’s side and said to Huang Renli, “Have the person come in and give Ningning a surprise!”

Huang Renli then waved his hand.

Jiang Xuehui, who had been waiting outside, collected her thoughts, bowed, and stepped in from outside the hall. Her eyes looked straight ahead without glancing sideways. She did not dare look around. Her hands, clasping an embroidered handkerchief, folded in front of her body. She walked straight forward and bowed in greeting, “Subject woman Jiang Xuehui pays respects to Your Highness the Grand Princess. May Your Highness enjoy golden peace!”

It was actually Jiang Xuening’s elder sister, the Jiang family’s eldest young lady, Jiang Xuehui!

Everyone was immediately shocked.

But Shen Zhiyi waved her hand. “Rise. From today onward, you too will be one of this Princess’s study companions. You are Ningning’s elder sister. With you accompanying Ningning, she can be happier.”

As soon as these words came out, everyone’s eyes widened: One Jiang family household had produced two study companions? And listening to the Grand Princess’s meaning, she had specially called this person to accompany Jiang Xuening!

For a moment, all kinds of expressions appeared.

Unlike Jiang Xuening, who had only returned to the capital at nearly fourteen or fifteen years old, Jiang Xuehui was a proper young lady educated in the great households of the capital. Her words, actions, and bearing were elegant, dignified, proper, and steady. Her features were clear, pale, and graceful—completely different from the bright, almost captivating feeling Jiang Xuening gave people.

However, no one could be happy about this.

Jiang Xuehui thanked Grand Princess Leyang for her grace, only then rising.

The embroidered handkerchief had originally been in her fingers. With the motion of standing, it also gently fell and unfolded. As it swayed, it revealed a corner of snow-white fabric embroidered with a red ginger flower.

Initially, when Xiao Shu saw the person, she only frowned.

But when this embroidered handkerchief, along with that red ginger flower, fell into her sight, the tranquility that had originally shown no ripples, the transcendent detachment that seemingly placed her above everyone else, all suddenly shattered. Her complexion had already changed dramatically in hidden ways!

Shen Zhiyi pulled Jiang Xuening’s hand and smiled as if seeking credit, “How about it, Ningning? Are you satisfied now?”

Jiang Xuening’s gaze lightly drifted toward Xiao Shu. Their eyes met directly, and seeing her expression, she suddenly realized that Xiao Shu at this age was only so much.

You dare use underhanded methods to harm me, and I dare place the person you truly fear right under your nose!

Making you unable to eat or sleep in peace, restless whether sitting or lying down!

Her older sister was no pushover; she’d better watch out!

A benevolent smile bloomed at the corners of her lips. When Jiang Xuening looked back at Shen Zhiyi, she was already beaming with genuine joy from the heart, sweetly saying, “Thank you for Your Highness’s thoughtfulness. Now I am truly satisfied!”

CONTENT END 81

chapters.title: Ning’er
chapters.content:
Jiang Xuening was satisfied, but there were plenty who were not.

By now, who could not see that Grand Princess Leyang was doing all this for Jiang Xuening?

Though Jiang Xuehui’s entering the palace was quite attention-grabbing, clever people could realize that Jiang Xuening stood behind this matter.

When she spoke the word “satisfied,” countless people in the hall secretly darkened their faces. Even if they had originally been in a good, playful mood, in that instant, it was completely destroyed.

Afterward, Shen Zhiyi even invited Jiang Xuehui to play together.

Among everyone, several people were clearly forcing smiles to keep her company. As for Xiao Shu, from the moment Jiang Xuehui appeared holding that brocade handkerchief, she had not spoken another word.

At Yangzhi Study, as night fell, palace lanterns lit up everywhere.

Returning from Mingfeng Palace and finally reaching her own room, this Eldest Young Lady of the Xiao clan, the niece by blood of the Empress Dowager in the rear palace, in the absence of others’ attention, finally allowed all other expressions to vanish from her face, leaving only a kind of coldly desolate, forest-like calm.

Finally, she raised her hand to lightly press her forehead.

Xiao Shu slowly closed her eyes. Her fingers tensely curved one by one. When she opened her eyes again, she directly swept the teacup on the table to the floor!

The palace servant attending nearby was startled, eyes widening as she looked at her.

Xiao Shu’s chest rose and fell slightly, but she did not look at anyone else.

What floated up in her mind was only that embroidered handkerchief she had once seen fall from Prince Linzi Shen Jie’s sleeve when they happened to meet, and the one she had seen on Jiang Xuehui today…

Others might have already forgotten.

But she remembered perfectly clearly.

It was not Jiang Xuening—that person actually was not Jiang Xuening!

But who could have imagined?

During this time in the palace, Shen Jie had also paid attention to Jiang Xuening at every turn, with many caring intentions in his words. When the Yongyi Marquis household met with disaster, Yan Lin had directly cleared Jiang Xuening of any connection.

All these scattered clues pointed to her.

That was why last time she had…

The fingers placed on the table clenched bit by bit. Xiao Shu only felt a kind of ironic twist of fate: not only had she failed to eliminate the real threat, but she had also left traces and created a truly formidable enemy for herself…

Jiang Xuening was ultimately still perceptive.

At the same time, in Jiang Xuening’s room, the atmosphere was rather subtle.

After Grand Princess Leyang’s extensive efforts here, all kinds of ornaments were already complete, fragrant, and exquisite. Even a painting or calligraphy casually hung on the wall was an authentic work by a famous scholar from the previous dynasty.

Jiang Xuehui was a learned person and could tell at a glance.

The palace servants had naturally already prepared her room, though it was no different from the other study companions. But when invited to come see Jiang Xuening’s room, she easily discovered the enormous gap between them—a vast chasm like heaven and earth. Thus, she gained an extremely direct and clear understanding of just how favored this younger sister was within the palace.

Jiang Xuening had already changed out of that complicated palace dress. She only wore a simple sky-blue pleated skirt with intertwining lotus patterns. Even the hair bun that had been carefully styled earlier was loosened, her raven-black long hair cascading behind her head, with a few strands being lightly twisted by her slender fingers into curls.

She only looked at Jiang Xuehui with a gaze that seemed half-smiling.

Jiang Xuehui sat opposite her, quite calm as still water, saying, “You had me enter the palace—what exactly do you want to do?”

Before Jiang Xuening lay a zither, but it was not Jiao’an, just an ordinary zither.

She reached out with her fingers to lightly pluck it.

Hearing that trembling musical tone, only then did she say leisurely, “Having come all the way to this palace and indeed brought that embroidered handkerchief, if Elder Sister says she does not know at all why I had you enter the palace, would that not be too false?”

Jiang Xuehui then lowered her head to look at that embroidered handkerchief and sighed softly, “How much you hate me, what our relationship is like—you and I understand all too clearly. To say you want to help me, I absolutely do not believe it.”

Her features actually resembled Wan-niang a little bit.

Looking at her, Jiang Xuening’s fingers plucking the zither strings paused. What came to mind instead were the things she had done in her previous life out of jealous hatred toward this person before her: after inadvertently learning that Prince Linzi Shen Jie secretly favored the owner of that embroidered handkerchief, she had done everything possible to prevent Jiang Xuehui from participating in the consort selection. She herself had taken this embroidered handkerchief and once again “happened to encounter” Shen Jie. Thus, she had stolen Jiang Xuehui’s marriage fate, became Princess Linzi, and later became Empress, thoroughly trampling this “elder sister” she hated beneath her feet.

But was she ultimately happy and proud?

It seemed she was not very happy, nor very proud.

Jiang Xuehui had still lived very well.

Sometimes, Jiang Xuening even wondered: When she stole Jiang Xuehui’s marriage fate, did Jiang Xuehui know or not?

From beginning to end, she had never been able to show off to her.

Because shortly after she was selected as Princess Linzi, Jiang Xuehui had married far away and left the capital. She had lost the opportunity to tell this elder sister the truth, to show off to her, to draw her hatred.

“It’s good that you know I will not help you. This palace is full of danger at every step. Some people misunderstood certain things, and methods that should have been directed at you were used on me instead. I nearly lost my life, you know?” Jiang Xuening mockingly curved her lips. Recalling how she saw Xiao Shu’s drastically changed expression today, she truly felt satisfied. “Someone saw you bring that embroidered handkerchief today, and her face completely changed. I imagine Elder Sister’s days in the palace from now on will not be very pleasant. As for me, naturally, I will stand by with folded arms and watch tigers fight from the mountain.”

If it had been someone else, they might not necessarily have guessed who had framed her that time.

After all, there were no real clues.

But Xiao Shu’s misfortune was precisely in encountering not just Jiang Xuening, but a reborn Jiang Xuening. Right now, no one yet knew of Xiao Shu’s designs on the future Empress position, but Jiang Xuening had fought her to the death in her previous life. From the very beginning, she knew that beneath that seemingly aloof face was also hidden vigorous ambition and burning desire.

Threading together the scattered clues, it was hard not to suspect her!

Hearing her words, Jiang Xuehui immediately recalled the rumors from some days ago: Ning’er had been framed in the palace for being connected to the traitorous words of the Tianjiao rebels and had nearly lost her life!

Her heart immediately felt a chill.

Only now did she vaguely understand: that incident was actually related to her!

Jiang Xuening could naturally tell her the cause and effect to let her be on guard against Xiao Shu. But after all, she could not help but mind Jiang Xuehui, and this elder sister truly was not stupid either. There was no need for her to say it, and she was too lazy to say it.

So she changed the topic.

While fiddling with her fingering techniques, thinking that tomorrow, when she went to Xie Wei’s place to learn the zither, she absolutely must not make any mistakes, she said carelessly, “Do you know whose hands that embroidered handkerchief you lost ended up in?”

Jiang Xuehui stared steadily at her, but in the end still lowered her eyes and slowly said, “I more or less know.”

Zheng—

Jiang Xuening’s fingers trembled lightly, and even the zither’s sound trembled along with them.

She abruptly raised her head to look back at Jiang Xuehui, her gaze suddenly sharp, as if wanting to see through her in this moment!

She knew!

Jiang Xuehui actually said she “more or less knew”!

If she already knew at this time, then in her previous life, when she had taken her embroidered handkerchief to “happen to encounter” Shen Jie and stolen her marriage fate, Jiang Xuehui should have known about it too!

Yet she had never erupted…

Jiang Xuening had even thought she had not known from beginning to end!

“What’s wrong?”

Jiang Xuehui had originally thought that this second younger sister, who had always been hostile toward her, doing what she did today, should already have some understanding of the full picture. But why, after she answered truthfully, did Ning’er instead show such an expression?

She did not quite understand.

“…”

But Jiang Xuening remained silent for a long time.

Lowering her eyes to look at the zither before her, she only felt she had lost all her mood to practice. She directly reached out to push the zither aside and said coldly, “I am tired. What needed to be said has been said. Please leave.”

She had always had such a capricious temperament. Being able to sit down and patiently talk with her for a while was already rare. Now issuing an order to leave was not surprising.

Though Jiang Xuehui felt she had left something unsaid, she could not very well ask more.

So she stood up, also telling her to sleep and rest early, and then pushed open the door and walked out.

That night, Jiang Xuening once again could not fall asleep.

*

Early the next morning, in class in Fengchen Hall, the palace servants added one more seat in the second row for Jiang Xuehui to sit. The original eight study companions officially became nine.

The teachers who came to give lessons were naturally all extremely surprised.

Because Jiang Xuehui had joined midway, she had not studied the lessons they had taught before. The teachers could not help but worry somewhat. Among everyone, some could not stand Jiang Xuehui, or some transferred their hatred of Jiang Xuening onto her. Though they had all heard that the Jiang family’s Eldest Young Lady was different from the unlearned and unskilled Second Young Lady and was a true young lady of a great family, what the palace teachers taught was different after all. Jiang Xuehui could not possibly know everything. So they all waited to watch the show, wanting to see her embarrassed in public.

But what happened next was like a slap across their faces—

Jiang Xuehui not only knew but knew everything!

Though the Jiang household’s status was not high, Lady Meng had genuinely raised Jiang Xuehui as a young lady of a great family. Poetry and songs, etiquette and manners—she was skilled in everything!

It was just that she usually did not like to show off and rarely displayed her talents before others, so few people knew.

But now, because she had to answer the teachers’ questions in the palace and did not dare be the slightest bit careless or perfunctory since she did not understand the palace situation, she brought out her full earnestness and easily won the teachers’ amazement.

The current teachers were different from those Jiang Xuening had encountered when she first entered the palace to study. After the incident with Zhao Yanhong, everyone more or less knew what kind of person Xie Wei was. On the surface, they no longer dared show too much favoritism toward Xiao Shu.

And Jiang Xuehui was Jiang Xuening’s elder sister.

Who in this palace did not know that Jiang Xuening was favored by Her Highness the Grand Princess? They had wanted to flatter her with a few phrases, but Jiang Xuening’s studies were too poor. Even if they had thick faces, they could not quite bring themselves to praise her.

Now this was perfect—Jiang Xuehui had arrived!

Just right!

First, she was Jiang Xuening’s elder sister and had also been specially selected to enter the palace by the Grand Princess. Second, her etiquette was proper; she was gentle and virtuous, and would not make things difficult for the teachers—not at all like that troublemaker Jiang Xuening. Third, her learning was outstanding; she was well-read in poetry and books—truly quite rare.

The teachers naturally no longer withheld their praise and lauded Jiang Xuehui highly.

In just two or three short days, Jiang Xuehui, who had only recently entered the palace, had already become a highly favored delicacy appreciated by the teachers in Fengchen Hall.

Originally, Xiao Shu had stood alone in Fengchen Hall.

Now, a dark horse had emerged midway, gradually somewhat overshadowing Xiao Shu’s brilliance. Two moons competed for radiance, both brilliant for a time—truly causing people to marvel with admiration.

Whether Xiao Shu was happy or not was hard for others to see.

But Jiang Xuening knew her nature quite well.

In the past, she could be transcendent and above worldly matters, with eyes that acknowledged no dust, only because no one could pose a threat to her. But once she began to feel threatened, that detached air of being high and mighty would naturally become precarious due to changing circumstances.

So, just thinking about Xiao Shu’s current mood, Jiang Xuening felt extremely pleased—

There was no helping it.

Having fought for so long in the previous life, and in this life, she had acted against her again because of that misunderstanding about the embroidered handkerchief—of course, she could not be too polite to her!

What was even more interesting was that though Jiang Xuehui’s birth was not as good as Xiao Shu’s, she was well-liked by the teachers in Fengchen Palace; ordinarily, she had not a trace of arrogance. Her conduct was entirely approachable, completely different from Xiao Shu’s, who always maintained some airs. She was quite liked by people.

Even Chen Shuyi was willing to talk with her.

Moreover, there had always been rumors in the capital saying the two Jiang sisters had never gotten along well, that Jiang Xuening was domineering and tyrannical in the household, always bullying this elder sister of soft temperament. Therefore, those few whose relationship with Jiang Xuening was not very good instead intentionally or unintentionally approached Jiang Xuehui, wanting to befriend her.

You Yue even felt that a great ally had arrived. On this day, while walking on the path, she sidled up next to Jiang Xuehui and said to her with a smile, “In the past, at various banquets, whenever I saw Elder Young Lady Jiang, I always knew Eldest Young Lady was capable. I did not expect you to be this remarkable. Compared to that unlearned and unskilled Second Young Lady Jiang, you are truly better by who knows how much—one in heaven, one on earth!”

Jiang Xuehui glanced at her but said nothing.

Chen Shuyi, nearby, also said coolly, “Clearly, you are the legitimate eldest daughter of the family. Your learning, talent, and character are all higher than your younger sister’s by who knows how much. Yet in the household, you actually swallow your grievances and let her bully you—it’s truly a strange tale. If I were you, meeting this kind of person who ruins the family’s reputation and is unlearned and unskilled, I’d seize every opportunity to properly deal with her! Otherwise, the entire household’s reputation will be completely ruined by her!”

These past days, everyone had spoken of Jiang Xuening before Jiang Xuehui more than once. Jiang Xuehui always listened without refuting. Everyone assumed the discord between the two sisters was real, so the words they said behind her back gradually became more unbridled.

Everyone felt Jiang Xuehui should share their enmity.

But who could have expected that once Chen Shuyi said this, Jiang Xuehui’s delicate brow actually furrowed? She stopped walking and looked at her, saying somewhat coldly, “Though my second younger sister is indeed unlearned and unskilled, she has not reached the point of ruining the family reputation and completely losing face for the household. Young Lady Shuyi’s words are rather biased and unfair. Though my Jiang household cannot compare to some great families, family discipline is still strict. If Younger Sister has any faults, our father and mother will naturally worry about it. What need is there for Young Lady Shuyi to say more?”

Everyone was stunned.

Jiang Xuehui was actually speaking up for Jiang Xuening!

What about the story that these two sisters had never gotten along?!

Chen Shuyi’s expression changed even more, her pupils contracting as she looked at Jiang Xuehui.

But Jiang Xuehui looked back at her neither humbly nor arrogantly.

You Yue could not help but gasp. Only then did she, along with everyone else, recall: No matter how poor their relationship internally, they were both surnamed Jiang, sisters from the same household! The so-called “younger sister”—even if she scolded her ten thousand times at home, she would not allow others to casually slander her! Moreover, bearing the family name and considering the family’s honor, it was one thing to speak vaguely in the past, but to explicitly say someone ruins the family reputation—how could Jiang Xuehui not react?

Now no one could respond.

The atmosphere was somewhat awkward.

Just then, ahead of them, Jiang Xuening emerged from inside holding a scroll of books, pushing open her room door. From afar, she raised her eyes and saw them outside Yangzhi Study, making it even harder to speak.

It was Zhou Baoying standing among everyone who looked at Jiang Xuening with some curiosity and asked softly and sweetly, “We were just talking about you with Elder Sister Jiang. Second Sister Jiang, are you going to study the zither again?”

The moment Jiang Xuening saw this group of people gathered together, she knew they had nothing good to say.

When Zhou Baoying said everyone was talking about her, some people’s faces changed.

She sneered inwardly and only said, “I am going to see if Teacher Xie is there.”

Last time, Xie Wei had told her to come to the side hall the next day to practice fingering techniques, but when she arrived the next day, Xie Wei had not come.

The palace servants said he was busy with court matters and temporarily could not get away.

For many days in a row, he had not appeared at Fengchen Hall again and had not taught a single class. Logically, Jiang Xuening could have stopped going to the side hall to study the zither, but she did not know when Xie Wei would finish being busy. The palace servants were even less clear, so she could only go to the side hall once each day and wait for a moment.

If Xie Wei did not come, she would leave.

Today was the same.

At this moment, Shen Zhiyi was not present.

Though You Yue was already thoroughly intimidated by Jiang Xuening and absolutely did not dare speak in her presence, there was still Chen Shuyi nearby.

Hearing Jiang Xuening mention studying the zither, she let out a soft laugh and actually glanced at Jiang Xuehui, who had just refused to give her face, saying meaningfully, “I’ve always heard that Teacher Xie has an old friendship with Lord Jiang. Though Second Young Lady Jiang’s zither studies are so worrying, he’s still willing to painstakingly teach her. Now Elder Young Lady Jiang has also come to the palace, skilled in all four arts. It is just a pity that the teacher has been busy lately and has not come to give lessons. Otherwise, seeing an unpolished jade like Elder Young Lady Jiang, he would surely be very happy. After all, facing rotten wood for too long, one really does feel sorry for Teacher Xie…”

Her words faintly carried a provocative meaning.

But Jiang Xuehui did not respond.

Even Jiang Xuening showed not the slightest sign of anger. She still smiled cheerfully and only said to Chen Shuyi, “The words Young Lady Shuyi spoke today, Xuening has noted them down. When I see Her Highness the Grand Princess tomorrow, I will definitely tell her.”

“You!”

Chen Shuyi had not expected her to say such words, using tattling as a threat to her face!

A breath caught in her throat. Her expression immediately became extremely ugly.

Recalling the scene of being scolded by Grand Princess Leyang that day, her body even trembled slightly—from anger!

But Jiang Xuening was too lazy to even look at her again. She let out a cold snort, then, holding the scroll in her hand, walked straight past her. She did not put this dark mass of people in her sight at all; her spine was straight as she strode in large steps toward Fengchen Hall.

At the palace entrance, only a young eunuch stood guard.

Jiang Xuening walked up the steps and asked, “Is Teacher Xie coming today?”

The young eunuch shook his head and pushed open the door for her, replying, “No message has come. But I heard that Teacher Xie was busy at court and did not sleep for two nights. He returned to his residence last night. It is hard to say if he will come today.”

Jiang Xuening then nodded and entered the hall.

Emei hung high on the wall, while Jiao’an lay flat on the zither table.

After entering the hall, she sat down before the zither table.

She set down the scroll in her hand—it was a medical text.

That day on the street when she happened to encounter Zhang Zhe and saw him carrying medicine, she suddenly remembered that Zhang Zhe’s mother was in poor health, suffering from headaches. It just so happened that these past days, Xie Wei had been busy, so besides practicing the zither, she also had leisure time. She asked Shen Zhiyi to borrow a medical text from the Imperial Medical Academy to read. In her early years growing up in the countryside, she had also played around following itinerant physicians, so she had a rough understanding of medical principles. The medical text was not written too obscurely, so by reading it slowly, she could understand it.

But today, though the medical text was set down, Jiang Xuening only stared blankly at it.

Clearly, having Jiang Xuehui enter the palace was something she had already decided on the day she was framed by Xiao Shu. This elder sister of hers had always been outstanding. Never mind that embroidered handkerchief—even without it, she could make Xiao Shu know that there were people beyond people, heavens beyond heavens, and she was not the only one standing out from the crowd in this world.

But truly watching Jiang Xuehui enter the palace, she was not as calm as she had thought she would be.

Was it because she had actually known very early on that the embroidered handkerchief was picked up by Shen Jie?

Or was it because Jiang Xuehui truly was as good as others said?

She had grown up in the countryside; Jiang Xuehui had grown up in the capital.

While she played and waded through water to spear fish, Jiang Xuehui studied the zither, weiqi, calligraphy, and painting.

She was wild and unruly, not knowing when to advance or retreat; Jiang Xuehui was virtuous and dignified, advancing and retreating with proper measure.

…

In her previous life, she had been resentful of this, jealous, even hateful.

And in this life, to calmly accept that she truly was not as outstanding as others—that also was not something easy to do.

One was Elder Young Lady Jiang, and the other was Second Young Lady Jiang.

It seemed they were naturally meant to compete.

Not only did others compare them, but even she could not help but subconsciously make comparisons…

The medical text lay properly before her, but Jiang Xuening only stared at the characters on the cover in a daze, momentarily lost in thought.

She did not even notice when someone entered from outside.

Xie Wei had changed again today into that ethereal pale blue Daoist robe, his hair quite simply bound with a single jade hairpin. He had merely come to make a trip to Fengchen Hall’s side hall, but arriving at the entrance, he heard from the young eunuch that Second Young Lady Jiang was there, which was somewhat unexpected.

He pushed open the door and entered.

Jiang Xuening still sat motionless before the zither table.

Xie Wei held in his hand a memorial marked with red approval. His footsteps made no sound as they crossed the plush carpet. Standing behind her, his gaze passed over her shoulder, and at a glance, he saw the medical text placed before her.

“…”

A moment of silence.

The sweet, fishy taste of fresh blood from years past mixed with the bitterness of medicinal herbs surged up together. Xie Wei could not help but think, “What harmful prescription was this little quack physician, who had nearly treated him to death, this third-rate itinerant physician, pondering now?”

This appearance showed she was lost in thought.

He walked over and raised that memorial, lightly tapping it on her head, only saying, “Wake up!”

Jiang Xuening was tapped and startled, nearly jumping up from her seat.

She looked up to see Xie Wei’s lips holding a trace of a smile as he walked past her from the side. In his expression was a subtle weariness not easily detected, his complexion seemingly paler than when she had last seen him.

Xie Wei tossed that memorial onto the desk, walked to the wall, and raised his hand to take down Emei, placing it on his own zither table. He removed the zither cover, his five fingers lightly plucking to test the sound. Without raising his head, he said, “I heard that Young Lady Ning’er has come these past days. You should have taken my words to heart and learned all the fingering techniques, right?”

Ning’er…

Hearing these two characters, Jiang Xuening froze, so much so that she did not hear anything he said after.

Why had she never before felt that such a strange form of address, these somewhat inappropriate two characters, sounded so pleasing to the ear, so comforting?

Jiang Xuening, Jiang Xuehui.

Jiang was the family surname.

Xue was merely the generational character for ordering.

Only the character “Ning” belonged to her and also distinguished her from others.

In her previous life, when she met Xie Wei on the road returning to the capital, Xie Wei had called her “Second Young Lady Jiang” like others. But after just a few days, after falling into danger, Xie Wei seemed to have changed how he addressed her—not calling her “Second Young Lady Jiang,” but rather “Ning’er.”

This life was no different.

But she had never understood why, nor did she know what was wrong with this person’s brain. In her previous life, she had not wanted any contact with Xie Wei. In this life, at first she had been too fearful, and later she had grown accustomed to it. She had actually never asked and rarely thought about why he addressed her this way.

Ripples suddenly arose in her heart, spreading out into a patch of bitterness.

Everyone called her “Second Young Lady Jiang.” In the past, she had not noticed, but with Jiang Xuehui present, no matter how she listened, it sounded grating.

Jiang Xuening’s eyes grew somewhat hot.

She had always known that Xie Wei’s insight into people’s hearts was unmatched by anyone, and she had experienced this before. But she had not known that this person had so early, so very early, seen through her completely. Not calling her “Second Young Lady Jiang” but rather “Ning’er”—no wonder everyone in court and country praised him. It was just that in her previous life, she had been truly dull and had not understood…

Clearly, in her previous life, this person had spoken harshly to her, had injured her dignity, and had made her uncomfortable. In this life too, she held fear toward him in her heart, and because of studying the zither, she had no good impression of him, deeply feeling his face was detestable.

Yet for these two characters, she actually felt Xie Wei perhaps was not so excessive after all.

Jiang Xuening sat before the zither table, looking at him, forgetting to answer.

Xie Wei spoke and, after a long time hearing no response, his brow furrowed. He raised his eyes to look, only to see that the young woman’s pair of distinct black-and-white eyes was staring straight at him, her eye rims somewhat reddened. Her eyelashes trembled once, and teardrops in her eyes rolled downward.

How was she crying again out of nowhere?
