His movement paused. He raised his hand to pinch the bridge of his nose, deeply feeling a headache. Helplessly, he sighed, “Who’s provoked you now?”

CONTENT END 82

chapters.title: Peach Pastries and Sachet
chapters.content:
Today, she had come to study the zither. She had not come to quarrel, nor had she come to sell her grievances. Moreover, Xie Wei had not provoked or bothered her—it was just that for a moment, the address “Ning’er” had made her think of more, touching her emotions such that she suddenly could not control herself.

Shedding tears before others was ultimately disgraceful.

Jiang Xuening hurriedly raised her sleeve and wildly wiped at her face, smearing her rouge and powder until she looked like a calico cat. She only said, “Sand got in my eye. It is nothing.”

“…”

Xie Wei suddenly fell silent.

But Jiang Xuening rallied her spirits, assuming an unbothered appearance. She casually set that medical text aside and asked him, “Is Teacher going to test the fingering techniques today? Still playing ‘Colorful Clouds Chasing the Moon’?”

Xie Wei looked at her and hummed an acknowledgment, saying, “You know it?”

Jiang Xuening said nothing, only straightening the zither on the zither table.

These past days, she had not been lazy.

Previously, she had not played the zither because Xie Wei had said her mind was not calm and would not let her touch it. But actually, she had always known that when studying under Xie Wei’s hand, one could not muddle through, much less harbor any lucky thoughts, simply because this person was very serious about everything.

At this moment, she thought of nothing else and directly stroked the strings, playing the opening finger exercise.

It was another such winter afternoon.

Because no one had been notified in advance of Xie Wei coming today, the charcoal braziers in this side hall had just been lit and were not yet very warm. The window shutters were half open, revealing a somewhat desolate coldness. Wind blew in, carrying the cold-tinged skylight wrapped in the breeze that fell on the hem of his pale blue Daoist robe. Xie Wei stood before that desk with some distance between them, watching Jiang Xuening play the zither.

It was true that her mind was hard to calm.

But when calmed, she was truly moldable material.

The tear stains at the corners of the young woman’s eyes had not yet dried; her face was messily stained with rouge, but those rippling eyes naturally lowered. Her thick, long eyelashes lightly covered them—a kind of seriousness not previously seen by others.

Her five fingers were slender and long, most suitable for plucking strings.

Gong, shang, jue, zhi, yu—every note was accurate, every sound harmonious. Though the fingering techniques and transitions still showed some roughness and shallowness when observed and listened to, the general appearance was there, and she had shed the clumsiness of her zither studies in Fengchen Hall in the past.

The flowing zither music rippled out from the trembling strings.

For a time, the hall was utterly devoid of human voices.

When that zither music finally faded away gracefully, only then did Xie Wei’s figure move. He slowly nodded, “These days, you indeed have not wasted time. You roughly have some semblance now. Coming to this side hall was not ultimately for sleeping—this can be considered gratifying.”

This was teasing her about falling asleep last time when he played the zither.

Jiang Xuening opened her mouth and said, “That was an exception.”

But just as she finished defending herself, her words barely having fallen, the feeling of hunger in her belly naturally surged up, transforming into a light “gurgling” sound. If there had been many people and much noise, it would have been fine, but at this moment in the hall, there were only her and Xie Wei. It was so quiet you could hear a pin drop, making this originally faint sound as obvious as thunder on a clear day.

Jiang Xuening: “…”

Xie Wei: “…”

Four eyes met. One was embarrassed and red-faced, wishing she could dig a hole and crawl into the ground. The other observed silently, clearly also not having expected this, even carrying a bit of amusement.

Xie Wei raised one finger and lightly pressed it against his thin lips. He still could not suppress his smile, saying, “Indeed, an exception. Last time, you had not slept enough; this time, you have not eaten your fill. Those who know say you are quite favored and trusted by the Grand Princess in the palace. Those who do not know, seeing you sleep-deprived and underfed like this, might think you came to the palace to be imprisoned and punished.”

This person, surnamed Xie, could be quite cutting when he spoke sometimes.

Jiang Xuening secretly gritted her teeth, looking at him without speaking.

Xie Wei then asked, “You have not eaten?”

Jiang Xuening sullenly hummed an acknowledgment. “This morning I was reading and forgot the time. Without paying attention, I fell asleep and forgot to eat.”

The palace was not like home—the Imperial Kitchen did not wait for people.

Unusually, Xie Wei wanted to smile again.

Following his typical temperament, he would be too lazy to bother with such a small matter. There was a common saying that went: eating one’s fill easily led to drowsiness; those who study were best served by maintaining a three-part feeling of hunger to stay alert and concentrate on their work.

Which was to say, being hungry was just right.

However, Ning’er had come to study the zither, and she had just played quite well, clearly having applied herself. Moreover, a young girl of this age was still growing. So he showed mercy and opened the food box sitting at the corner of the desk.

At the top layer was a small dish of peach pastries.

Xie Wei took it out and set it beside the tea table, then, while placing the water kettle on the stove to heat, called to Jiang Xuening, “Come drink tea.”

From the moment he opened that food box, Jiang Xuening’s gaze followed his movements, nearly glued to that small dish of peach pastries, unable to tear away.

Empty belly, itching heart.

Hearing him call her to drink tea, the first thought that popped into her head was, “I cannot go.” Xie Wei was the teacher; she was the student—there should be hierarchy between superior and subordinate. She had heard Xie Wei’s treasonous words from back then and knew secrets about Xie Wei unknown to others. Xie Wei had contemplated killing her to silence her. What if there was poison in the tea?

But that small dish of peach pastries was sitting right there.

Jiang Xuening ultimately could not quite resist that subtle temptation. She stood up and shuffled over.

This definitely was not for the food.

Xie Wei had called her to drink tea—how could she not comply?

Jiang Xuening said, “Thank you, Teacher,” and sat before the tea table. She glanced at Xie Wei, then silently extended a paw, took a thin slice of peach pastry from that small dish, and nibbled a bite.

“…”

The moment the pastry entered her mouth, her movements suddenly paused.

The faint secret delight originally on her face also stiffened slightly.

At first, Xie Wei did not pay attention. He was using a teaspoon to scoop tea from the tea jar. He looked up and glanced at her, saying, “What’s wrong?”

Jiang Xuening came back to her senses and immediately shook her head. “Nothing.”

It was just different from what she had thought.

But stopping to think about it with her brain, she knew—given Xie Wei’s current status and where they currently were, how could she hope to taste that certain flavor? It was best not to reveal any telltale signs. Otherwise, if he noticed and recalled those events from years past, heaven knew if a thought might arise, and he’d want to kill her again.

She quickly lowered her head and chewed slowly.

The soft ingredients of the peach pastry slowly dissolved in her mouth. If she ignored that overly sweet and cloying taste, it could be considered refined. Eating two slices to pad her stomach and satisfy her hunger was sufficient.

Before Xie Wei, Jiang Xuening did not dare to be picky about food.

She ate one slice, then took another.

Xie Wei observed her expression and features, but finally detected something. He asked, “The pastries made by the Imperial Kitchen—are they unappetizing?”

Jiang Xuening hurriedly shook her head.

Xie Wei’s gaze fell from her onto that dish of peach pastries. The pastries were specially prepared for him in this side hall—he had rarely touched them. At this moment, he picked up a slice and took a small bite. When the pastry reached his tongue tip, his brow rose slightly.

For some reason, Jiang Xuening’s heart panicked extremely.

She did not even dare raise her head.

Xie Wei slowly set down that unfinished slice of peach pastry and quietly watched her for a long time. Only when he heard the water beside them boil did he shift his gaze, lift the kettle to pour over the tea implements, and methodically begin brewing tea.

This time, Jiang Xuening understood what it meant to “be unable to swallow food.”

Xie Wei said nothing else; only during the intervals of brewing tea did he ask her about the texts she had studied in recent days, casually testing her learning.

After one pot of tea had been steeped four times, he called her to go practice the zither again.

He himself did nothing more, returning to sit before the desk, staring at the red markings on that memorial for a long time.

After most of an hour, he said to Jiang Xuening, “Though your attitude is present, your foundation is still too thin. People often say diligence can make up for clumsiness—this is not entirely correct, but it cannot be called wrong either. That is all for today. After you return, do not slacken. Starting tomorrow, I will also test you on literary methods. Come to the side hall at this same time.”

Jiang Xuening finally breathed a sigh of relief, stood up, and acquiesced.

Then she took leave of Xie Wei, carrying a trace of caution as she quickly withdrew from the side hall, fleeing far away.

But Xie Wei sat in this side hall a while longer before taking that memorial and leaving the palace.

The Xie residence was separated from the Yongyi Marquis residence by only a single wall.

The difference was that the Yongyi Marquis’ residence faced the front of the street while the Xie residence faced the back. The two residences faced one east and one west, back to back. So when his carriage returned to the residence, it had to pass the Yongyi Marquis’ residence. He could easily see the heavy troops surrounding the outside, each one using cold eyes to scrutinize passersby.

Just after descending from the carriage and entering the residence, after reaching the covered walkway, Jianshu hurriedly walked toward him and said in a low voice, “Besides what Instructor Gongyi said, our people also reported that early this morning they saw Young Master Dingfei come out of the Hengyuan gambling house. But that place is a mixed bag of fish and dragons. At the time, they were not paying close attention and lost track of him.”

Xie Wei stood in the corridor without speaking.

From the side door not far away came the sound of someone laughing and talking. Someone had greeted the gatekeeper and was walking into the residence.

Hearing this, Jianshu turned to look and smiled. “Old Tao is back.”

It was the residence’s cook, skilled at making good dishes.

Old Tao was broad-shouldered and thick-waisted, plump and white, but his face was full of joy. One hand carried a vegetable basket, the other still held a fish. Seeing Xie Wei standing under the corridor, he hurriedly came over to pay respects, saying, “My Lord has returned! Today I bought a fresh large carp—it’s quite lively! The pastries I made some days ago were secretly eaten completely by Young Master Dao Qin. I also bought several jin of glutinous rice and one jin of peach kernels. I can try making some peach pastries!”

Xie Wei looked at his basket packed full to the brim. His gaze lowered, and he nodded.

*

Jiang Xuening fled from Fengchen Hall’s side hall in one breath. Only after walking far away, reaching the entrance of Yangzhi Study, did she lean against the door and look back to see that no one had followed. Only then did she let out a long sigh of relief.

Eating a peach pastry had nearly scared her sick!

She truly had grown bold—not only daring to eat things Xie Wei gave her, but also daring to fantasize that Xie Wei had made it himself. She simply did not want to live anymore!

Fortunately, the other party had not noticed, and she had escaped safely.

She lightly patted her own chest.

When Yao Xi and You Yue walked out from inside Yangzhi Study, they happened to see her like this. What came to their minds was her posture when she had turned to find Zhang Zhe that day. For a moment, hatred surged up, so she smiled coolly, “Did not Second Young Lady Jiang go to study the zither? Coming back looking like a thief—were you scolded by Teacher Xie again?”

Jiang Xuening turned her head and saw her.

These days, Yao Xi’s hostility toward her had gradually shown signs. But there were many who hated her—who did Yao Xi think she was?

She had not yet reached the point of needing too much attention.

Hearing the sarcasm, Jiang Xuening was not angry. After all, today she had played the zither well and barely earned Xie Wei’s praise, had she not?

Not floating to the heavens would be letting herself off lightly.

She raised her eyebrows and smiled, assuming a leisurely appearance, saying, “Then I will have to disappoint Young Lady Yao. Today, I was finally able to touch the zither and just received a word of affirmation from Teacher Xie. In the future, I will certainly redouble my efforts and not disappoint Teacher’s painstaking instruction of me.”

People in the world might not necessarily want to see their friends doing well, but definitely enjoyed seeing their enemies doing poorly.

If someone you hated was doing poorly, even if you could not see it with your own eyes, just hearing the news from afar would secretly please your heart.

Jiang Xuening was undoubtedly Yao Xi’s enemy.

But not only was she doing well, but she was telling others to their face that she was doing well. That relaxed, smiling look in her eyes and brows was directly like needles, one after another, piercing until one’s heart bled!

Yao Xi choked and stopped speaking.

You Yue had long been frightened and now kept her mouth shut like a sealed gourd, not saying a word.

Jiang Xuening then clapped her hands and walked away from them with light steps.

You Yue observed Yao Xi’s expression and said softly, “Perhaps she’s putting on a brave face. Who does not know she’s famously unlearned and unskilled? Studying the zither also depends on natural talent. Being so clumsy, she does not even know the fingering techniques—how could Teacher Xie possibly praise her? It is just deliberately said to make you feel blocked, that is all.”

Yao Xi took a deep breath and turned with a flick of her sleeve.

But just as she reached the entrance of Yangzhi Study, her gaze inadvertently swept across something, and her steps paused. Where Jiang Xuening had just stood, a sachet had actually fallen.

You Yue followed her gaze and quite naturally bent down to pick up this sachet. Turning it over to look, on a moon-white base, deep blue silk thread embroidered an exquisite peony with fine, dense stitches—very beautiful.

“Is this not Jiang Xuening’s?”

Feeling somewhat disgusted in her heart, she curled her lip and raised her hand, wanting to toss it into the corner of a nearby flower pot.

Unexpectedly, when Yao Xi saw this, she directly snatched it from her hand and held it, looking at it.

You Yue was somewhat puzzled. “Are you going to return it to her?”

Yao Xi’s thoughts stirred. Though her eyes held a shadow, she only said, “It’s just a small sachet. What’s the hurry?”

You Yue stopped talking.

Yao Xi stared at this sachet for a long time, then casually tucked it into her sleeve, saying, “It will not be too late to return it to her when we come back. Seeing her wear it every day, who knows, it might be an important item. It would be good if she gets anxious when she loses it and cannot find it.”

You Yue then smiled. “That is good.”

Jiang Xuening had just left, and they had picked up the sachet. Too lazy to turn back and call her, they headed straight toward the Imperial Garden.

Some days ago, the tiger-hoof plum blossoms planted in the palace had already bloomed.

The Empress Dowager’s cold had also improved somewhat. To seek good fortune, the Empress invited the consorts from each palace to come out to the Imperial Garden to admire the plum blossoms. Because of Xiao Shu’s face, the study companions from Yangzhi Study could also benefit and went to have a look, joining the excitement.

Naturally, Yao Xi and You Yue did not want to miss Su Shangyi at an event.

In the plum garden, the tiger-hoof plum blossoms bloomed early, and the wintersweet had also grown small buds.

Walking through the garden, there was quite a lot of interest.

You Yue came from the Qingyuan Earl household, of quite humble origins. She loved making friends, not to mention encountering this once-in-a-lifetime occasion. She single-mindedly went to curry favor and flatter before the various palace consorts. Yao Xi, however, did not look favorably upon this.

She came from a great family and disdained such behavior.

So halfway through the banquet, she simply said nothing, abandoned everyone, and went to the outer garden to admire the plum blossoms.

The plum garden was quite large.

Yao Xi said she was admiring plum blossoms, but looking and looking in this already somewhat cold weather, she could not help but recall seeing Zhang Zhe that day in Cining Palace. Then she thought of that letter declining the marriage engagement she had seen in her father’s study. With desolation in her heart and rising hatred besides, unknowingly, she walked quite far.

At the furthest point, it was actually somewhat desolate.

A pavilion rarely visited by people on ordinary days stood in the plum forest, surrounded by densely planted clusters of plum trees, making it appear quite thick.

It just looked gloomy, making people somewhat afraid.

Yao Xi’s courage was not very great. Upon arriving here, she came back to her senses and wanted to turn back. But unexpectedly, having walked back only a few steps, a series of footsteps accompanied by low conversation came from the other end of the plum garden.

“If I, the Empress Dowager, had not noticed something wrong that day at Yangzhi Study and you had allowed that little palace maid to be interrogated in court with your thoughtless planning, if she had not been tight-lipped and had revealed the truth through a careless slip, how would you have dealt with it yourself?!”

“It was this niece who was muddled and lost her usual composure.”

“All matters are easier to act upon than to think through, especially so in the palace. No one is a fool! Without even ascertaining your opponent’s reality, you rashly acted—you’ve truly disappointed this Empress Dowager.”

“…”

“Now Jiang Xuening is unharmed, and you’ve gained this formidable enemy for yourself for nothing. Outside, another Jiang Xuehui has entered, who, though not outstanding in appearance, can compete with you in studies and is extremely likely to be the true owner of Jie’er’s embroidered handkerchief. You are not just muddled!”

“Aunt’s reprimand is justified.”

Empress Dowager Xiao walked in front; Xiao Shu followed behind her.

One could not quite suppress the anger all over her face, somewhat sternly rebuking. The other had lost her usual aloof calm from high above, lowering her head to quietly listen.

Neither had palace servants following behind them.

Very obviously, such words were not suitable for palace servants to overhear.

The footsteps gradually drew near.

Yao Xi ordinarily had a good relationship with Xiao Shu and was close to her. Even if she could not recognize Empress Dowager Xiao’s voice, she could distinguish Xiao Shu’s voice. Suddenly hearing what the two discussed, she only felt cold sweat pour from her head, her heart pounding madly in her chest.

She absolutely did not dare show herself at this moment.

Seeing a cluster of plum tree branches nearby overlapping and interlocking that could hide a person, she held her breath and quickly hid behind them, not daring to breathe heavily.

Empress Dowager Xiao continued walking forward, passing by that plum tree cluster, saying, “Though you are a rarely seen clever person of the Xiao clan, you are still young in years after all. You’ve experienced too few matters, your thinking is not thorough enough, and you have not thought through sufficient contingency methods. That day, you nearly fell into a passive position in the hall. Moreover, you acted privately without even telling this Empress Dowager! Does the Empress Dowager appear unable to see through your intentions?”

Xiao Shu said, “Ah Shu has failed Aunt’s instruction.”

But Empress Dowager Xiao sighed and said, “The Emperor personally experienced Prince Pingnan’s rebellion back then. From then on, he became suspicious. Even toward this Empress Dowager, his birth mother, he is not affectionate. Even selecting an Empress, he selected one from a small household background. He would not select even a single person of the Xiao clan for a consort position—he’s being wary. But Jie’er has a gentle temperament and is more intimate with me. I know you also have great ambitions. Looking across the capital at daughters of noble families, no one is more suited than you for the position of Empress.”

Hiding behind the tree, Yao Xi temporarily did not dare move. Though her heart warned her that if she wanted to live, she should not listen, she could not seal her two ears. Those words continuously entered, making her increasingly frightened and terrified the more she heard.

That incident at Yangzhi Study—it was actually Xiao Shu who framed Jiang Xuening!

It was for Prince Linzi Shen Jie to become the future Empress!

Then she heard Xiao Shu say, “Aunt’s meaning is…”

Empress Dowager Xiao said coldly, “As long as the Emperor is still alive, if he wants to establish Jie’er as Imperial Prince, he will not tolerate a woman of the Xiao clan becoming Princess Linzi. You must be patient.”

Xiao Shu said, “Must I just watch someone else take that position?”

At this time, the two people’s footsteps had become somewhat distant, their voices also somewhat far.

Yao Xi swallowed and did not dare stay any longer. She quietly circled around that plum tree cluster and was about to leave.

But who would have thought that in panic and disorder, errors easily occur?

As she hurriedly bent down, she accidentally bumped a plum branch. Immediately, the plum blossoms shook and trembled, and the sound of branches colliding transmitted outward.

“Who’s there?”

Empress Dowager Xiao turned her head. From that distant place, she could only see that plum branch move. Instinctively, she let out a stern shout!

Yao Xi immediately knew she had revealed her whereabouts. In her panic, she chose no path and took to her heels, running.

Only at the extreme of fear did evil thoughts also surge up.

A vicious color overflowed from her eyes. Her mind stirred, and she directly reached into her sleeve, felt that sachet she had picked up earlier, and directly threw it on the ground. Then she quickly exited this plum garden, circled around to another place, and only then returned to the plum blossom viewing banquet.

*

A group of palace consorts was admiring plum blossoms in the palace, and with an Empress Dowager Xiao present, Jiang Xuening did not want to join that excitement.

In Liushui Pavilion, Fang Miao had been pulled by Zhou Baoying to sit there playing xiangqi.

So she walked over and sat beside them, peeling peanuts brought up by palace servants while watching the two compete on the board.

Only when the sky darkened did those who went to admire plum blossoms return.

Seeing people playing xiangqi in Liushui Pavilion, everyone gathered over, wanting to see how much Zhou Baoying would win against Fang Miao in this round.

Xiao Shu was also among them.

Seeing that Jiang Xuening had already peeled a pile of peanut shells beside her hand, Xiao Shu smiled faintly. As her eyes flashed slightly, she raised her hand and held a sachet before her, saying, “I just picked up an item outside. It looks somewhat familiar—is it Second Young Lady Jiang’s?”

Jiang Xuening froze and raised her eyes.

The sachet hanging from Xiao Shu’s fingers was precisely the one You Fangying had specially embroidered for her using silk sent by the silk farmers when she completed her first business transaction. The deep blue peony was quite unique and very beautiful.

Lowering her eyes to look at her own waist, she did not know when it had become empty.

She raised her eyebrow slightly and took the sachet from Xiao Shu’s hand, but did not express profuse gratitude. Still somewhat cool, she said flatly, “It’s mine. I do not know when it fell. Thank you for the trouble.”

The edge of the sachet had somehow been snagged by something, making it somewhat frayed.

Seeing this, Jiang Xuening felt somewhat distressed. She gently stroked it once before frowning and hanging it back at her waist.

Xiao Shu quietly observed her expression, watching her actions. She easily detected that coolness of not wanting to speak more with her, but apart from this, she was remarkably composed.

You Yue, behind them, watched with some confusion.

But Yao Xi, seeing this scene, felt her heart pound like a drum, nearly unable to stand as her feet went soft.

CONTENT END 83

chapters.title: Hot Temper
chapters.content:
Having something lost returned was naturally a cause for happiness.

However, the person returning it was Xiao Shu, so it carried a somewhat strange feeling. Jiang Xuening was not very accustomed to it. Fortunately, Xiao Shu also had no intention of using this as an excuse to speak with her. After returning the sachet, she left.

So Jiang Xuening was happy to be at ease and continued watching Zhou Baoying and Fang Miao play chess.

This round, they were playing weiqi.

Fang Miao’s move had entered deep contemplation and could not be decided for quite a while.

Zhou Baoying looked utterly bored. She also grabbed some peanuts from the side to shell, then turned her head to glance at Yao Xi and You Yue, asking curiously, “Did you two elder sisters also go admire the plum blossoms?”

Only after Xiao Shu left did Yao Xi breathe a sigh of relief. But hearing Zhou Baoying’s question, her heart could not help but tighten again. She forced herself to smile as if nothing had happened. “We went too, but did not look for very long. We spent most of the time talking with the ladies from each palace.”

Zhou Baoying then said, “Oh.”

She seemed to want to say something, but just at that moment, Fang Miao placed a stone with a “clack.” Her gaze immediately shifted away, and she clapped her hands, laughing, “I knew Sister Fang Miao would play there! Watch me eat half your territory!”

Fang Miao looked at where her finger had fallen and immediately cried out anxiously, “You! How can you play there? No, no, I have not thought it through yet. I am not playing there!”

“Once a stone is placed, it cannot be taken back, Elder Sister!”

Having finally won another game, Zhou Baoying absolutely would not allow her to easily take back her move. The two began tussling over the weiqi board.

Having just experienced such danger, Yao Xi felt mentally and physically exhausted. She pretended nothing was wrong and watched in Liushui Pavilion for a while before claiming she was tired and walking outside.

Seeing this, You Yue’s gaze flashed, and she followed along.

When Jiang Xuehui came out of her room, she happened to see the two of them returning one after another and lightly greeted them. But perhaps because she had previously refuted them to their faces, both their expressions looked rather unfriendly, displaying a somewhat strangely cold indifference.

At this time, she did not pay it much mind.

By the time she returned to her room after the evening meal, noticing the scratch on Jiang Xuening’s sachet, she asked, “What happened to this sachet?”

Jiang Xuening lowered her head to glance at it, saying, “Probably carelessly dropped it. When Xiao Shu picked it up and returned it to me, it was already like this. It must have gotten scraped somewhere.”

Sachets and handkerchiefs were all young ladies’ private items.

She was accustomed to mixing about outside and did not pay much attention to such small details. But Jiang Xuehui had been raised in the inner quarters of a great household. Hearing this, her brow lightly furrowed as she said, “When did you lose it?”

Originally, Jiang Xuening’s relationship with her was not close. Unless necessary, the two of them did not speak.

But now Jiang Xuehui was actively asking.

After thinking carefully, Jiang Xuening understood what she was worried about. After all, if such a private item passed through someone’s hands in the palace and some matter between men and women was drawn out, falling into the eyes of someone with ulterior motives would be enough to create a major incident.

She did not respond, only untied the sachet again and directly opened it to look.

Inside still contained dried flowers and fragrance chips—nothing extra had been added.

However, within the originally delicate scent of sweet flag, there was now faintly an additional penetrating cool fragrance…

Extremely subtle, but still discernible.

Jiang Xuening’s heart immediately became slightly alert. What floated up in her mind was the plum blossom viewing banquet in the palace today that she had not attended. From leaving this morning until eating dinner in the evening, the places she had stayed or passed through were only from Yangzhi Study to Fengchen Hall, plus those palace paths in between. She absolutely had not encountered any plum blossoms in the middle, much less tiger-hoof plum blossoms, which bloomed earliest…

Unless Xiao Shu used plum fragrance.

But to her knowledge, she did not.

Jiang Xuehui had only wanted to ask when it was lost, fearing someone in the palace would use this sachet to make an issue. She had not expected that after Jiang Xuening opened the sachet and sniffed it slightly, she would furrow her brow tightly.

She inevitably worried, “Something wrong?”

Jiang Xuening’s eyes were covered with a layer of shadow. She only looked toward the outside of the entrance of Yangzhi Study and the palace path beyond. Without answering, she tied up the sachet. Seeing no one else around, she went straight down the steps, looking carefully all along the way.

Reaching the entrance of Yangzhi Study, she suddenly recalled something, and her steps stopped.

The palace gates in the palace were all made of wood.

At this moment, the two doors had not yet been closed, with round copper rings hanging on both sides. But on the left door, at about the same height as a person’s waist, a wooden splinter protruded with several strands of extremely fine moon-white silk hanging from it.

Looking carefully, Jiang Xuening discovered it.

She lightly raised her finger to remove those few silk strands, then spread open the sachet in her palm. The scrape mark on the sachet was still fresh, and the moon-white base color was exactly the same as these fine silk threads.

Thinking back, when she had returned from Fengchen Hall to Yangzhi Study earlier, she had indeed been leaning against this door looking back.

Thinking this way, it must have been lost then.

At the time, she had encountered You Yue and Yao Xi but had not seen anyone else. Yet this sachet was ultimately picked up by Xiao Shu, and it also carried traces of plum fragrance on it…

Seeing her posture, Jiang Xuehui knew something had happened.

But Jiang Xuening seemed to know what she wanted to ask and only said, “You do not need to worry about it.”

Having said this, she took the sachet back to her room.

After experiencing the previous incident of being framed when Yangzhi Study was searched, Jiang Xuening had become much more careful. After all, she was no longer the Empress from her previous life—even others’ minor schemes could trap her in danger.

Whether there were suspicious circumstances in this matter, that remained to be discussed.

What was important was: if there were suspicious circumstances, what would be implicated?

The lights were lit in the room. The sachet and that silk thread were both placed under the lamp. Jiang Xuening sat before the desk, looking for a long time.

The night had deepened.

Soon, she heard the laughing and noisy sounds from Liushui Pavilion quiet down, immediately followed by the sounds of Fang Miao and Zhou Baoying bidding farewell. They had apparently finally finished their weiqi game and agreed to continue the battle tomorrow.

At this time, Jiang Xuening thought: “Rather than sitting here thinking and suspecting, might as well directly find Xiao Shu tomorrow and ask first to seize the initiative.” After all, things not done were simply not done. If others wanted to frame and slander, there would inevitably be imperfect or incomplete aspects that would certainly reveal flaws and be discovered.

Moreover, Xiao Shu truly was not muddled.

Having made up her mind, she planned to wash and rest.

Unexpectedly, just as she stood up, knocking sounds came from outside.

“Knock knock.”

Someone lightly knocked on her door, followed by Zhou Baoying’s soft, sweet voice, “Sister Ning, are you asleep? The pastries in my room are all gone. Do you have any left?”

Jiang Xuening immediately froze.

Whether in her previous life or this one, her interactions with Zhou Baoying had not been deep. She only vaguely remembered that this young lady later married Prince Yanping and did not think about various matters, spending her days researching food and drink, uncommonly carefree and at ease.

Looking for food in the middle of the night?

She went forward to open the door, saying, “There’s still some. Shall I get you some?”

Zhou Baoying had just finished playing weiqi with Fang Miao and returned. Standing outside the door somewhat bashfully, as if asking someone for food like this was very embarrassing, when she saw Jiang Xuening open the door for her, she beamed with joy and hopped one step into the room, saying, “Thank you, Sister Ning.”

The palace pastries were all given according to regulation.

Zhou Baoying loved to eat, and her mouth never stopped from dawn to dusk. Her own room’s pastries being completely eaten was a common occurrence.

But Jiang Xuening was the complete opposite.

After entering the palace, she ate very little, not being very satisfied with the current palace cooks.

She placed her several dishes of pastries all into a food box, saying, “I do not like eating them either. Why do I not give them all to you?”

Zhou Baoying bit her lip. “Ah, that is not quite right…”

Though she said this, her hand involuntarily reached toward the food box Jiang Xuening passed to her, clutching it tightly. Her two eyes curved like crescent moons—she was simply bubbling over with happiness.

Those who gave food were all good people.

So, facing Jiang Xuening, compliments poured out in basketfuls, “I knew Sister Ning was beautiful with a kind heart and cares for me so much! I also saw that the sachet Sister Xiao picked up and returned to you today. But at that time, I was standing in the corridor, and Sister Yao Xi and Sister You Yue were at the doorway—they had already picked it up first. I thought they would return it to you, so I did not go over. When they came back without mentioning returning the sachet to you, I was puzzled for a bit. Fortunately, Sister Xiao actually brought it out. Really, if I had picked it up, at least now I would not be eating Sister’s pastries for free…”

Her two brows locked together, assuming a somewhat worried little appearance.

When she spoke, it was soft and sweet, but her speaking speed was not very slow, like pouring out beans, with its own natural rhythm.

This string of words passed by so quickly that it almost did not give one time to react.

But when Jiang Xuening realized what she had said, she suddenly raised her head to look at her, already slightly stunned, her heart greatly shaken!

But Zhou Baoying seemed completely oblivious to this. Clutching the food box with both hands, looking somewhat distressed and troubled, as if making a firm resolution, she bit her teeth and said to Jiang Xuening, “How about this! Having taken Sister’s pastries this time, when the palace servants bring pastries next time, I will share half of my portion with Sister—absolutely no backing out!”

Jiang Xuening: “…”

Zhou Baoying took it as her agreement. “Then it is settled! Thank you, Sister. I’m…going back now?”

Only then did Jiang Xuening smile faintly, saying, “Go back. Rest early.”

Zhou Baoying hopped once more and jumped out the door, waving to Jiang Xuening. “Sister, you rest early too!”

Having said this, she carried the food box to her own room in high spirits. Halfway there, she could not resist lifting the lid to take out an almond cookie and stuff it in her mouth—clearly she had been craving it terribly.

Jiang Xuening watched her back disappear around the corner of the long corridor before lowering her eyes and slowly closing the door.

Her thoughts suddenly churned.

So it really was Yao Xi and You Yue…

However, she had suspected this earlier, so hearing it from Zhou Baoying’s mouth was not very surprising. What surprised her was Zhou Baoying secretly slipping over to speak with her at all.

It seemed unintentional, but if she had not previously detected the suspicious circumstances of this matter, these words would have been enough to awaken her and make her vigilant.

This little girl…

Jiang Xuening could not help but smile. Though she liked eating and drinking, she was ultimately the xiangqi fanatic who could kill Fang Miao on the board, leaving not even armor behind. She was not as foolish as she appeared on the surface. This cleverness—ordinary people did not have it.

*

The next day, getting up early to go to class at Fengchen Hall, Jiang Xuening had a face as if nothing had happened.

Xiao Shu also had her usual appearance.

But Yao Xi seemed not to have slept well, somewhat listless and lacking energy.

Chen Shuyi even teased her, “Looking at this little appearance so haggard—what were you thinking about at night? Oh my, I forgot—our Young Lady Yao Xi is different. She’s someone whose marriage is already arranged, so naturally she has more to think about.”

If she had said this before, Yao Xi would definitely have blushed all over her face.

What would follow would be everyone frolicking about, the atmosphere relaxed and pleasant.

But unexpectedly, hearing these words, Yao Xi’s expression immediately changed, even becoming quite ugly. She raised her head to look directly at Chen Shuyi, actually carrying a trace of anger.

Chen Shuyi immediately realized.

The smile on her face stiffened. She stopped laughing and, after hesitating a moment, said, “What, did you not decide not to break off the engagement with that Zhang Zhe?”

Everyone in the hall was clear about her and Zhang Zhe’s engagement. At first, they knew she wanted to break the engagement, but later, for some reason, it was not broken off. After accidentally seeing Zhang Zhe at Cining Palace, she even seemed quite satisfied with him.

Talented scholar and beautiful lady—though not matching in family status, if the woman had no complaints, they could still become a good match.

By common sense, this marriage was naturally settled.

Even if there was a letter from Zhang Zhe initiating the broken engagement, no one thought it was a problem.

Including Xiao Shu, everyone’s gaze turned over, looking toward Yao Xi.

Yao Xi’s fingers placed on the table clenched tightly.

She only felt that these curious gazes all concealed malicious probing and scrutiny, even carrying a kind of faint expectation of watching a good show. She had already seen Zhang Zhe’s resolute letter breaking the engagement and had even been coldly rebuked by her father because of jokes made in Fengchen Hall!

Thinking about it made her hate.

What she hated even more was that Zhang Zhe actually dared to break off the engagement with her!

Someone like her, a young lady of a great family, where would she put her face in the future?

At this moment, everyone’s concerned gazes not only did not ease the awkwardness in her heart, but instead intensified the resentment in her heart.

But this kind of matter, she absolutely would not willingly speak of.

What young lady would be willing to frankly say she had been jilted?

Yao Xi clenched her teeth and smiled at Chen Shuyi, without being polite, saying, “That Zhang Zhe does not know good from bad. Coming from a small household, even with a talented appearance, he seems shabby. Moreover, we had someone do fortune-telling—he has the unlucky destiny of a Lone Star. So thinking it over, we decided to forget it.”

Everyone gasped in surprise.

But Jiang Xuening had personally heard Zhang Zhe say he would initiate breaking off the engagement. Now hearing what Yao Xi said, it sounded as if she had been the one to initiate breaking Zhang Zhe’s engagement. And opening her mouth, she actually said Zhang Zhe had “the unlucky destiny of a Lone Star”!

How was this different from what she had discussed with You Yue that day?

Her expression cooled slightly.

But Yao Xi looked at her deliberately in a provocative manner, saying meaningfully, “However, people I do not fancy, those from small households probably all scramble to get. So even with the broken engagement, that Zhang Zhe might be able to find someone quite good. Though not necessarily comparable to me, who knows—the pot might find its lid, catching someone’s eye!”

Others heard in confusion.

Only Jiang Xuening clearly understood that these words were cursing her. Her chest swelled with anger for a moment. She wanted to flare up, but the other party had not named names. If she jumped out, it would seem as if she truly had some unspeakable relationship with Zhang Zhe, playing right into their hands.

Just at this time, the teacher for the class arrived, so she forcibly suppressed this fire in her chest.

Only that the more she suppressed it, the more this fire blazed.

Today’s lessons were calligraphy and etiquette. Throughout, her expression never improved.

The teachers on the platform would glance at her and think they had taught something wrong. After learning that Jiang Xuening had driven away two previous teachers, they all trembled with fear, afraid they would be the next to suffer. So they did not come to trouble her.

When class ended, and Jiang Xuening was about to leave the hall, Yao Xi also happened to walk up.

She did not want to yield, and Yao Xi did not want to yield either.

The two squeezed past each other.

Jiang Xuening’s temper flared. Her brow furrowed, and she directly pushed her once, saying without the slightest courtesy, “I was walking in front—what are you rushing for? In a hurry to be reborn?”

Today, Yao Xi had also been suddenly asked about the marriage matter by Chen Shuyi; recalling that incident of Zhang Zhe breaking the engagement filled her with hatred. Her suspicions rising, she always felt this matter was related to Jiang Xuening. So unconsciously, she wanted to oppose her and would not yield, forgetting what kind of temperament Jiang Xuening herself had—one that absolutely would not tolerate being wronged, igniting at the slightest spark.

With that push, she nearly stumbled and fell!

The teachers in the hall had not yet left, and palace servants stood to the side. Seeing this scene, they were simply stunned, completely unable to believe someone’s temper was this explosive, flaring up directly before everyone’s eyes!

Even Yao Xi herself had not expected it.

She was supported by someone and only then stood steady. After reacting, she was greatly enraged. “Jiang Xuening, what do you mean?!”

Jiang Xuening sneered coldly, “Meaning, I want to mess with you.”

Shen Zhiyi had not walked that quickly and was still behind them. She did not know what previous grievances and entanglements the two had. Looking at this scene, even she was stunned for a moment.

Others all secretly observed her expression.

Yao Xi wanted to compete with Jiang Xuening, but looking back at Shen Zhiyi, who was paying attention to the situation’s development, she was extremely wary. She withdrew the finger pointing at Jiang Xuening and said hatefully, “Those who do not act like thieves do not have guilty consciences. Of course, those who act like petty people in the shadows become ashamed and enraged.”

Jiang Xuening let out a light snort, “No need to point at mulberry trees and curse locust trees. I advise you to restrain yourself better. If you are jilted, obediently tuck your tail and behave. After all, it was one fated connection ending on good terms. Others will not spread it everywhere. But if you desperately try to save face and will not let others have peace, that person also has a thousand, ten thousand ways to make you uncomfortable. If you dare go out and talk nonsense for even one sentence, I dare let the entire capital know what you did to be jilted!”

Jilted!

So Yao Xi was actually the one who was jilted?

Had she not previously said with complete confidence that Zhang Zhe breaking the engagement was to avoid implicating her, and as long as she declined, this marriage would definitely work out?

Everyone who heard Jiang Xuening’s words was stunned.

Looking at Yao Xi again, their gazes became somewhat subtle—some sympathetic, some hard to express.

Yao Xi had not expected Jiang Xuening to be so impolite, saying this matter before everyone. Being looked at by everyone’s gazes, her face alternated between green and red. She was so angry that her body visibly trembled.

Tears pattered down.

Young ladies naturally cared about face. Being slapped in the face publicly, she was naturally extremely aggrieved.

But Jiang Xuening had finally vented her anger. Too lazy to even look at her again, she flicked her sleeve and directly left, heading toward the side hall.

Anyway, she was tyrannical by nature—others could say what they wanted.

It was just that she, this person, kept her word and followed through!

If Yao Xi dared to do those wretched, despicable things from her previous life to slander and suppress Zhang Zhe, even if she had to give up leaving the capital in this life to stir things up in this slaughter field, she would fight her to the bitter end and make her pay the price!

*

Inside the side hall, there was a warmth throughout. The underfloor heating had been lit in advance, and even the water for brewing tea had been placed on the stove beforehand.

Xie Wei had arrived early.

Beside a small food box, a dish of peach pastries sat at the corner of the tea table. But he was looking at the pale greenish tea liquor in the cup before him, somewhat lost in thought.

When Jiang Xuening pushed open the door and entered, he turned his head and saw her.

Only compared to usual, this face full of cold, icy appearance looked as if she bore a grudge against someone.

Xie Wei lightly raised his eyebrows.

He wanted to ask again: “Who has provoked you now?”

But thinking he had asked this question yesterday, he did not speak.

But Jiang Xuening felt her anger was blazing. She walked over and first bowed in respect to Xie Wei. Upon rising, seeing him observing her expression, she knew her emotions were showing on her face. Fearing Xie Wei would misunderstand, she said, “I just quarreled with a despicable person. Teacher, please do not blame me.”

Xie Wei: “…”

Using those words, she was truly angry to the point of losing her head. Ning’er never usually said such things. In other words, to be worthy of the words “despicable person,” the matter must be very serious.

Pondering her belly full of fire, it also did not seem like she could calm her mind to play the zither. So he pointed to the seat opposite him, saying, “Sit.”

Jiang Xuening sullenly walked over and sat down.

Xie Wei looked at her face full of bitter resentment. After sitting down, she did not move. So he lowered his eyes, drank a sip of tea, and said flatly, “Waiting for me to pour you tea?”

The tea had been prepared before Jiang Xuening arrived and had been poured into the teapot for serving.

Only then did Jiang Xuening react.

In the past, when Xie Wei poured her tea, it was the tea brewer’s etiquette. She had only drunk it twice and had not paid attention. Being reminded by him like this, even the back of her head cooled down. She quickly picked up the teapot. Seeing Xie Wei had set down his teacup, she very obediently first refilled his, then turned to pour herself a cup.

She did not dare speak, holding the teacup with both hands and drinking a small sip.

Today’s tea was Houkui.

Clearly, also imperial tribute from the palace. It entered the mouth smoothly with a sweet aftertaste lingering between teeth and cheeks. After drinking, one could still smell a fragrance carrying some sweetness…

Mm, sweetness?

Was Houkui tea this flavor?

Jiang Xuening suddenly froze, her eyeballs rolling. At a glance, she saw the dish of peach pastries beside her.

Same as yesterday.

That flavor—she found it somewhat disagreeable and did not want to try it a second time.

After one glance, she withdrew her gaze and continued drinking tea.

Xie Wei said, “In palace affairs, restraint is paramount. Yet you are making enemies everywhere. For what reason did you quarrel with someone?”

Jiang Xuening muttered, “I also know my temperament is not suitable for staying in the palace, but you all did not give me a choice either.”

As she spoke, that sweet fragrance drifted over again.

She could not resist and turned to glance at that dish of peach pastries again: “Clearly so unpalatable, yet the fragrance was so enticing—what’s going on?” The palace cooks were just full of flowery tricks and bad intentions! One must have backbone—absolutely must not reach out! Otherwise, in a bit, if she could not finish eating and had to force herself to stuff it down before Xie Wei, it would be absolutely tragic!

Xie Wei raised his eyebrow. “Are you blaming me?”

Jiang Xuening’s mind wandered. She did not even remember what she had just said. Instinctively saying “Ah,” she immediately said, “I would not dare, I would not dare.”

But Xie Wei’s gaze shifted toward that dish of peach pastries.

He had already noticed Jiang Xuening had glanced at it more than once. He said, “If you want to eat it, just take it. No one’s restraining you.”

“No, no, no, I am not hungry.”

Jiang Xuening immediately shook her head, expressing refusal.

Xie Wei: “…”

CONTENT END 84

chapters.title: Finally Got to Eat
chapters.content:
What was that expression?

Jiang Xuening looked at him somewhat suspiciously, inexplicably feeling a bit cowardly, only suspecting she had said something wrong. “Then shall I eat one?”

Xie Wei: “…”

Jiang Xuening immediately changed her tune, “Then I will not eat after all.”

Xie Wei suddenly felt this was somewhat amusing.

But he was not laughing at Jiang Xuening.

He was laughing at himself.

Inexplicably, he shook his head, looking at the tea in his palm, but thought of Yan Lin, saying, “Willful nature, bad temper, and no sense of propriety either—I do not know what possessed Yan Lin.”

Why bring up Yan Lin out of the blue?

And wondering why Yan Lin fancied her?

Jiang Xuening twitched the corner of her mouth and muttered quietly, “So that is why Yan Lin has someone who loves him, and you do not have a wife.”

But the moment the words left her mouth, she saw Xie Wei’s eyes lift. She immediately said, “You are right. I am unlearned and unskilled. I am not worthy of Young Master Yan.”

“…”

This appearance of harboring resentment yet not daring to argue with him was quite amusing to see. But just as the corners of Xie Wei’s lips curved up a bit, they somehow sank back down.

Yan Lin.

The Yongyi Marquis household.

The coming-of-age ceremony.

Unknowingly, the day was already very near.

Having said those words, Jiang Xuening almost simultaneously realized this point. The relaxed expression on her face also fell.

She still remembered the coming-of-age ceremony from her previous life.

At that time, she knew nothing about the situation in court and country, nor did she know the Yongyi Marquis household was already in dire straits. She had already firmly resolved to strive to become Empress, but had not yet reached the point of putting it into action. So she was still very playful with a childish temper, pondering how to find an especially good birthday gift for Yan Lin.

As a result, unexpectedly, she missed the appointed time midway that day.

She was late.

By the time her carriage arrived at the Marquis’ residence, the entire mansion was already soaked in blood reaching the heavens, with armor gleaming cold. Inside was a scene of wailing and crying. The nobles who had gone to attend the banquet were scared-pale and weak-kneed, fleeing out as if running for their lives.

She grabbed someone and asked, “What happened? What’s going on?”

No one answered her.

So she took the birthday gift she had prepared and tried to go in to find people.

But the soldiers blocked her.

She desperately wanted to go in.

However, at this time, a severed head rolled out from inside, falling on the steps, splattering blood everywhere. She was immediately terrified. Turning her head to look, those people holding swords were all coldly watching her.

She did not know who pulled her, but finally, someone pulled her back.

After returning home, she fell ill.

Which was to say, in her previous life, she had not even been able to attend Yan Lin’s coming-of-age ceremony.

Later, Yan Lin had misunderstood that she was avoiding trouble, that knowing the Marquis’ household had met disaster, she had deliberately not come.

After all, not long after, she told him she wanted to become Empress.

Later, that former youth who had already experienced wind, frost, rain, and snow, returning to the capital draped in glory as a general, stood in her magnificent palace hall, gently pressed her shoulder, helped her remove the golden hair ornament from her head, and said to her, “That day, I waited for Your Majesty for a very long time. Standing in the hall, watching each guest who stepped in, full of anticipation, always thinking maybe the next one would be you. But I waited for one after another and looked at one after another. Prince Linzi came—you did not come. Teacher Xie came—you did not come. Even Xiao Shu came—you did not come. But I thought: Ningning promised me, so she would definitely come. So I waited and waited, waited and waited. I waited until heavy troops surrounded the residence, waited until the imperial edict confiscated the household, waited until blood flowed on the steps, but never saw you…”

Jiang Xuening had no way to defend herself.

Or rather, for that former youth who had fallen into hatred and darkness, all explanations appeared pale.

She could only silently close her eyes.

All the past life events suddenly surged back like a tide. After a while, Jiang Xuening slowly looked toward the teacup in her hand.

The calm tea liquor was like a small water mirror, reflecting the figure of Xie Wei sitting opposite her.

She asked, “For Yan Lin’s coming-of-age ceremony, I heard Teacher Xie will give him his courtesy name.”

Xie Wei said flatly, “Mm.”

Men received the cap at twenty, after which they could establish families and careers.

Receiving the cap meant receiving a courtesy name, used to explain one’s given name and express one’s aspirations.

Men born to noble families would basically invite distinguished scholars and renowned scholars to give them courtesy names at their coming-of-age ceremony. Though Xie Wei’s age could not compare to that of other distinguished scholars in the literary world, he was the Junior Tutor who presided over the classics lectures at the Wenyuan Pavilion. In the past, she had never heard of anyone who could invite him to provide enlightenment instruction or give them a courtesy name.

Yan Lin seemed to be the first.

Also, the only one so far.

But Jiang Xuening actually did not know what Yan Lin’s courtesy name was in her previous life. Had it been given?

After the Yongyi Marquis’ household met disaster, all topics related to the Yan clan became taboo. No one dared mention them.

After Yan Lin returned to court, no one could be intimate enough to call him by his courtesy name.

Perhaps there were such people, but she did not know.

Xie Wei observed her for a moment, saying, “Now all the great families in the capital know the Yongyi Marquis’ household’s situation is dire. Though coming-of-age ceremony invitations were sent, few responded. You do not look like someone with a kind heart either—will you go when the time comes?”

Jiang Xuening looked at him, saying, “Yan Lin is my best friend.”

So no matter what the circumstances, she would go. And in this life, she would not be late again, would not miss the appointed time, would not disappoint that youth again.

After hearing this, Xie Wei raised his eyebrow and actually let out a soft snort.

Best friend?

He did not know if he had something he wanted to say. In any case, he shook his head and ultimately did not say it. He also seemed to have lost interest in drinking tea. He only set down the teacup in his hand, saying, “Practice the zither.”

Jiang Xuening’s tea actually was not finished, but she was not very thirsty anyway. After talking about this topic, the fire from her earlier quarrel with Yao Xi completely vanished.

What replaced it was heaviness.

She set down the teacup and sat before the zither table to practice, still playing “Colorful Clouds Chasing the Moon” as the opening exercise.

Yesterday, she had played it well. By rights, today should be even better.

But unexpectedly, it was not as smooth as yesterday at all. Halting and stumbling, after just a few phrases, she played a wrong note.

Xie Wei turned his head to look at her.

Jiang Xuening stopped at once, looking at her slender fingers pressed on the zither strings. They trembled lightly beyond her control, causing even the strings pressed beneath them to vibrate.

She slowly moved her fingers away, folding and clasping them tightly before her body.

But that trembling sensation travelled from her fingertips to her heart.

She lowered her head and closed her eyes.

For the first time, Xie Wei did not reproach her for anything, only saying flatly, “If you cannot calm down, do not play.”

Yan Lin’s coming-of-age ceremony was imminent…

Not mentioning it would have been fine, but once mentioned, how could she calm her mind?

Jiang Xuening only felt a cold heaviness at the bottom of her heart, pressed by something weighty, unable to catch her breath. Even the spirited expression from when she had quarreled with Yao Xi earlier had lost its luster. She answered lowly, “Yes.”

Fengchen Hall fell silent again.

Xie Wei looked at the official documents on the desk, but did not seem to be reading them very well either.

Jiang Xuening sat in a daze before the zither table. Before long, her spirit wandered beyond the heavens.

After about two quarter-hours, a eunuch came from outside again with something to report to Xie Wei.

But seeing Jiang Xuening inside, he did not speak.

So Xie Wei stood up and said to Jiang Xuening, “Brew tea and read by yourself. Rest for a bit.”

Having said this, he walked out of the hall.

That young eunuch followed him to the corridor, lowering his voice to report something.

Jiang Xuening could not hear clearly.

Xie Wei’s matters—she did not dare to listen to them either.

Having sat blankly before the zither for a long time, she had not noticed while spacing out, but coming back to her senses, she felt her body was somewhat stiff.

This Jiao’an zither had been gifted by Yan Lin.

The youth’s ardent and sincere face still floated on the surface of memory’s waters. But the more this was so, the more stifled she felt looking at this zither. So she still stood up and simply truly sat at that tea table, reheating water to brew tea.

That dish of peach pastries still sat in its original place.

Jiang Xuening happened to see it.

When drinking the first steeping of tea, she did not touch them. Drinking the second steeping, she felt her stomach somewhat empty and bitter. By the time the tea reached the third steeping, she finally felt she needed to eat something. So she extended her hand toward that dish of peach pastries.

Snow-white slices, one after another, dotted in the middle with some whole peach kernels.

At first glance, they seemed about the same as yesterday’s.

But looking carefully, each peach kernel seemed larger than yesterday’s.

The palace cooks were not good at other things, but all kinds of pastries were made to look very attractive and smelled very delicious, though the feeling after eating them might be different from what one imagined.

But this was in the palace, after all.

Who cared if it was truly delicious?

Holding a thin slice of peach pastry in her hand, Jiang Xuening stared at it for a long time, mentally grumbling, then finally casually stuffed it in her mouth.

The glutinous rice was all kneaded together. Beyond being tender and resilient, it did not lack softness.

Sweet but not cloying, refreshing but not bitter.

This taste…

At first, she did not pay attention, but when the flavor spread across her tongue, Jiang Xuening’s eyelid truly jumped. She nearly scared herself to death by choking. Her hand shook, and she almost knocked over the teacup!

Never mind what flavor this peach pastry was!

In any case, it was not made by the palace cooks!

In her last life, she had all the pastry chefs in the palace try, and not one could make the flavor she wanted to eat!

In this life, the palace had not changed head chefs—it would be even more impossible!

Then this dish…

Jiang Xuening only felt that what she had just eaten was probably poison. She raised her hand to press her eyelid and also press her heart, wishing she could vomit out that slice she had just eaten!

Heavens, what had she done!

That same phrase again—how dare she even eat Xie Wei’s things!!

Who knows, he might be using this dish of peach pastries to test whether she still remembered those events from four years ago?

Xie Wei was ruthless and vicious.

It was all because his attitude had been too amiable recently, causing her to habitually take a li when given a cun, losing her vigilance!

Calm down.

Calm down.

It is just one slice.

Xie Wei had not necessarily counted them.

To the naked eye, this dish looked no different from before.

Rearrange it a bit more, and he will not be able to tell.

Jiang Xuening hurriedly reached out and rearranged that dish of peach pastries, concealing the gap left from taking one slice.

Then she waited for Xie Wei to return.

But after waiting a long time, Xie Wei still had not returned.

Jiang Xuening vaguely smelled that faintly sweet fragrance again. Originally looking down at the tea water, her eyeballs turned to glance at the peach pastries, then turned back. Then glanced again and turned back again.

Actually…

This dish looked quite plentiful.

Eating one more slice would not necessarily make a difference.

She twisted her head to glance toward the side hall entrance, listening to those fragmentary sounds of talking that had not yet stopped. Her courage grew somewhat. She stealthily reached out again, snatched out a slice from the dish, and quickly stuffed it in her mouth.

Looking again at that dish of peach pastries.

Good, very good, no flaws. Just that slice on the left looked somewhat abrupt, inexplicably eye-catching.

Jiang Xuening felt she could not let it sit there like that. If it were so eye-catching and attracted Xie Wei’s attention, that would not be good.

Throw it away?

That would be too wasteful.

So she might as well eat it. This did not count as her stealing food, nor did she really want to eat it—it was to make this dish of peach pastries look normal!

She swore that, after eating this one slice, she truly would not eat anymore. Eating more would get someone killed!

But this kind of thing called stealing food…

Where there was one, there were two; where there were two, there were three. Where there were three, addiction was not far off. Moreover, eating slice by slice, one really could not tell much difference between this plate of peach pastries now and before…

The sinful little paw reached out once again.

“Really, the last slice, the last slice!”

Jiang Xuening made a vow over the tenth slice of peach pastry in her hand, then bit down.

At this time, Xie Wei happened to enter from outside. He did not hear clearly, only saying, “What last?”

Cough, cough, cough!

Jiang Xuening was so frightened she shuddered. The peach pastry she had just eaten, before she could even swallow, got stuck in her throat!

She hurriedly poured herself half a cup of tea, only then avoiding the danger of choking to death. Turning around, she said, “Noth-nothing. I was saying this is the last steeping of tea and wondering why Teacher Xie had not returned yet.”

Xie Wei approached and looked. She had indeed brewed tea, but…

Had this dish of peach pastries originally been this sparse?

He looked at Jiang Xuening with a smile that was not quite a smile.

Jiang Xuening followed his gaze and looked. The small dish that had originally held the pastries…

When had the arrangement become so sparse?

No, no, no; it does not matter!

Maybe Xie Wei is blind!

She smiled awkwardly. “I was a bit hungry just now, so I ate a little, just a little…”

Xie Wei raised his eyebrow. “You take me for blind?”

Jiang Xuening gritted her teeth. “A bit more than a little.”

So Xie Wei said, “Oh,” then asked, “How did they taste?”

Jiang Xuening thought to herself that she absolutely could not remember the flavor from back then. Opening her eyes, she told a bare-faced lie, “About the same as yesterday. The palace cooks are just full of fancy tricks—they look good but are not good to eat. But they are acceptable for having with tea.”

Xie Wei suddenly felt—

This girl was probably truly tired of living.

With a thought, he walked forward, making as if to take away that plate, saying, “Since they are not delicious, you need not force yourself. Might as well throw them out and have the palace cooks make Young Lady Ning’er a fresh plate.”

Throw them out?!

Jiang Xuening blurted out, “Do not—”

The moment the words left her mouth, she wanted to slap herself twice.

Xie Wei stopped and looked at her with great interest.

Jiang Xuening finally understood that she was not just someone with a reverse scale—she was someone with a vital weak point.

The transition from extravagance to frugality was difficult.

Growing up in the countryside, her appetite was hard to satisfy. So having tasted something good, she could never forget it.

Her heart felt bleak. She simply threw caution to the wind—a dead pig feared no boiling water. Expressionless, enduring his scrutiny, face not flushing and heart not racing, she said with profound sincerity, “They are not that bad. People should practice frugality and simplicity, and not be wasteful.”

Then she took that dish of peach pastries from Xie Wei’s hands.

Xie Wei: “…”

If he had known earlier that one dish of peach pastries could subdue this ancestor so completely, why had he gone to such great effort before, coaxing and scolding, worrying she would not study properly—what had it all been for…?

He suddenly felt a bit doubtful about his own ability to judge people.

He inexplicably laughed once.

CONTENT END 85

chapters.title: Sharing
chapters.content:
When leaving Fengchen Hall, Jiang Xuening took along the unfinished peach pastries.

Xie Wei watched her.

She even explained with a righteous and stern expression, “Teacher Xie frequently enters and exits the palace. I imagine you would not bring pastries in and out. This way, this plate of peach pastry left in the hall would go uneaten. If left until tomorrow, it probably would not taste good anymore. Better to let this student take it back.”

Xie Wei said nothing.

Jiang Xuening took his silence as tacit agreement.

Carrying the food box in her hand, she strode out of Fengchen Hall with large steps: In any case, her cover was already blown—she’d played her part and pretended as she should. If Xie Wei had not noticed, he would not notice; if he had noticed, she could not change his thoughts or decisions anyway. Rather than that, while her head was still on her neck, it was better to live one more day at a time and eat what she could. Peach pastries traded for with her life—of course, she had to take it back and continue eating!

Having thought this through clearly, her footsteps became lighter.

Walking down the road, she seemed about to take flight.

Watching her from behind, Xie Wei only felt that both her sorrows and joys were very genuine and very simple.

Among all the study companions at Yangzhi Study, only Jiang Xuening was singled out by Xie Wei to spend additional time studying and practicing the zither, so her schedule often did not align with others. When others rested, she might just be returning; when she rested, others might already be studying.

This time was no different.

When Jiang Xuening returned carrying the food box, everyone was basically taking their afternoon rest, and the entire Yangzhi Study was quiet and peaceful. She entered her room and placed the food box on her desk. Opening it, she could not resist eating two more slices before pondering the situation.

Being framed had already happened once. She could still make excuses for herself, saying she was not prepared, that it was careless. But if it happened a second time, there would not even be excuses to find—she would truly be stupid and dull.

Rather than secretly guessing, it was better to clarify things face-to-face.

Moreover, in this lifetime, she truly had no direct conflict of interest with Xiao Shu. During her time in the palace, things should not have been this difficult.

The sachet that might have caused trouble now sat at the edge of her desk.

A torn and damaged scratch was very obvious.

Jiang Xuening stared at it for a moment. When her mind was made up, she closed the food box, grabbed the sachet directly from the desk, pushed open the door, and walked out.

Her room was in the most remote corner of the entire Yangzhi Study.

Xiao Shu’s room, however, was the best one here—facing south with windows on two sides, excellent lighting, adjacent to a corridor, and with no one else nearby.

It did not take long to walk there.

But palace servants stood quietly at the door serving.

When Jiang Xuening walked over, the palace servant standing outside saw her, bowed in greeting, and directly said to her, “Second Young Lady Jiang has come to find Young Lady Xiao, has she not? Our young lady is waiting for you.”

Jiang Xuening immediately raised her eyebrows in surprise.

This was quite unexpected.

She glanced at the palace servant without speaking.

The palace servant said no more, stepped forward to push open the door, and invited her in.

Jiang Xuening walked inside.

This room was decorated no worse than hers, everywhere revealing the foundation that only aristocratic noble families possessed. It did not look ostentatious, but even a flower vase casually placed in the corner had the sky-blue glaze of after-rain celadon.

A palace servant stood by the writing desk, grinding ink and serving brush.

Xiao Shu wore a light purple flowing immortal dress, one hand pulling up her sleeve and the other holding a brush, painting. A great river flowed away, both banks emerged, ancient pines stood upright on high cliffs, and a solitary sail drifted with its distant shadow gradually fading at the water’s edge.

The spirit was quite impressive.

Other women, whether daughters of great families or daughters of humble households, mostly favored meticulous flower and bird paintings, writing about spring resentments from their chambers. But Xiao Shu clearly did not love such things—she preferred ink-wash landscapes, her vision more expansive.

Or perhaps, this was the impression she wanted to give others.

When Jiang Xuening entered, her brush tip happened to be dotting the sail’s shadow. Looking up and seeing her, Xiao Shu smiled with curved lips and said, “I knew Second Young Lady Jiang would come find me, though much earlier than I expected.”

As she spoke, she set down her brush.

She also waved her hand to dismiss the palace servant attending to the ink and brush.

Only the two of them remained in the room.

Jiang Xuening had long known that Xiao Shu was not easy to deal with. Hearing this, she was not surprised, only saying, “Then it seems I am still quite beyond Eldest Young Lady Xiao’s expectations.”

Xiao Shu nodded, “Not just beyond expectations—I am almost impressed.”

Jiang Xuening said, “You are referring to the matter of the Yangzhi Study search?”

Xiao Shu smiled, “Second Young Lady Jiang is perceptive.”

Jiang Xuening scoffed, not wanting to waste words, and directly placed that sachet on the writing desk. “The sachet you returned to me yesterday is indeed mine. However, where you found the sachet probably is not where I lost it.”

Xiao Shu actually said, “I know.”

Jiang Xuening immediately raised her eyebrows.

But Xiao Shu fell silent for a moment, seemingly considering her words, before saying, “The matter of searching Yangzhi Study was my doing, but all this stems from an absurd misunderstanding. I did not mean to target you.”

Jiang Xuening suddenly found her very interesting.

Looking back at her, she smiled faintly. “I also know.”

This exchange was quite meaningful.

Between the two, there was mutual probing.

In fact, when she first learned of someone called Jiang Xuening, Xiao Shu had not thought to make her an enemy. First, she came from a high family, and few people could threaten her; second, there was no substantial conflict of interest between Jiang Xuening and herself.

To become enemies, both factors were indispensable.

However, after entering the palace, everything seemed to change.

Jiang Xuening was visibly receiving attention. Though her background was inferior, in the palace, she was no worse off than Xiao Shu herself. Following that was Shen Jie’s excessive concern for Jiang Xuening—he even privately kept an embroidered handkerchief. Anyone slightly perceptive knew that Shen Jie was highly likely to be established as Crown Prince, and she was a woman who wanted to become Empress.

Under such circumstances, Jiang Xuening was enough to become her threat.

And a very significant threat.

That time, she happened to learn the palace would order a search. Calculating before and after, she felt that even if this plan did not succeed, it could make Jiang Xuening suffer in the Shenxing Division. Whatever happened inside naturally would not be for Jiang Xuening herself to decide.

Thus, she could easily eliminate the threat this person posed.

But unexpectedly, facing crisis, this Second Young Lady Jiang from a minor household, remained calm under pressure and argued forcefully with reason, even going so far as to threaten with death, forcibly resolving this crisis.

Even more unexpectedly, the embroidered handkerchief in Shen Jie’s possession had another owner.

Her enemy was not Jiang Xuening at all, but her elder sister Jiang Xuehui!

What an enormous joke!

Xiao Shu had always cared about face. When scolded by her aunt, the Empress Dowager, over this matter, no matter how unwilling or displeased she felt inside, she could not refute it—

She had made a wrong move and played a foolish hand.

Going forward, she would have to deal with both Jiang Xuehui and Jiang Xuening, this newly made enemy. It really was not worth it.

No matter how strong a person was, they only had the courage of a common man, unable to withstand thousands of blades and swords.

Xiao Shu was unwilling to make too many enemies.

And right now, this sachet matter provided an excellent opportunity to remedy her previous mistake and reduce one formidable enemy.

Xiao Shu observed Jiang Xuening’s expression, gently waving her hand to invite her to sit, saying, “That day was truly a momentary lapse, an unintentional mistake. I nearly caused Second Young Lady Jiang trouble, and I feel quite guilty and uneasy. However, having no real connection with Second Young Lady Jiang and not understanding you well, I did not know how to resolve this misunderstanding…”

A momentary lapse, an unintentional mistake?

If that frame-up had succeeded, she would already be dead with her head separated from her body!

Truly worthy of the Xiao clan, born of a high family, really not treating others’ lives as lives—so high and mighty! Even Xie Wei did not have such a detestable face!

Jiang Xuening discovered that this was probably why she could never like Xiao Shu no matter what.

But she also had no intention of personally tearing into Xiao Shu in a life-or-death struggle.

Since the other party had the intention to win her over and make peace, she did not need to refuse immediately. At the very least, she should get back some interest before anything else, right?

Therefore, Jiang Xuening smiled faintly, feigning relaxation as she said with a slight smile, “For someone of Eldest Young Lady Xiao’s esteemed status to wish to resolve a misunderstanding is giving me face. How would I dare not respond?”

It all depended on whether one wanted to or not.

Xiao Shu looked back at her, seemingly weighing the truth of her words. After quite a while, too lazy to beat around the bush with her, she simply said, “There’s no point in going in circles with clever people. Let me be frank—if you are ultimately going to leave the palace, I am unwilling to be enemies with you. Although I am above you, harming the enemy a thousand costs oneself eight hundred. What’s more, I still have to deal with your sister. I am willing to show sincerity, but I wonder if that previous grudge can be written off?”

Written off?

What lovely thinking.

Quite skilled at forcing deals, are you not?

However, this was what she thought inside. On the surface, Jiang Xuening looked very agreeable, saying with great interest, “That is naturally no problem. After all, I am insignificant with little influence, isolated and alone, truly unable to contend with you. I just wonder how much sincerity Eldest Young Lady Xiao has.”

Xiao Shu picked up her sachet, contemplating it for a moment while looking at it, then smiled and said, “There are always some jumping clowns causing trouble behind the scenes, making people disgusted. Second Young Lady Jiang does not like them; I do not like them either. Why not handle it properly so everyone can have some peace and quiet?”

Jiang Xuening looked very satisfied. “That is truly wonderful.”

Even thinking with her toes, she knew some troublemaker behind the scenes must have used this sachet to frame her, probably involving some important matter.

Xiao Shu, of course, was not any kind of benevolent person.

All this talk of “sincerity” and “writing off grudges” just sounded nice. In fact, even without her existence, Xiao Shu would definitely find the person who really dropped the sachet and eliminate them to prevent future trouble!
