But Xiao Yuan did not notice. Perhaps because of Xiao Dingfei’s words, he was reminded of the scene from back then—his face showed a trace of ashen pallor, looking extremely uncomfortable.

Xie Wei still remained unmoved.

Gu Chunfang, who stood in the same row of civil officials, furrowed his brow and interjected, “Since Prince Pingnan and Wan Xiuzi discovered the young master’s identity, they likely harbored treacherous designs again and wanted to use the young master to threaten the Duke.”

Xiao Dingfei glanced at him.

Seeing he was a decrepit old man, he actually did not pay much attention, but noting his position stood even slightly ahead of Xie Wei, he knew this was likely an old fox. So he spoke with some respect, “My Lord, you guessed correctly—that is exactly what those two thieves intended. Although this guilty minister was young at the time, I understood the gravity of the situation and would never dare let the relief army fall into a dilemma. When Prince Pingnan challenged them to battle, whipping and cursing this minister, I clenched my teeth and did not dare cry out even once.”

That was a child not yet seven years old!

Pampered in silks and jade, a blessed child of heaven.

Being whipped and humiliated before two armies, yet able to clench his teeth and not make a sound—what kind of willpower and determination must that have been?

The court officials had all seen much, but hearing Xiao Dingfei’s words and imagining the scene at that time, they could not help but feel somewhat moved with pity.

But Shen Lang’s gaze turned toward Xiao Yuan.

It had already been twenty years since those events.

Xiao Yuan could not help but recall, speaking in a hoarse voice, “When the incident occurred that year, this minister was not in the palace. When I led troops to reinforce the capital, we did indeed face Prince Pingnan’s rebel forces in opposition beneath the city walls. The other side did indeed hold a small child from afar, claiming it was this minister’s legitimate son, but from such a distance, I could not see clearly. First, that child did not make a single sound, neither crying nor making a fuss. Second, as a minister, one must devote oneself entirely until death—even if that truly had been this minister’s child, I could not have concerned myself with it at the time. Therefore, after hesitating for a moment without paying attention, I charged straight into the city, intending to capture the two rebel leaders alive. Unfortunately, those two slipped away too quickly with oil on their feet, and in the end, they still managed to escape…”

Put this way, the events of that year and all the details before and after actually matched up.

Only Shen Lang still felt somewhat uncertain…

That glance back from the child who had studied alongside him before leaving, like ruins revealed when water recedes, slowly emerged in his now very hazy memory, overlapping with the pair of eyes of Xiao Dingfei below at this moment, gradually becoming clear.

Could it be he had misunderstood?

Was Xiao Dingfei truly a loyal minister? When he went in his place back then, had there been no resentment at all while his mother, the Empress, had kept Lady Yan in the palace as a hostage as a precautionary measure, which was actually needless worry?

Shen Lang rested his hand on the pure gold armrest cast with two dragons playing with a pearl, slowly saying, “But later, when the city was breached, you were not found. At that time, the Duke was also very worried about you, but in the pile of frozen corpses stacked like a mountain before the palace gates, they only found your clothes and jade pendant from that time. Did they not kill you?”

Xiao Dingfei said, “This is precisely this minister’s crime!”

He kowtowed again to the ground, “When this minister clenched my teeth and made no sound, Prince Pingnan was already enraged to the extreme and wanted to take this minister’s life. But that Tianjiao leader Wan Xiuzi said keeping this minister alive had great use. At the time, this minister wanted to end my own life, but that Wan Xiuzi moved too quickly, intercepted this minister, then actually bound me all the way out of the capital, fleeing to Jiangnan, where they imprisoned me. Unable to die and wanting to know what they were planning, I feigned compliance after enduring for a time. After many years of gaining their trust, I accidentally overheard that the reason this old thief Wan Xiuzi kept this minister alive and wanted to win over my heart was so that one day, given the opportunity, he could have this minister return to the capital, restore my identity, and then legitimately control the military forces of the two great camps at Fengtai and Tongzhou, making me their puppet. Moreover, this minister’s death would inevitably bring discord between the Xiao and Yan clans. Lady Yan is this minister’s birth mother, and Yan Mu is this minister’s uncle. If they lured them with news that this minister was still alive, they might well be able to win over the Marquis’ Manor.”

All the civil and military officials felt a chill in their hearts, and hearing this, every one of them thought of the previous case of the Yongyi Marquis’ Manor secretly colluding with rebels!

At the time, word spread that letters had been found showing correspondence with Prince Pingnan, the Tianjiao, and other rebel factions.

One of those letters said that the Young Master Dingfei from back then was still alive.

When everyone had deliberated in the Southern Study, they all believed this was bait deliberately used by the Tianjiao to lure the Yongyi Marquis’ Manor. Who would have thought it was actually true! Thinking back on the Marquis’ Manor case, suddenly all the inconsistencies from before and after became clear and transparent.

Someone immediately let out a long sigh, “Alas, treasonous ministers and rebels are truly detestable—how deep their calculations, how extensive their schemes, truly outrageous! Only the former Yongyi Marquis’ Manor was also truly too confused. No matter what, they should not have had dealings with such people! Even if Young Master Dingfei had died back then, it would have been a loyal death. For the Marquis’ Manor to act this way—could they actually have dared to harbor resentment toward His Majesty?!”

The fingers hanging at Xie Wei’s side quietly clenched tight.

A surge of sinister energy raged and rampaged in his chest, yet it was locked up tightly, unable to find a single outlet for release, instead battering his flesh until it was covered with bleeding wounds!

Kneeling on the ground, Xiao Dingfei’s line of sight could only see Xie Wei’s hanging sleeves and the hem of his robe. Even though he could not see his expression, hearing a minister say such words, he could not help but feel chilled and shudder. He glanced toward this person and directly drew an X over his head in his mind, treating him as already dead.

Shen Lang asked again, “So this time you were actually in Tongzhou…”

Xiao Dingfei then said, “After the Tianjiao heard that Gongyi Cheng had been captured by the court, they were terrified that he could not withstand torture and would reveal many of the Tianjiao’s secrets, so they dispatched heavy forces to raid the prison. Moreover, if they could rescue Gongyi Cheng, they could have him plan the matter of sending this minister back to the capital. Therefore, they sent this minister along. Only then, through this coincidental twist of fate, this fortuitous chance, was I rescued by this Lord Xie, able to escape the Tianjiao, and come alive to have an audience with Your Majesty to explain the circumstances.”

Everyone listening felt there were no problems.

Shen Lang also sighed, “So that is how it was.”

Only Zhang Zhe, standing below, lifted his eyelids and suddenly asked coldly, “If it is truly as Young Master Dingfei says, when the young master was in Tongzhou and learned that among those who returned from the prison raid, there were court personnel mixed in, your heart should have been extremely happy. Why then, in that critical moment, did you instead expose to the Tianjiao rebels that Zhang was a person planted by the court?”

CONTENT END 143

chapters.title: Arrogant Words
chapters.content:
Right now was the moment when His Majesty was reuniting with an old friend from years past, hearing about those past events. Among these officials standing in court and realm, who would not feel moved?

Yet suddenly Zhang Zhe spoke such words—

Really too tactless.

What a mood killer.

When everyone turned to look at him in unison, they all thought the same.

Xiao Dingfei had performed this act until even he almost believed it was real, as though he truly were that Young Master Dingfei who survived the great calamity twenty years ago. Just when he was about to give one more push and wrap things up, who could have expected Zhang Zhe to suddenly ambush him from the side?

Ha.

This dead-fish-faced fellow with his thick eyebrows and big eyes—it turned out he was not any good guy either. So he’d been lying in wait for him here all along!

That was right.

Back then at the Shangqing Temple in Tongzhou, he had indeed betrayed them at the critical moment and stabbed Zhang Zhe in the back, nearly costing the man his life. As for the reason behind it, though…

He unobtrusively glanced sideways at Xie Wei.

Zhang Zhe was someone recommended by Gu Chunfang, always an upright minister who could not tolerate even a grain of sand in his eye and had a thoroughly trustworthy character.

Though Shen Lang sometimes found this person troublesome, at this moment, he could not help but raise an eyebrow.

He directed his gaze toward Xiao Dingfei. “Dingfei, what’s this about?”

Xiao Dingfei had always rolled around in the marketplace—lies came readily to his lips, and his mind was agile. In just the blink of an eye, he put on an embarrassed expression, touched his nose, and said sheepishly, “A misunderstanding; this was all a misunderstanding…”

Gu Chunfang stood to the side with an air of composure, glancing at him. “A misunderstanding?”

In his heart, Xiao Dingfei directly cursed this strange old man who interjected right into a coffin, but he said aloud, “At the time, this Lord Zhang claimed to be a retainer of the Dujun Hermit. I am sure you lords have some understanding of the Tianjiao—this Dujun Hermit is as notorious in the sect as that dog thief Gongyi Cheng, always committing every evil, rotten to the core, and compared to Gongyi Cheng, even more elusive, like a dragon showing its head but not its tail. Naturally, I was afraid. To be honest, from the ruined temple in the capital all the way to Tongzhou, watching that child called Xiaobao, I always felt he was peculiar and strange. I tested him slightly a few times along the way, and moreover, he seemed quite concerned about my name being ‘Dingfei.’ So when the Tianjiao leaders said there were spies sent by the court within the sect, I assumed this person was Xiaobao, not Lord Zhang, who claimed to be a retainer of the Dujun Hermit. In that situation, I was trying to make the Tianjiao fight among themselves, to have the snipe and clam grapple. Who could have thought, who could have thought…”

The more he spoke, the more ashamed his expression became.

Right then, he bowed properly toward Zhang Zhe with apparent sincerity. “Who could have thought I would mistakenly injure Lord Zhang and nearly cost you your life? This one is terrified and begs Lord Zhang’s forgiveness!”

Zhang Zhe stood neither near nor far, his posture straight, a pair of cold, somewhat impersonal eyes watching Xiao Dingfei bow deeply toward him. He seemed not to have dispelled the doubts in his heart and did not speak.

In the Golden Throne Hall, the atmosphere became somewhat quiet.

At this moment, Xie Wei stepped forward and said to Shen Lang, “That one called Xiaobao is a fellow villager of one of this minister’s subordinates. By chance learning he was in the Tianjiao, we made him into a spy. Because Lord Zhang disguised his identity to infiltrate the Tianjiao, which was a dangerous undertaking, this was originally meant as secret support. Never did we expect to encounter Young Master Dingfei, which led to such a misunderstanding, a case of being too clever by half that nearly harmed Lord Zhang. I beg Your Majesty’s forgiveness.”

Zhang Zhe looked toward him but in the end said nothing.

Everyone already knew the stratagem was Xie Wei’s idea. That he had made secret preparations was really nothing surprising, so they did not suspect anything.

Shen Lang also had his own calculations.

He laughed and actually played the peacemaker. “Fortunately, Lord Zhang entered the tiger’s den with courage and strategy, returning safely. This time, he even rescued Young Master Dingfei back; he should be promoted and richly rewarded!”

Right then, he turned to ask Gu Chunfang, “For a promotion, does Lord Gu have a suitable position?”

Gu Chunfang said, “Lord Zhang excels at deciding cases. The position of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice happens to be vacant.”

Shen Lang then said, “Then from today, promote Zhang Zhe to Director of the Ministry of Justice, in charge of the Bureau specifically handling detailed reviews and vindications.”

When his words fell, there was an immediate chorus of praise and merit.

Just like that, Zhang Zhe was promoted.

Next came the distribution of merit rewards. Xie Wei received top honors. The position of Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works happened to be vacant, so he filled it. Generally, vice ministers were of third rank, but Xie Wei held the title of “Imperial Preceptor to the Crown Prince,” so with that designation, he counted as upper second rank. It seemed that if Consort Wen in the palace successfully bore a son and gave birth to a dragon heir, the position of “Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince” would surely be his.

As for Dingguo Duke Xiao Yuan, he was rather unlucky.

Originally, he had been the first to receive news and went to suppress the Tianjiao, but who could have expected he’d fall for their scheme? Not only did he fail to eliminate the rebels, but he also led many soldiers and nearly had his entire army wiped out in their ambush!

This was a reckless advancement seeking glory, not only without merit but actually at fault.

Shen Lang was quite displeased and directly fined him half a year’s salary.

This bit of money was naturally a drop in the ocean for the vast Xiao clan, but what mattered was the loss of face; it made him unable to hold his head up.

The most glorious one was none other than Xiao Dingfei.

He was rewarded with a thousand taels of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, silk and cloth, rare treasures and antiques, fine carriages and precious horses, and even directly granted the title of “Commandant of the Imperial Guards.” This was one of the Eight Commandants of the Western Garden, an official rank above fourth grade, with some soldiers under his command.

Others worked themselves to the bone and still could not climb to this position.

But he got it as soon as he returned.

It truly made others green with envy.

Only after the merit distribution was complete and Shen Lang had chatted with Xiao Dingfei for a while about old times in the palace from their youth, did he suddenly ask, “Just now when Dingfei mentioned the past, you invariably addressed him as ‘the Duke’ or ‘Dingguo Duke’ but did not call him ‘father.’ I wonder what the reason is?”

The court was full of astute and observant people.

Quite a few had noticed this point from the moment Xiao Dingfei mentioned Xiao Yuan leading relief troops to protect the Emperor in the capital, but they had not dared bring it up. Hearing the Emperor ask, their gazes could not help but wander back and forth between this “father and son” pair.

Xiao Dingfei had done this deliberately. Heaven knew that if he dared to call this bullshit Xiao Yuan “father” even once, Xie Wei would chop off his head when he got back.

Having just gotten his hands on gold and silver, he was loath to die.

A mocking smile and a cold laugh appeared on his handsome face as he said coolly, “Twenty years in exile, I have never regretted my loyalty to His Majesty, but one regret remains etched in my heart, tormenting me day and night, and cannot be undone. Lady Yan, the mother of an unfilial son, died due to grief; less than a year after her passing, the Duke remarried. Even with the imperial decree in place, I still feel resentful.”

Shocking!

Openly and clearly reproaching Dingguo Duke Xiao Yuan for being unfaithful to his first wife!

Suddenly, there were sounds of gasps in the hall.

Even Shen Lang had not expected this and froze for a moment.

Xie Wei lowered his eyes, quietly watching his own shadow cast on the ground.

Xiao Yuan’s face instantly turned the color of liver, and he flew into a rage. “You unfilial wretch, what nonsense are you spouting!”

Xiao Dingfei smiled without mirth and retorted sarcastically, “If you can produce an unfilial wretch, you are no good guy either!”

Xiao Yuan choked with anger. “You!”

Xiao Dingfei had grown up rolling around in the marketplace; his sharp tongue was no easy opponent. He’d long found this old bastard displeasing to the eye, so cursing him came especially smoothly: “A family of dukes and marquises, a prestigious household—marrying a second wife who enters the door seven months pregnant and gives birth to a daughter without any signs of premature birth complications, lively and kicking! The Duke truly did right by my mother!”

The entire civil and military court stood slack-jawed!

Wonderful!

Thrilling!

Dingguo Duke Xiao Yuan’s hasty marriage to his current wife, Lady Lu, back then had already been criticized. However, such a vast Duke’s manor truly did need a mistress to manage it, so remarrying after mourning his first wife for just a month or so was also understandable. But marrying her in and having her give birth to an eldest daughter who just happened to be premature—that was somewhat meaningful.

Everyone had originally thought that when this Young Master Dingfei returned to the capital, returned to the Xiao clan, and met his father from the past, there would be a deep father-son sentiment that moved people to tears. Who could have expected this was someone not to be trifled with!

Right before the Emperor!

A few sentences were like slap after slap, viciously thrown at his own father’s face!

Serving together in court, who wanted to see anyone else doing well?

Much less the overwhelming Xiao clan.

At this very moment, everyone’s faces looked proper, but in their hearts they’d already pulled up stools and clenched their fists, just short of shouting and cheering, “Fight, fight!”

Xiao Yuan could not believe what he was hearing, nearly choking on his breath, and raised his hand to point at Xiao Dingfei, his whole body trembling. “You dare show disrespect to your legitimate mother—this is truly outrageous…”

Xiao Dingfei said impatiently, “I do not even want to acknowledge a thing like you as my father, and that stinking hag counts for nothing!”

The Golden Throne Hall immediately erupted in uproar!

CONTENT END 144

chapters.title: Wolves and Jackals
chapters.content:
Vulgar and filthy language from the marketplace—many people were not unfamiliar with it, but this was in a court assembly!

Even the eunuch standing beside Shen Lang was scared witless!

Only at this moment did everyone realize that this Young Master Dingfei was truly not what they’d imagined. After all, he’d entered a den of thieves like the Tianjiao. Just listening to the way he spoke, the Xiao clan would surely suffer!

Officials from the Ministry of Rites always emphasized the word “propriety.” If this had been an ordinary occasion, they would have long stepped forward to reprimand him. But right now, looking at Xiao Dingfei and then at the Emperor, they pondered that this was the Emperor’s lifesaver.

Do not dare speak, do not dare speak.

Every one of them buried their heads down, acting like turtles retreating into their shells.

Xiao Yuan said indignantly, “Your Majesty!”

Shen Lang’s face fluctuated at such crude words, his brow furrowing with some difficulty.

But Xiao Dingfei had long prepared his words and likewise addressed him, “Of all virtues, filial piety is foremost. As a son unable to repay his loving mother’s kindness, that is already unfilial. This minister has no choice; this knot in my heart cannot be untied. If Your Majesty insists on forcing me, you might as well bind me up under the name of Tianjiao rebel and throw me into prison. This minister would be done with it all, dying cleanly!”

Shen Lang immediately said, “How could that be allowed?”

He glanced at Xiao Yuan and sighed, “Even a wise judge has difficulty settling family disputes; I cannot judge this either. You have merit in rescuing me. Before all the people under heaven, how could I repay kindness with enmity? Would that not put me in an unrighteous position? Since you’ve returned to the capital, there’s time to resolve this knot with Duke Xiao—no need to rush. First, rest and recuperate, and another day, enter the palace to pay respects to the Empress Dowager. As for other matters, we will discuss them later. Court is dismissed.”

As his words landed, as if afraid these matters would cling to him, he flicked his sleeve and walked out from the Golden Throne Hall.

The eunuchs followed, calling out the dismissal.

Though Xiao Yuan had towering rage, it was all suppressed back down. His chest ached painfully. Having no choice, he followed the other ministers in bowing down together, calling out in unison, “Respectfully seeing you off.” When he rose, with a dark and gloomy face, he was about to grab Xiao Dingfei and unleash his fury, but looking up, where was anyone left in the hall?

Xiao Dingfei had long since scrambled up from the ground. Outside the hall, he inquired of the eunuchs standing at attention with hands down, “Brothers, where’s the best brothel in the capital? When can the gold and silver His Majesty bestowed be delivered to my place?”

The ones guarding outside were just minor eunuchs—where had they ever seen such behavior?

Immediately, they were frightened pale.

Though the Xiao clan was indeed powerful, having been arrogant and overbearing for many years, they’d naturally offended quite a few colleagues in court.

Some with malicious hearts had already seen the signs.

Just after court was dismissed, three to five officials surrounded him, congratulating him and cozying up to Xiao Dingfei. In no time at all, they were walking off with arms around shoulders, not even glancing at Xiao Yuan once!

It was almost imaginable that the dignified Dingguo Duke would soon become a laughingstock!

Xie Wei watched Xiao Yuan’s flustered and exasperated appearance from afar, his face bland and invariant. He even walked forward to console him with a few words, smiling. “Why should the Duke mind? Presumably, your son has not been in the capital for many years and has many misunderstandings about you. Since you conduct yourself properly, given time, Young Master Dingfei will surely realize it is all a misunderstanding and apologize to you.”

It was better not to have said anything—saying this was like adding fuel to the fire!

But while Xiao Yuan dared to lose his temper at Xiao Dingfei, he absolutely did not dare lose it at Xie Wei. He could only say through gritted teeth, “I am grateful for Imperial Preceptor Xie’s comfort.”

Both having gone to Tongzhou to suppress the Tianjiao, Xiao Yuan received a scolding, while Xie Wei gained real power in the Ministry of Works, effectively promoted a rank. It could be called riding high on success. When he smiled, it only made people feel like an immortal descending from the clouds of the Nine Heavens.

Others also surrounded him to offer congratulations.

This made Xiao Yuan appear even more bedraggled and utterly embarrassed.

After Xie Wei finished dealing with everyone and was about to leave, a young eunuch hurriedly came to summon him to the Southern Study.

One could guess it was Shen Lang summoning him.

When Xie Wei arrived at the Southern Study and entered, he saw Shen Lang was actually playing weiqi with someone. Sitting across from him was a monk whose appearance was not particularly gentle—he even carried a bit of fierceness. Upon seeing Xie Wei arrive, he very naturally stood up, pressed his palms together in salutation, and said with a slight smile, “Amitabha, Lord Xie, greetings.”

Xie Wei bowed slightly and also smiled, “It’s been quite a while since I’ve seen Master Yuanji. Looking at you now, you seem increasingly peaceful—it appears your Buddhist teachings have progressed further.”

Yuanji was very modest: “Before you, I dare not speak of Buddhist teachings.”

These two—one was the current National Preceptor, the other was the Emperor’s tutor.

Back when Shen Lang was able to smoothly ascend the throne, he’d relied on these two’s full support, so they were quite familiar with each other.

Shen Lang did not need to say much.

He tossed a weiqi piece from his hand back into the box and only said, “Just now I was discussing with the Master about that Wan Xiuzi from the Tianjiao. This scoundrel lost to the Master in a debate on Buddhist teachings back in the day, but would not give up his treacherous heart. Now he’s bringing calamity to the world—truly a great threat to my heart. This Young Master Dingfei, who returned this time—what does Master think?”

Xie Wei counter-asked, “What does Your Majesty think?”

Shen Lang said, “I truly have not seen Dingfei for twenty years—how could I completely remember his appearance? Moreover, twenty years have passed in a flash. Childhood appearances do not count—people change as they grow. Only when I mentioned childhood matters with him in the hall did I also test him. He still remembered some amusing incidents. I deliberately made up things that did not happen, and he had no impression or did not dare confirm whether they existed or not—this actually made it seem more genuine. Only I truly dare not believe that the Dingfei from back then has become like this…”

His eyes flickered, actually somewhat inscrutable.

Xie Wei said, “If what Young Master Dingfei said in the hall is true, the Tianjiao raised him, intending to use him as a puppet—they could not possibly have taught him literary and martial strategies. Even if he had the talent of Zhongyong in the past, to learn nothing later and become useless is ordinary. Compared to whether this person’s identity is genuine, Your Majesty is probably more worried that this is a scheme set by the Tianjiao, right?”

Shen Lang then sighed, “The one who knows me is Master!”

He stood up, pacing with his hands behind his back in the Southern Study. “If the Tianjiao truly wants to make him a puppet, how do we know his coming to the capital now is not the Tianjiao’s scheme? Wan Xiuzi is full of cunning schemes—he cannot be underestimated. Only…”

Xie Wei continued, “Only this person is, after all, Your Majesty’s lifesaver from the past, and there are the countless voices of all the people under heaven. Your Majesty finds it very difficult.”

Shen Lang said, “The thorny aspect lies precisely here.”

Hearing this, Xie Wei laughed, “Why should Your Majesty worry?”

Both Shen Lang and Monk Yuanji looked toward him.

Xie Wei said, “Since Your Majesty remembers the old friendship and there are the countless voices of all under heaven, showing Young Master Dingfei double kindness and virtue is the natural principle. Allowing him to speak wildly in the Golden Throne Hall sufficiently demonstrates the depth of your grace. If this matter is a Tianjiao scheme, it will reveal flaws sooner or later. Rather than releasing Young Master Dingfei, it is better to keep him under your nose to watch. If he truly has no more connection with the Tianjiao, Your Majesty naturally need not be in a dilemma. If he’s still entangled with the Tianjiao, Your Majesty will have already treated him generously. At that time, killing him would be his own doing—who under heaven could criticize?”

Shen Lang pondered for a long while and said, “Thus, it can be considered that I’ve done all I righteously could. By the way, I heard you were ambushed on your way back to the capital?”

Xie Wei nodded. “All the assassins were death warriors. It seemed they came for Young Master Dingfei.”

Shen Lang asked, “Was anyone left alive?”

Xie Wei said plainly, “In the end, one was left alive; however, I saw he was a death warrior and knew no words could be gotten from him, so I ordered someone to kill him.”

“Ah, like that…” Shen Lang seemed somewhat not to have expected this. He lowered his eyes to ponder for a moment, as if feeling some regret. “That is really quite a pity.”

But he had no intention of pursuing the matter at all.

Xie Wei said, “It was this minister being too rash.”

Shen Lang quickly waved his hand, saying, “No matter, it is just a death warrior. Presumably, it was the Tianjiao’s side with their treacherous hearts refusing to die, wanting to kill Young Master Dingfei to silence him. Thinking he was with the Tianjiao for so long, he must know quite a bit about the Tianjiao’s internal affairs. Now that he’s just returned to the capital, it is not quite suitable, but later you can have him speak more about it. I will have to trouble Master Xie to take pains over this.”

Xie Wei bowed. “This minister should naturally atone for his errors through merit.”

Shen Lang smiled, “Master Xie’s words are too serious.”

Only then were the proper matters finished. He invited Xie Wei to sit down for a game of weiqi before ordering the attending palace eunuch to personally escort Xie Wei out of the palace.

After Xie Wei left the Southern Study, Monk Yuanji looked at the black and white pieces locked in fierce combat on the weiqi board, a thoughtful look in his eyes, and said, “If a death warrior was captured alive and brought back to the capital, it would not necessarily be impossible to pry open his mouth—after all, who is not afraid of death? Especially one who’s walked before the gates of King Yama once. That Xie Ju’an captured him yet directly killed him—this really does not fit with his steady and cautious nature.”

But Shen Lang let out a long breath.

He lifted his hand and lightly swept—the weiqi pieces on the board were all knocked to the ground.

He laughed coldly. “If Master Xie did not kill this death warrior, how would we know whether bringing him back to the capital and interrogating him would reveal the mastermind to be the Tianjiao or someone else? If he had not stopped the assassins, the one who might have died was my ‘lifesaver.’ If he’d captured the assassins and brought them back, the one revealed might have been Dingguo Duke Xiao Yuan. Between two difficulties, taking the middle path—it is better to kill this death warrior cleanly. After all, if the Tianjiao truly had such formidable death warriors, why would they not have used them earlier? Kill all the officials, large and small, cleanly. Either kill in one strike or do not make a move at all. Though Xiao Yuan is my uncle, he really causes trouble, doing things uncleanly and still needing Master Xie to clean up after him! If this time he had not encountered Master, if what he did behind the scenes was exposed, would it not make all under heaven suspect what happened back then?!”

Between his words, there was already a murderous aura.

Monk Yuanji then knew the Emperor had already developed killing intent toward the Xiao clan. Xiao Dingfei might truly become a good weiqi piece.

However…

He was more curious about another point: for instance, those two people under Xie Wei’s command, Dao Qin and Jianshu, were a bit too formidable. The Duke sent a squad of death warriors, yet they could not gain any advantage.

*

Xiao Dingfei only felt that his past life had never had such a glorious moment. Fair-weather friends, drinking and eating companions—the whole table was full of court officials and scions of aristocratic families. Raising cups together, they all called each other brothers.

Never mind what these people’s intentions were—drinking together, eating together—they were all buddies!

He completely performed the dandy airs he’d cultivated over many years to perfection. All sorts of bawdy jokes and amusing words came readily from his mouth, winning roaring applause from the whole hall from time to time.

After finishing the drinking session, he lay down in the warm private room and actually slept until dusk in one go.

The steward sent by the Duke’s manor to fetch him had long been half-dead with anger downstairs.

But he was in no hurry. After waking up, he lazily and unsteadily descended the stairs with uneven steps. Seeing the group waiting below, he did not even deign to glance at them. He jumped onto the waiting carriage outside by himself, but suddenly seemed to remember something and stood still on the carriage shaft.

The steward could not help but urge him through gritted teeth.

Unexpectedly, he actually said, “First, go to Lord Jiang’s manor. I heard Second Young Lady Jiang is exceptionally beautiful—even better than that bullshit Xiao Shu. When arriving in the capital, one must first pay respects to the local boss. I must personally go pay a visit.”

The steward was immediately dumbfounded.

The Dingguo Duke manor intended to bring Xiao Dingfei back to see what he was really like. The whole household, high and low, had practically waited for him all day. At this juncture, he actually said he wanted to go to the Jiang manor.

The steward was originally a confidant of the current Duke’s wife, Lady Lu. Naturally, when he heard that a “Young Master Dingfei” had suddenly emerged, he knew it was not good.

There was only one position of heir.

Originally, Young Master Xiao Ye was a sure thing. But with the addition of Xiao Dingfei, who was also the Emperor’s lifesaver, heaven knew what kind of struggle would erupt in the Duke’s manor.

Following Lady Lu and loyal to Xiao Ye, the steward naturally found Xiao Dingfei displeasing everywhere he looked.

He immediately wanted to refuse.

But on second thought—if he was so ignorant of propriety, would that not just be perfect? If this kind of reputation spread, wanting to seize the Duke’s manor’s heir position would be a pipe dream!

So the steward’s eyeballs rolled around, and he actually did not object. He truly ordered the coachman to drive the carriage to take him to the Jiang manor, presented the visiting card, and straightforwardly said he wanted to pay a visit to Second Young Lady Jiang.

This really frightened Jiang Boyou.

Immediately followed by fury.

During this morning’s court assembly at the Golden Throne Hall, he’d seen clearly—how could he not know what kind of absurd scoundrel this newly returned Young Master Dingfei was? Coming to the Jiang manor was one thing, but he did not even pay respects to him, the head of the household, and directly said he wanted to see his daughter!

Outrageous!

In his study, Jiang Boyou was so angry that he directly slapped the tea table and stood up, loudly saying, “Absurd! What kind of propriety is this! Quickly have someone chase him out! How can I let him ruin my daughter’s reputation?!”

Chang Zhuo, who was attending in the room, trembled fearfully, cold sweat beading on his forehead.

But he stood rooted in place as if his feet had grown roots.

Seeing him standing there without moving for ages, Jiang Boyou angrily said, “Why have you not gone yet?”

Chang Zhuo smiled bitterly. “Second…Second Young Lady happened to pass by and overheard. She’s already gone to meet him.”

“…”

Jiang Boyou was completely stunned.

CONTENT END 145

chapters.title: Stirring Up Trouble
chapters.content:
In the flower hall, Jiang Xuening sat on the left side, looking up at the person sitting to her right, unable to help but wonder: He also appeared tall and slender with a thin, lanky build, but how did the guts in his belly grow so fat?

She’d thought he would come find her, but had not expected it would be this soon.

It had only been two days.

Xiao Dingfei had not brought that obstructive steward in at all. He picked up tea and took a sip, narrowing his eyes with an expression of enjoyment, smiling broadly as he said, “Did not Second Young Lady say you’d cover for me?”

Jiang Xuening smiled, “You remember quite clearly.”

Xiao Dingfei cupped the tea bowl with both hands, sighing, “Second Young Lady does not know; I am completely alone in the capital with no one to rely on. This morning in the Golden Throne Hall, I even offended that cheap father of mine.”

Jiang Xuening gave him face. “Oh?”

So Xiao Dingfei embellished and exaggerated as he recounted the morning court assembly situation. But he showed not a trace of remorse; instead, he gesticulated animatedly, his words actually carrying a hint of pride as if he’d done something remarkable.

Jiang Xuening knew this was a complete bad egg.

In the previous life, Xiao Dingfei had been very close to her. Examining the reasons: first, because at that time she and Xiao Shu, and the Xiao clan were in an adversarial relationship, fighting viciously; “the enemy of my enemy is my friend.” Second, Xiao Dingfei was the type who did everything based on appearances; a lecher and womanizer. She just happened to be the type who loved to string people along and tease them. Were they not two peas in a pod?

She also liked people like Xiao Dingfei.

There was no helping it; a good knife could often stab the Xiao clan until they jumped in frustration, yet they had no way to deal with it. Even someone as lofty and unshakeable as Xiao Shu would often be angered enough to drink medicine to cool her temper.

As for this lifetime…

Jiang Xuening looked at how his gaze wandered over her face as he spoke and determined in her heart that the “judging by appearances” aspect had not changed. But the other reason was probably because of her relationship with the Yongyi Marquis Manor.

The Yongyi Marquis Manor was Xiao Dingfei’s maternal family’s. Yan Lin was his younger cousin.

Who in the capital did not know that she had a good relationship with Yan Lin?

Thinking of Yan Lin, Jiang Xuening’s mood dropped somewhat. When she came back to herself, she only heard the person before her getting more and more exaggerated; something about the Emperor nearly shedding grateful tears for him, Xiao Yuan being so angry he stamped his feet and wailed…

The bragging was about to fly to the heavens!

She suddenly felt a headache and had to interrupt in time: “Young Master, I already know. So what do you want me to do to cover for you?”

Xiao Dingfei was just getting to the exciting part, almost ready to say even that surnamed Xie would kneel before him. Being suddenly interrupted, he felt a bit unhappy. But looking up and seeing this girl who interrupted him with her red lips and white teeth, bright as the sun rising with morning glow and radiant as lotus flowers emerging from green ripples, with delicate crescent brows gently painted into one’s heart, he felt even the tip of his heart tingling, his whole body comfortable. How could he still remember any displeasure?

He ingratiatingly leaned toward her. “Nothing much, just want to ask for advice.”

Jiang Xuening raised her eyebrows. “Ask for advice?”

Xiao Dingfei counted on his fingers. “Look, I have a cheap father, a cheap younger sister, a cheap younger brother, and a cheap stepmother. Sigh, when someone like me returns, they definitely will not be happy and will want to mess with me. I heard you were also a notorious troublemaker in the capital back in the day. When you returned, you caused such turmoil that the whole household had no peace. I originally wanted to come learn from you. But then I thought, the Xiao clan is much more formidable than the Jiang manor, right? Tell me, should I act like a turtle hiding in its shell for a while, preserve my life first, get familiar with the lay of the land, and then mess with them?”

Jiang Xuening: “…”

How did she become a “troublemaker”?

Xiao Dingfei blinked. “What, is something wrong?”

Jiang Xuening smiled, “No, nothing. Just thinking, if you want to be a turtle hiding in its shell, I am afraid it will not help, will it?”

Xiao Dingfei did not understand, “How so?”

Jiang Xuening adopted the air of someone experienced, slowly saying, “There’s great learning in this. You must know, people always pick the soft persimmons to squeeze. If you show weakness from the start, everyone will think you are easy to bully. From then on, forget about peace; anyone who wants to will step on you. Think about what kind of life you lived in the Tianjiao in the past. Now you’ve returned to the capital, returned to your own home; are you really going to live more miserably than when you were with the Tianjiao? Then what did you come back for? Moreover, you’ve already offended them. What use is cowering? “

Xiao Dingfei nodded, “Makes sense.”

Jiang Xuening looked at him this way and did not believe he could not think of this himself.

But was that not how people would pretend with each other?

She smiled and said, “Young Master Dingfei, in this world, do you have any ambitions?”

Xiao Dingfei answered without thinking, “Eat the best food, drink the strongest wine, sleep with the most beautiful women; live freely and happily, and do not let anyone make me go back to suffering days!”

Mmm.

Exactly the same answer as the previous life.

Jiang Xuening felt reassured. Wearing a twelve-point benevolent smile, she said, “Then do you know who’s preventing you from living a good life?”

Xiao Dingfei thought to himself, “Aside from that dog-shit surnamed Xie, who the fuck else could it be?” But then thinking about it, without Xie Wei, he would not have today’s life either.

Only he could not say this to Jiang Xuening.

He put on an expression of listening attentively. “Who?”

Jiang Xuening misled him: “It’s precisely the Xiao clan.”

Xiao Dingfei became serious. “How so?”

Jiang Xuening guided him step by step. “You know about the Yongyi Marquis Manor?”

Xiao Dingfei said, “I know; it is my maternal family. It has already fallen.”

Yes, it had already fallen.

Jiang Xuening slightly lowered her eyelids, thinking of Yan Lin’s birthday, how the Xiao siblings had both appeared at the banquet, their words and actions, and later Xiao Yuan’s arrogant behavior.

A trace of coldness appeared between her brows and eyes.

Only she did not reveal it. In the blink of an eye, she smiled again and continued, “I feel sorry for the young master. After twenty years away from the capital, someone else has stolen your nest like a magpie. That Xiao Ye was born of a second wife, yet he treats himself as the heir. The position has not even been granted yet, but he’s already throwing his weight around in the capital. The siblings are both extremely arrogant, occupying your status, your position, spending your wealth, and enjoying your blessings! This grievance, even just thinking about it, I cannot endure it. If the Marquis Manor were still standing, if Lady Yan had not died from melancholy and worry, she would surely stand behind you to support you. How could it be the Duke’s turn to scold you in the Golden Throne Hall? Back then, if Lady Yan had not married him, he probably could not even have gotten the Duke’s position. A bunch of ingrates! Young Master, you are a dignified man; you should not weaken your spirit before such a pack of beasts, should you?”

Xiao Dingfei seemed thoughtful. “I should not.”

Jiang Xuening watched him, knowing he was full of bad intentions. Coming to find her today, he probably had not come with good intentions either. But she did not mind them using each other, so she said slowly, “You’ve just arrived in the capital. If you do not know how to stir up trouble, how about I teach you?”

Xiao Dingfei finally broke into a brilliant smile. “Second Young Lady is truly too good to me.”

After all that roundabout talk, this was what he wanted to hear!

He alone did not dare go stir up trouble; heaven knew if that surnamed Xie would use him as an example! But if he “learned” tricks from Jiang Xuening and went to do it, that surnamed Xie could not blame him, right? Moreover, following Jiang Xuening’s words and thinking it over, though that surnamed Xie had never instructed him on what to do when he got to the Xiao household, if he really became a turtle hiding in its shell, though that surnamed Xie might not say anything aloud, he’d surely be sneering inwardly.

Right then, Jiang Xuening raised her voice to tell the servants guarding outside to get lost. After people left, she called Xiao Dingfei to lean his ear close and whispered to him for a good half hour.

Xiao Dingfei nodded repeatedly.

When he finally took his leave, his face was full of the spring breeze. He looked at Jiang Xuening like looking at a Bodhisattva enshrined in a temple, cupping his hands. “The Emperor bestowed quite a few things on me; they should be delivered soon. Another day, I will have people carry them over to honor Second Young Lady.”

Jiang Xuening also felt in an excellent mood, looking at him. After exchanging polite words, she watched him leave the hall.

The Duke’s manor carriage had been waiting outside for who knew how long.

The steward and coachman’s faces were ashen. Shrinking their necks in the cold wind after nightfall, frozen and shivering, they saw Xiao Dingfei emerge from the Jiang manor with light steps and nearly ground their steel teeth to powder with hatred!

Xiao Dingfei did not pay them any mind.

After taking his leave from Jiang Xuening, he was as arrogant as if he’d obtained a death-exemption medallion, his nostrils pointing to the sky, not looking at anyone. He jumped onto the carriage and said, “What the fuck are you standing around for? This young master is going back to the manor to take a look.”

The steward nearly fainted from anger.

But after all, he’d mixed in a place like the Duke’s manor long enough to have some experience and position. He could still restrain his anger and, moreover, thought someone like Xiao Dingfei would surely never amount to anything. After returning and reporting to the madam, if she was pleased, there might be a great reward.

So all along the way, he suppressed his anger, just waiting to return to the manor and watch the Duke and Madam discipline this maniac.

The Dingguo Duke’s manor was a wealthy household in the capital. The residence occupied half a street. Outside the vermillion gate studded with door nails stood two stone lions that looked exceptionally imposing.

Right now, the manor gates were wide open, but the carriage was supposed to go to the side entrance.

As soon as Xiao Dingfei emerged from the carriage and saw this, he raised his eyebrows and completely ignored the steward’s guidance, lifting his feet to walk straight to the main gate.

The steward was startled and blocked Xiao Dingfei’s path. “Young master, this main gate is not for you to walk through.”

Xiao Dingfei was no good-tempered master.

He was the aggressive type. With a cold laugh, he kicked this sarcastic old thing. “Your mother’s ‘young master’! This young master is the Shizi personally granted by the late Emperor twenty years ago. If you blindly call out one more fucking time, I will chop off your head and bring it to the palace! Let’s see who will give you justice!”

The steward had come all the way to fetch him back, and though he felt the man did not like paying attention to people, he had not felt he was this arrogant. How could he expect that as soon as he got off the carriage, he’d turn hostile and directly kick him?

A pain in his knee, and he was directly kicked over and rolled away.

Like a rolling gourd, dust from the ground covered him all over; his head also knocked against the steps before the main gate, hurting enough to make him cry out.

But Xiao Dingfei did not even glance at him. He’d seen much more miserable and vicious things in the Tianjiao; this did not even count as a fart. He was even too lazy to move his position and simply stepped on the man’s chest as he climbed the steps.

The attendants guarding the gate had long been dumbfounded; who dared stop him?

They just buried their heads and watched helplessly as he walked in.

Right now, the eunuch who came from the palace to deliver rewards had just left. All the Xiao clan members were in the hall, and the dishes on the table had long grown mostly cold.

Xiao Yuan’s face was extremely ugly.

Xiao Ye had broken a leg in Tongzhou and now sat to the side with his injury.

Duke’s wife, Lady Lu, was several years younger than Xiao Yuan. She still looked well-preserved with lingering charm; only the gathered lines between her brows inevitably carried several traces of gloom.

Xiao Shu had also specially left the palace today.

When she heard news of Xiao Dingfei’s return to the capital, the Empress Dowager had already fainted. The Imperial physicians diagnosed it as her emotions being too agitated. Cining Palace told outsiders that the Empress Dowager had fainted from joy at seeing the Xiao clan’s blood relative return.

But Xiao Shu knew it was not that at all.

For the entire Xiao clan, even for the Imperial family, those words “Young Master Dingfei” were like a curse that could strike down and stir up the deepest fears in people’s hearts, making them shocked, angry, and afraid.

From the moment Xiao Dingfei kicked the steward and walked in through the main gate, someone had already rushed ahead to announce it.

Hearing this, Xiao Yuan cold-laughed.

He was determined to give this unfilial son a show of power and properly discipline him, so he deliberately put on airs. Seeing someone entering from afar, he sat in his seat without moving and only said, “You still know how to come back!”

Walking all the way from the main gate to here, Xiao Dingfei only felt that the Xiao residence was truly too large. Everywhere he looked were artificial mountains and pavilions, carved beams and painted rafters; it could truly be called magnificent and luxurious. Too extravagant!

Thinking this would all be his in the future, he really could not be happier.

So when he stepped through the door, his face also wore an extremely sincere smile. “Oh my, you are all waiting for this Shizi? How thoughtful of you; it could not be better. This Shizi was just thinking that, having just returned, I need to establish rules for you all. Right now, you are all here, saving this Shizi from seeking you out one by one.”

What?!

Xiao Yuan’s eyeballs nearly popped out. Caught completely off guard, he did not even think of what to say in response.

Xiao Ye could be said to be the person with the most resentment in his heart.

In the past, who in the capital did not respect him as the future Dingguo Duke’s heir? His father and mother had always told him that after he came of age, they could legitimately petition His Majesty to grant him the Shizi position.

But halfway out popped a Cheng Yaojin51!

Now he was told that his older brother from back then, who had saved the Emperor and been granted the Shizi title by the late Emperor, had not died!

The moment he saw Xiao Dingfei, his eyes turned red with fury. He cursed, “Who are you to dare establish rules? There’s hierarchy between elder and younger; Father is still here! Would you not first pay respects to Father?”

Only then did Xiao Dingfei notice there were others nearby.

He could not help but turn his head, looking left, looking right.

As for the others’ rebuke, he did not feel much. After all, having begged as a child and having been beaten and cursed at since young, he was not the type to be provoked by two or three sentences.

Only looking him over, he felt this young master really looked too inferior. Though his eyes and eyebrows were handsome individually, put together, they appeared mean and malicious, full of a petty air. Even though he’d always been unwilling to admit that surnamed Xie’s divine bearing and transcendent appearance, examining Xiao Ye, he really could not match one or two parts out of ten compared to Xie Wei’s.

Xiao Dingfei could not help but shake his head and sigh, “Come here.”

Xiao Ye was stunned, not understanding what he meant.

Xiao Shu watched this person’s whole manner and, for some reason, suddenly recalled how, in the palace, when Jiang Xuening openly framed You Yue, that kind of unbridled arrogance that regarded no one; she imperceptibly furrowed her brows.

Seeing that he did not come over, Xiao Dingfei thought this little friend was not very easy to fool, so he walked over instead. Very naturally, he lifted his foot and stepped on the square table before him that was laden with jade dishes of delicacies. With his left hand, he picked up a chicken leg from a plate, took a bite, and smiled. “What are you so nervous about?”

Xiao Ye sat while he lifted his foot onto his table.

This was clearly an insult!

How had Xiao Ye, pampered since childhood, ever suffered such treatment? He opened his mouth with a cold laugh, wanting to humiliate him. “Truly, the low-class airs learned from the den of snakes, rats, and thieves in the Tianjiao—”

But he did not even get to finish his words!

In the brightly lit hall, there was only a crisp “pah” sound!

Xiao Dingfei raised his right hand and mercilessly slapped him across the face. The force was so brutal that it snapped his head to the side, nearly making him stumble and fall to the ground beside him!

“Ye’er!”

“What are you doing?!”

Two shocked and furious shouts rang out almost simultaneously; Xiao Yuan and Lady Lu never expected he would suddenly strike Xiao Ye. Finally unable to stay seated, they sprang up, glaring at him with fury!

Xiao Shu fared no better.

When had she ever seen such a hooligan?

That slap was so vicious it made half of Xiao Ye’s face swell high; a shocking sight!

Her eyelids twitched as she said coldly, “Elder Brother Dingfei has just returned home, yet already cannot tolerate his own flesh and blood siblings. If this spreads, will it not ruin your virtue?”

Xiao Yuan walked toward Xiao Dingfei with a dark face.

Xiao Dingfei glanced at him, then looked back to see Xiao Ye, whom he’d just slapped senseless, had finally managed to sit up straight again. Just as he was about to open his mouth to say something to him, a low laugh emerged from his throat, and he backhanded another slap across his face!

The people in the hall, like Xiao Yuan, simply could not believe what they were seeing.

The servants attending outside were all scared witless!

Xiao Dingfei grabbed Xiao Ye, who was about to faint and collapse, and hauled him up. With a half-smile, he turned back to Xiao Yuan. “I advise you to calm down. You should know I am an important person whom Imperial Preceptor Xie brought back this trip. His Majesty is still counting on me for information to suppress the Tianjiao. If you dare lay a hand on me, I can turn your two ‘children born of a second wife’ into ‘children born of adultery’!”

Xiao Yuan only felt blood and energy rushing chaotically in his head. At his age, how had he ever received such intense stimulation?

Raising his hand to clutch his chest, his vision went blurry, and he could not stand steadily.

His body swayed, nearly collapsing to sit on the ground.

Lady Lu was both alarmed and afraid, tears coming out. She rushed forward to support Xiao Yuan, crying, “Master, master, what’s wrong with you?”

Xiao Yuan finally managed to catch his breath, trembling. “You, what exactly do you want to do?”

Xiao Dingfei only felt this family was used to peaceful days and could not withstand even this little torment; truly, too fucking disappointing. He could not help but shake his head and sigh, saying coolly, “I do not want to do anything. It is just that when you bastards have good days, I cannot have good days.”

It’s really not that I want to oppose you.

He thought to himself, “Your good days end today. If I do not mess you up, I cannot deliver on my assignment!”

Xiao Shu had always been a rare intelligent person. She’d imagined countless times in her mind the situation after Xiao Dingfei returned to the Xiao household, but none of them matched the scene before her eyes.

Someone who did not play by the rules; anyone who encountered him would find him thorny.

But she was still relatively calm. She quietly clenched her fingers, forcing herself not to lose her temper, put on a smile, and said, “His Majesty values Elder Brother. The Shizi position will ultimately be Elder Brother’s, and in the future, the Duke’s manor will also be Elder Brother’s. We are all family; when one prospers, all prosper; when one suffers, all suffer. Elder brother really does not need to be so wary of my younger brother and me…”

“If you, you stinking bitch, dare call me ‘Elder Brother’ one more time, I guarantee you will not even know how you died in the future.” Xiao Dingfei felt all sorts of falseness in those words, “elder brother.” Looking at her, though she had a pretty face, from the hair on her head to the corners of her clothes, not a single part did not exude an annoying fakeness. Just one glance made him lose his appetite. He could not help but mutter quietly, “Damn, looking like that, even if you stripped naked and begged me to fuck you, I would not.”

Though it was a mutter, the voice was not small.

Xiao Shu had studied poetry, books, and propriety; when had she ever heard such vulgar and filthy language? In an instant, her expression had changed dramatically!

CONTENT END 146

chapters.title: Weng Ang
chapters.content:
Early the next morning, Jiang Xuening heard that a fight had broken out at the Duke’s Manor the night before.

The great aristocratic families had servants everywhere. Any random person sent out to purchase supplies would spread the news throughout the entire capital, which would then reach the ears of the masters.

Not to mention it caused a commotion directly at the palace early in the morning!

Xiao Dingfei was truly a ruthless person; with just one sentence, he had offended Xiao Shu.

What proper young lady from a distinguished family could tolerate him speaking such outrageous words?

In her fury, at the slightest disagreement, she actually called for people, and both sides came to blows. Originally, they had not really intended to do anything serious to Xiao Dingfei, but who could have anticipated that this scoundrel would refuse to suffer even the slightest loss? After his wild remarks, he felt no remorse whatsoever. When the servants tried to restrain him, he kicked each one. In the struggle, inevitably, there were some minor injuries to flesh and skin.

Now that was it; Xiao Dingfei would not let it go.

Late at night, he ran to sit on top of that courtyard wall and wailed, claiming over and over that the Xiao clan could not tolerate him and wanted to murder him for his wealth. After his wailing, he slipped away. That very night, he stayed in the capital’s most luxurious brothel, the Cangjiao Pavilion, spent the night embracing fragrant jade and soft warmth, and even ran up a tab, saying that the Duke’s Manor would naturally come to settle it another day.

Even when visiting prostitutes, he made the Xiao family pay!

Before dawn had broken, Xiao Yuan, who had only managed to calm his blood and qi enough to fall asleep around the early morning hours, had not slept even one full hour before being woken by someone. It turned out the steward had come with a grief-stricken face, trembling as he reported that the pimp from the Cangjiao Pavilion had come to the manor to collect the debt.

Xiao Yuan could not catch his breath and, with qi rushing to his head, collapsed directly to the ground!

The Duke’s Manor immediately erupted in wails and cries.

On one side, they frantically summoned a physician, while on the other, a summons came directly from the palace, ordering this group of Xiao clan members to attend an Imperial audience.

It turned out that scoundrel Xiao Dingfei, after leaving the brothel, had headed straight to the Imperial Palace early in the morning.

The villain actually complained first! He submitted his token to enter the palace and accused them before the Emperor of being unable to tolerate him, claiming that Xiao Shu, a mere young lady without rank or title, dared to incite the manor’s servants to beat him.

Before the Emperor, he removed his clothing.

Good heavens, there really were some purplish bruises, clearly fresh injuries from last night!

Although Shen Lang had also vaguely learned that the current Shizi Dingfei was no longer the same as the former Shizi Dingfei and had mostly become a scoundrel, for him to cause such a scene just one day after returning truly made him, the Emperor, lose face.

No matter what he thought privately, on the surface, Xiao Dingfei was still his savior.

The subjects of the realm were watching.

He immediately flew into a rage and ordered people to summon the Xiao clan members to the palace for a reprimand.

Xiao Yuan was advanced in years, and his health was already poor. After fainting, he was barely revived, but his body was weak, and he could hardly stand. Yet the Emperor had summoned him, so he had no choice but to have people carry him into the palace. He could at least play the victim before the Emperor. Thinking of how favored he had been in the past and that the Xiao clan was the Empress Dowager’s maternal family, they surely would not really do anything to the Xiao family; it would mostly just be for show.

But who could have expected that Shen Lang would not buy it!

In the great hall, with a stern voice and expression, he rebuked them, demanding to know whether they truly could not tolerate Xiao Dingfei. If they truly could not tolerate him, then they need not tolerate him anymore; they should immediately hand over the position of Duke to Xiao Dingfei, and the Xiao clan might as well move out of the capital and split into two branches, which would be better than causing disturbances daily without any propriety.

The entire Xiao clan was immediately shocked.

The Emperor’s attitude was truly beyond their expectations. No one had reacted in time, scared until their legs went soft.

How could they still dare to speak of holding Xiao Dingfei accountable?

Xiao Shu did not think she was in the wrong and claimed it was Xiao Dingfei who had spoken disrespectfully and offended her.

But when asked exactly what he had cursed at her, she could not speak it aloud.

Young ladies had thin faces; that was one reason.

Prince Linzi Shen Jie’s selection of a consort was imminent; that was the second reason.

Although she certainly had not done anything improper, if Xiao Dingfei’s foul language spread, even innocence could be twisted into something unsavory. Her reputation could be ruined with ease, so she absolutely did not dare tell anyone else.

For a moment, she truly was like a mute eating bitter herbs; suffering but unable to speak of it.

When leaving, the Emperor still coldly issued a direct order, assigning a team of personal guards to Xiao Dingfei to protect his safety. Additionally, he ordered Xiao Yuan to punish those servants who had dared to lay hands on Xiao Dingfei that day under the charge of “subordinates offending superiors,” and if there were any repeat offenses, they would absolutely not be leniently treated.

Poor servants; they had acted on Xiao Shu’s orders.

Yet when the masters returned from the palace, they still had to severely punish them. Xiao Dingfei identified them one by one. Anyone who had pulled him even once last night was dragged out and pressed down in the courtyard to receive fifty heavy strikes. Their legs became bloody and mangled; they absolutely could not get out of bed for several months without proper recovery.

Devoted to their masters, yet their masters could not protect them and even pushed them out as scapegoats. How could servants have expected to encounter such a thing?

Never mind those who were beaten.

The other servants working at the Duke’s Manor, watching coldly from the sidelines, inevitably felt somewhat chilled. From this incident, they easily recognized the Xiao clan’s current situation: All that talk of aristocratic families with glory and wealth was bullshit! The just-returned Shizi Dingfei was the true future master of the Duke’s manor, personally protected by the Emperor! Anyone who still did not have eyes and opposed Xiao Dingfei was courting death!

Originally, when Jiang Boyou heard yesterday that Jiang Xuening had gone to see Xiao Dingfei, he had quite a few complaints, believing Jiang Xuening should not get mixed up with such a libertine and ruin her own reputation while also damaging the Jiang Manor’s good name.

But Jiang Xuening said, “Father, do not forget; I met this person in Tongzhou.”

Jiang Boyou did not understand at first.

So Jiang Xuening smiled faintly again and said, “A chaotic demon king like this; if you go along with his wishes, it is still fine, as he will at least remain within the capital’s territory. He’s the kind of scoundrel your daughter can see clearly. He’s absolutely not someone our manor can afford to provoke. If we do not meet him and anger him, and he reveals the matter of your daughter being kidnapped all the way to Tongzhou by the Tianjiao rebels, would that not truly ruin everything? Our manor still has someone who needs to be selected as a princess consort, does it not?”

Jiang Boyou had nothing more to say.

The next day, after hearing what happened at the Duke’s Manor, he sighed deeply and finally stopped mentioning Jiang Xuening’s association with Xiao Dingfei. He only instructed her to be careful in her conduct and not to go too far.

Jiang Xuening thought to herself: “Someone as slippery as Xiao Dingfei, beaten until he cried and complained to the palace, with purplish bruises all over his body? Heaven knows whether those were left by last night’s courtesan or if he had truly been beaten!”

But since this person was under her protection, there was no need to expose him.

Watching this master, full of wicked schemes, begin to torment the Xiao family, she could not be happier. She wished she could take a plate of melon seeds to the Duke’s Manor to crack them while watching the show. Throughout these days from after the New Year to the Lantern Festival, she had forgotten all her worries completely, feeling thoroughly pleased in her heart.

On the day of the Lantern Festival, a letter from You Fangying also arrived from Sichuan, saying everything was going well upon first arriving in Shu. Besides some local dialect she could not quite understand, the villagers were all very kind. The Zhuotong Well construction was proceeding energetically; the Ren saltworks had reopened and hired many laborers. Ren Weizhi, being a scholar by training, took quite good care of her, though he was somewhat single-minded; once absorbed in the Zhuotong Wells, he ignored everything else. So in matters of human relations and worldly affairs, she helped look after things somewhat.

It seemed everything was progressing very smoothly.

However, after reading this letter, Jiang Xuening furrowed her brow instead, only raising her head to look outside at the cold wind blowing and scraping. In winter, when things were dry and prone to fire, it was precisely the time to be careful of flames. Whenever there were new things and new ventures, they always had to experience some setbacks when first emerging into the world. It was rare for anything to succeed smoothly and simply. She hoped Fangying still remembered her warnings and would watch over Ren Weizhi, telling him not to be too aggressive.

Ever since the incident at the Yongyi Marquis Manor, after Jiang Xuening sold most of her shares in the Ren saltworks, she had only two thousand shares left in her hands. Most of the saltworks’ shares were probably in Lu Xian’s hands, with a small portion in You Yue’s hands. The remainder consisted of her own shares and some scattered individual investors.

After the Lantern Festival, she would have to enter the palace again for study sessions.

After thinking it over, she had Tang’er and Lian’er instruct someone to prepare a carriage. She rarely made a trip to the Shuxiang Inn to check on the situation.

Along the way, she naturally could not avoid hearing about the various glorious achievements Xiao Dingfei had accomplished these past days.

His conduct was already domineering and tyrannical. Ever since everyone in the manor knew what weight his words carried, who still dared not listen to him? Thus, fine horses and fragrant carriages, beautiful jade and beautiful people; anything good was hauled into his quarters.

What had originally been a proper Duke’s manor, luxurious though it was, had, after years as an aristocratic household, been decorated with considerable refined charm.

But Xiao Dingfei was vulgar.

All those broken wood and broken pillars were coated and wrapped in a layer of gold. Carpets had to be laid in bright red, screens had to use peonies, and even the footstool in his bedroom was replaced with one cast from pure gold.

From then on, when going out, he never mentioned he was the Shizi anymore.

He would smile at everyone and say, “Do not disbelieve me; actually, throughout the entire Xiao clan, from top to bottom, whether old or young, every single one is a grandson washing this young master’s feet!”

Ever since shares of the Ren saltworks were listed at the inn, the Shuxiang Inn had become a place merchants frequently visited. And because the Liulichang52 was nearby, with scholars and students coming to the capital for examinations often passing through, the inn became lively and crowded. Naturally, traveling scholars were also happy to lodge there.

Scholars loved to discuss politics more than merchants did.

There had been far too many events happening in the capital recently. As Jiang Xuening entered from outside and was led by a server upstairs to a private room, she heard several tables downstairs talking.

“I think this Shizi Dingfei is proficient in wine, women, gambling—everything. He really does not seem like anything good. Poor Xiao clan, actually being tormented like this. It truly shows heaven has eyes. Their past arrogance and tyranny has finally met someone even more wicked to discipline them.”

“That is not quite right.”

“Exactly. How could things be as simple as they appear on the surface? Just think, how favored was the Xiao clan in the past? Even the Yongyi Marquis Manor has fallen, yet they are the Empress Dowager’s maternal family. By rights, His Majesty should protect them. But this time, not only did he not protect them, he even slapped their faces. In my view, the Emperor’s heart is unfathomable. I am afraid the Xiao clan is about to face misfortune. His Majesty is merely using this Shizi Dingfei to warn and discipline them.”

As soon as these words were spoken, everyone at the tables was shocked.

Even Jiang Xuening, who was about to step onto the stairs, could not help but stop in her tracks and look with surprise and doubt in the direction where this person sat.

It was a scholar in a long robe.

From his appearance, he was undoubtedly a scholar. He had quite a handsome face, but his two long eyebrows flew upward with considerable unrestrained freedom. While others at his table drank tea, he drank wine. Who knew if he had drunk too much, but he displayed an air of wild abandon, as if nothing was beneath his notice; a sense of prideful talent, putting no one in his eyes.

The people beside him were startled and could not help looking left and right, lowering their voices to advise him, “Brother Qifan, wine can be drunk carelessly, but words cannot be spoken carelessly. You are drunk!”

That scholar pushed him away. “Weng is perfectly sober!”

With a smile on his face, he took another drink of wine, raised his hand with somewhat of an air of directing the nation and inspiring with prose, and declared boldly, “Look at yourselves, look at the court! Truly a bunch of useless people! The Xiao clan schemed and plotted to bring down the Yongyi Marquis Manor, causing the border to be unmanned, unable to keep the Tartars beyond the passes. Now their envoys have pressed all the way to the capital, and the great Qian dynasty must push out a daughter for a marriage alliance to secure momentary peace! Such backbone, such magnificent work! His Majesty is truly willing to part with his sister. If you ask Weng, whoever caused the disaster should be the one to fix it. Why not simply push out a daughter from the Xiao clan for the marriage alliance? Her status is noble enough, her appearance is good; guaranteed to satisfy the Tartars!”

These words became increasingly frightening.

Those at nearby tables truly did not dare stay any longer, deeply afraid this person’s misfortune would come from his mouth. They quickly covered his mouth and, repeatedly saying “Excuse us, excuse us,” pulled him out with much commotion.

The inn was immediately filled with a buzzing of discussion.

A dark gleam flashed in Jiang Xuening’s eyes as she lightly furrowed her brow. After careful consideration, she suddenly felt the name “Weng Qifan” was vaguely familiar, as if she had heard it somewhere. She smiled lightly and asked the server beside her in a gentle voice, “Who was that person speaking downstairs just now?”

The server said “Oh,” clearly knowing the answer.

While graciously leading Jiang Xuening, he smiled and said, “Do not be fooled by his frequent drunkenness; he’s actually a Juren53 from Hubei, named Weng Ang. Everyone calls him ‘Weng Qifan.’ His literary talent is quite outstanding.”

Weng Ang?

Jiang Xuening’s expression immediately became somewhat strange. She finally remembered where she had heard this name;

The unlucky Bangyan54 from her previous life?

He had clearly succeeded in the imperial examination, yet on the day before the results were announced, he got drunk, got into an argument with someone, and was accidentally beaten to death by several street thugs. When the news spread, it immediately shocked the entire capital. Beyond sighs of regret, everyone regarded it as a strange tale.

CONTENT END 147

chapters.title: Getting Scolded
chapters.content:
It was common knowledge that the Juren55 with scholarly titles need not kneel even when meeting officials in court, and wherever they went, people had to show them considerable respect. If they sent a visiting card to an ordinary person’s residence, not only would others provide food and drink, but they would also have to present some silver as a greeting gift.

In other words, they need never worry about food or clothing.

Generally speaking, thugs bullied the weak and feared the strong, and had to have some discernment; not everyone in the capital could be bullied.

Some had said this incident was highly unreasonable.

But others said, when drunk, who could recognize who was who? It must have been the wine causing trouble.

In any case, the thugs who beat the man to death ran away and were never caught in the end.

From then on, it became an unsolved case.

In her previous life, Jiang Xuening had been busy scheming over the matter of being selected as Prince Linzi’s consort at this time and had no energy to pay attention to the various happenings in the Imperial examinations.

She only heard about Weng Ang’s matter as a joke after marrying Shen Jie.

Today, unexpectedly hearing this person’s wild words and witnessing his wild behavior, upon careful thought, she actually felt there might be something worth discussing in this matter.

Pushing Xiao Shu to marry the barbarians…

These words coming from Weng Ang’s mouth could truly frighten a whole group of people to death.

But falling into Jiang Xuening’s ears, they took root.

Even after she checked the soaring share prices of the Ren saltworks, returned to the Jiang Manor, slept, and woke to begin preparing all the matters for entering the palace for study sessions after the New Year, these words still occasionally floated through her mind, unable to disappear no matter what.

It was already afternoon, and the remnant snow had melted.

Two weiqi manuals sat at the corner of the desk by the window.

They had been prepared at the notification from Jiang Xuehui’s side, saying that during the period when she was not in the palace, although Teacher Xie had received an Imperial order to pursue and suppress the Tianjiao and had not taught anything new, another teacher had been inspired to teach everyone weiqi. This time, upon entering the palace, they would probably continue learning.

Jiang Xuening now stared at them, lost in thought.

On Lian’er’s side, she was counting the banknotes and several ingots of silver cast in various shapes that had been prepared for Jiang Xuening’s palace entry this time, intending to use them later to give gifts to palace servants.

But as she counted, she pursed her lips.

Then she chattered away, “This palace entry date, not earlier, not later, falls precisely on your birthday. At noon, Madam sent someone to invite you over to celebrate your birthday together with the Eldest Young Lady, but you turned them down with just one sentence, letting them make merry over there. Those who do not know, seeing this, might think today is only the Eldest Young Lady’s birthday. If it were this servant, whoever invited me, I would go, and not only would I go, I’d celebrate more happily than all of them! Once you enter the palace, where rules are so strict, it will not be easy to make a big fuss celebrating birthdays again…”

After hearing her string of words, Jiang Xuening came back to her senses and realized she was thinking about her birthday matter.

In her previous life, how could she not have gone?

Indeed, just as Lian’er said, not only had she gone, she had celebrated happily. After all, the situation then was different from now. In her previous life, she had pleased Shen Jie, and ultimately, the person going to be selected as Prince Linzi’s consort was her, a virtually certain thing. Therefore, she was especially proud and deliberately sought to spoil things for Jiang Xuehui and Lady Meng on such an auspicious day as her birthday, causing everyone’s expressions to change with just a few words.

Jiang Xuehui had looked at her for a long time then.

Then, without saying anything, she dismissed everyone else and got up to take her leave herself.

What Jiang Xuening detested most was precisely this “sister’s” calm face, which gave her the feeling of punching cotton. So she chased after her and called out to stop her, asking with a cold laugh, “Do you not like Shen Jie? But now the person Prince Linzi will marry is me. Back then, you stole the magpie’s nest and took my identity, living so many years of comfortable, good days with food and clothing assured. Hatefully, heaven has no eyes and still lets you live comfortably and peacefully. Then I can only do it myself and let you know the taste of retribution.”

Jiang Xuehui still wanted to leave.

She stepped forward and blocked her way.

Only then did she finally stop, raise her eyes to look at her, and slowly say one sentence, “Are you truly happy?”

Why would she not be happy?

Marrying the refined and elegant Prince Linzi, stealing the marriage match from the sister who had occupied her identity back then and still bore the title of legitimate daughter to suppress her, having everyone in the entire manor look at her mood, with glory and wealth just around the corner…

Jiang Xuening felt she had originally been very happy.
