chapters.title: Wan Xiuzi
chapters.content:
A ladle of cold water splashed onto her face, and Jiang Xuening finally groggily awoke.

A faintly pungent taste still lingered in her throat and nasal passages.

She coughed twice, somewhat uncomfortably. When she tried to raise her hand to cover her mouth, she discovered both her hands were bound behind her, tied to a circular column about a chi in diameter. The hemp rope was somewhat coarse, bound too tightly, and had already rubbed the skin at her wrist raw, leaving several red marks of varying depth.

Water droplets fell from her thick, long lashes, obscuring her vision.

She blinked with difficulty, and her surroundings gradually shifted from blurry to clear.

A somewhat crude room with wooden windows and wooden floors. The doorway was crowded with dark groups of people. Directly ahead sat a raised-head table and a tea table. An old Daoist with white hair wearing a blue-gray Daoist robe sat in a chair beside it, padded with brocade cushions, scrutinizing her from head to toe.

A young Daoist acolyte beside him, seeing she had awakened, tossed the water ladle in his hand back into the bucket and retreated to stand beside the elder with his head bowed.

Jiang Xuening finally remembered.

Several days had passed since she was captured. That group of masked figures had suddenly burst from the forest with extreme speed. She had not even had time to cry out before someone from behind covered her mouth and nose with a cloth soaked in a pungent drug. In moments, she had lost consciousness. She had awakened several times midway, all on a horse-drawn carriage. These people would rouse her to make her eat something. But the watch was extremely strict; often, right after eating, they would drug her unconscious again.

Her entire being was thus in a daze.

Having just awakened, when she shook her head, it felt like she was shaking porridge.

However, upon seeing this old man, she suddenly became clear-headed.

Not only because she had never seen this old man before.

More importantly, waking now was not on a horse-drawn carriage but in a room. Moreover, they had bound her to a wooden column, which surely meant they were going to interrogate her.

Although this old man also wore Daoist robes, he was different from Xie Ju’an.

Xie Ju’an’s Daoist robes were the kind that worldly scholars and hermits customarily wore. Though improved from the style of Daoist priests’ robes in Daoist temples, they never embroidered the Taiji symbol or the Bagua71. However, this elder wore Bagua patterns adorning his sleeves and robe hem. Combined with his hair bound in a topknot, his tall and thin frame, high prominent cheekbones on both sides of his face, slightly sunken eye sockets, and eyes containing restrained brilliance, were it not for a faint air of heretical deviance about him, paired with that grizzled beard, he would indeed have had the bearing of an otherworldly master or enlightened immortal.

His pinky finger bore a not-short nail.

Though the person was old and thin, his face did not have too many wrinkles, clearly possessing the skill in preserving youth.

A graceful young woman of exquisite figure, appearing only sixteen years old, wore a pomegranate-red gauze dress. Whether intentionally or not, her clothing was slightly disheveled, her chest open, revealing her entire neck and one fragrant shoulder. She only obediently knelt beside the old man, gently massaging his legs.

The old man’s hand slid down from her neck.

Following her delicate skin, he gently placed his hand at her nape and then switched to the back of his hand, actually using this young woman as a hand warmer!

Jiang Xuening’s eyelid twitched.

Yet the old man’s gaze remained on her, carefully examining her subtle expressions. Seeing that although she had been doused with cold water to wake from the drug’s effects, she had only glanced around without panicking, he could not help saying, “Little lady is quite composed. No wonder he took notice of you.”

Jiang Xuening did not know who the “he” he mentioned was.

But looking left and right, those holding knives and swords were present; those wearing ordinary clothes and Daoist robes were plentiful. Yet only this old man sat alone with a little beauty massaging his legs. Without thinking, she knew he must be the instigator of this entire affair.

Where was any panic in her?

She simply said, “Your honor mobilized so many people, expended such great effort to drug and capture me. Besides binding me, you neither beat nor kill; clearly, I still have considerable use value. Since that is the case, my life is secure. What use is anxiety?”

The old man then laughed once, actually showing some appreciation. “Not bad. You understand the situation. This poor Daoist has cultivated the Dao for many years and has forgotten his worldly names. My Daoist title is ‘Wan Xiuzi,’ though you may also call me ‘Daoist Zhenyi.’ Taking such great pains to invite Young Lady Jiang as a guest, those youngsters under me acted without measure on the road. If there were any offenses, please forgive them, Young Lady.”

Wan Xiuzi!

Daoist Zhenyi…

Although she had been mentally prepared, when this name truly rang in her ears, Jiang Xuening still felt a chill rise in her heart.

Wan Xiuzi said, “Not even surprised by this?”

Jiang Xuening said, “If I am not mistaken, the attack on Tai’an Prefecture in Shandong last year should have been your handiwork. It simply did not succeed that time. There’s no principle of ‘guarding against thieves for a thousand days’ in this world; even wanting to guard against them is difficult. The Daoist Master schemed and waited for the right moment to strike. Success is not strange.”

Wan Xiuzi immediately clapped his hands and laughed heartily. “Good, good!”

Jiang Xuening had indeed heard of this person.

Although she had never seen him in her previous life and did not know his ultimate fate, over twenty years ago, he had allied with Prince Pingnan’s faction to attack the capital, dyeing half the capital with blood. Even the Imperial clan nearly perished; this could be considered a heavily inked entry in the history of treason.

The court simply hated this person to the bone.

Unfortunately, the Tianjiao held great power in the south. Ever since that failed attempt years ago, Wan Xiuzi rarely appeared before others again, only controlling the cult members through trusted subordinates. Unless absolutely necessary, he never showed himself, keeping his whereabouts extremely secret.

So even though the authorities had conducted multiple extermination campaigns, they had achieved nothing.

For the moment, she could not quite guess why the other party had captured her, so she dared not speak easily.

However, the girl kneeling on the ground massaging Wan Xiuzi’s legs, hearing Wan Xiuzi speak so pleasantly to Jiang Xuening, actually became jealous. She shot Jiang Xuening a sideways glance, then turned her head to press her chest forward even more pitifully toward Wan Xiuzi, her voice so soft and coquettish it gave one goosebumps. “Cult Leader, dusk is already approaching. Would you not take your immortal elixir? This servant…this servant’s legs have been kneeling so long…”

Wan Xiuzi looked down at her.

That young woman then ingratiatingly drew from her bosom a purple-red pill and offered it to him. This pill had been refined with much effort and was what Wan Xiuzi took daily. As for its effects…

Wan Xiuzi also groped the woman’s face before taking that small pill and swallowing it.

Watching this, Jiang Xuening vaguely perceived the relationship between these two, viewing it with a wave of revulsion.

After taking the pill, Wan Xiuzi’s complexion became slightly more ruddy. He only tapped with his hand across the young woman’s chest and neck and finally pinched her chin, lifting her face to examine it. Then he looked again at Jiang Xuening, as if comparing something.

That woman said sourly, “Am I not beautiful?”

Wan Xiuzi had been fine before, but somehow after this sentence, his expression instantly darkened. He actually pinched the woman’s chin and roughly pushed her backward, coldly mocking, “You dare compare yourself to her?”

That woman aggrievedly shed tears.

Wan Xiuzi seemed about to lash out, but seeing her pitiful appearance, he gently reached out to pat her cheek, treating her like a plaything. Yet in a flash, he recovered that previous bland tone, saying, “Dujun broke his rule and took a liking to her. Naturally, she’s much better than you.”

That woman bit her lips tightly, yet in an instant looked toward Jiang Xuening, seemingly unable to believe it, even showing jealousy stronger than before.

Even the surrounding cult members suddenly produced some clamorous voices.

Gazes from all sides seemed to suddenly fall upon Jiang Xuening.

There was surprise; there was inquiry; there was disbelief.

Jiang Xuening’s entire being felt somewhat off; not that she had not seen the world or was frightened by this small scene, but rather, she felt these people now looked at her differently than before, as if examining someone they had never seen before.

Listening carefully, she vaguely heard someone say, “Master Dujun actually found someone to cultivate with,” and “This woman has such great ability”…

The “Dujun” mentioned in their words…

Jiang Xuening had an impression of this name. During the Tongzhou battle, Zhang Zhe had infiltrated the Tianjiao under the false name “Master Dujun”! Now, Wan Xiuzi actually said it was Dujun who had taken a liking to her?

Her thoughts raced, and her expression inevitably changed somewhat.

Wan Xiuzi saw this.

He suddenly realized something. His whitish pupils slowly turned in a circle. “You still do not know Dujun’s identity?”

Jiang Xuening’s heart jumped.

Without Wan Xiuzi’s question, she naturally would not have understood.

However, with this additional question, a flash of inspiration in her mind split like lightning, nearly causing her entire body to tremble. In her heart floated that answer that no one would dare believe if spoken.

Xie Ju’an!

Wan Xiuzi smacked his lips, seeming to find it interesting. He pulled that young woman over, groping up and down. His abdomen hardened, yet his expression seemed unmoved. Only when mentioning the two characters “Dujun” did he gradually recall events of these twenty-some years.

He coldly snorted.

When speaking, however, there was a somewhat sighing feeling: “So many years in a flash. Originally, we thought we were doing good deeds for Heaven, never imagining we’d invited wolves into the house, nurturing a tiger as calamity. This poor Daoist is not exactly unable to endure, only that though this body is still properly nourished, able to possess women at night, harmonizing yin and yang as the way of cultivation, ultimately, years pass easily, and life spans are finite. If we do not raise an uprising now, I fear it will only be making a wedding dress for that surnamed Xie. Never thought that Heaven has virtue in cherishing life and actually aided me; he was misled by female beauty, exposing such a great flaw! How could this poor Daoist not accept with a smile?”

Jiang Xuening vaguely understood the meaning: they had captured her to deal with Xie Ju’an.

That young woman hummed and whimpered under Wan Xiuzi’s hands.

Yet Wan Xiuzi treated her only like an object. Though he toyed with her, there was not half a trace of pity; watching it only made one’s hair stand on end.

He even laughed once.

Only saying, “Our Tianjiao is the orthodox Daoist tradition and should seek to reduce desires. However, merely abstaining from bedroom affairs does not count as cultivation. It must be the harmonization of male yang and female yin, separation of body and mind, bodies merging while mind guards the center, not disturbing one’s nature; only this is ‘attaining the Dao.’ I originally thought he had wisdom roots, so I had Gongyi find several clean ones, born in a yin year, yin month, and yin day, and put them on his bed for him to cultivate with. I was thinking, ‘solitary yang cannot grow long.’ That place of women is ultimately a soul-destroying den, a hero’s tomb. Without early cultivation, when encountering some exceptional beauty or seductress on an important day, he would be unable to walk away from the lower half of his body; it would ultimately ruin matters. Who knew he would not appreciate the favor?”

Speaking to this point, Wan Xiuzi’s expression had already become somewhat pleased.

Especially when looking toward Jiang Xuening, he actually revealed some satisfaction.

These two years, he had rarely encountered such a proud moment, especially catching Xie Wei’s weakness. Just waiting for him to walk into the trap, his entire person relaxed considerably. “Hmph, these years I also knew he was restless. In the capital, he clearly no longer placed this Cult Leader in his eyes. However, he’s always been meticulous in his actions, untouched by desire, love, or hate. Even killing several of his trusted subordinates, he’s cold-blooded, not blinking an eye, not asking a question. Truly, I could not find any flaw. Pity that when he paid no attention back then, I could not get a hold on him. Now, it has become his fatal weakness. Such a formidable person ultimately could not escape the character for ’emotion,’ falling at a woman’s hands. Even Heaven favors me, wanting me to ascend the great throne and dominate the world!”

Listening to this foul old Daoist’s obscene talk, Jiang Xuening’s complexion had already worsened considerably.

Thinking again of how she was trapped, yet not knowing how much trouble she would bring to Xie Wei, Yan Lin, and others, she had even less ability to smile.

Yet Wan Xiuzi seemed deliberate, asking again, “He was stabbed by you and did not strike back. Presumably, having you accompany him in cultivation was quite enjoyable?”

“Cultivation”…

The corner of Jiang Xuening’s eye twitched slightly. She simply acted as if she had not heard.

Instead, she said, “In the palace, there are magicians who refine cinnabar with mercury, serving only the Son of Heaven, able to make people return to their youthful prime. If the Cult Leader worries about advancing years, you might try it.”

“Ha ha ha ha…”

Wan Xiuzi actually threw his head back and laughed aloud, completely unmoved by her words.

“That dog Emperor obtained elixir pills presented by evil magicians; his life will not last long! Little lady, do you think I do not know mercury is severely toxic? Daoist cultivation is the way of nourishing life, naturally requiring gentle tonification. If you want to see me take an elixir pill and die suddenly, I am afraid that is not possible.”

Jiang Xuening: “…”

A cult leader seriously pursuing health cultivation among these lands full of mercury-pill-taking magicians; truly a clear stream indeed.

She was genuinely impressed.

Wan Xiuzi glanced at the gradually darkening sky outside, only saying, “Less than two hours remain. If Dujun does not come…”

He turned his gaze back to Jiang Xuening.

Jiang Xuening silently cursed in her heart. Thinking of Xie Ju’an’s character, she was too lazy to even roll her eyes at this Cult Leader, only saying, “Do not worry, Xie Ju’an will definitely come. He just definitely will not come alone. If I were the Cult Leader, I’d pack up and run now; there’s still time.”

Wan Xiuzi’s pupils slightly contracted, as if weighing her words.

After a long while, he laughed eerily, saying ominously, “This seat also wants to see.”

The two spoke no more.

Though Jiang Xuening spoke thus, it was only based on her previous life’s understanding of Xie Wei and this life’s interactions with him. Her heart was not truly confident. When that person went crazy, she had truly witnessed what he was like. Doing something like going alone into the tiger’s den—it was not impossible.

Only then would he fall into someone’s trap.

Not only would he fail to rescue her, but he would likely plunge both of them into the same predicament.

In her heart, she prayed that Xie Ju’an would not appear.

Thus, waiting until the beginning of the hour of Zi72, still no one came.

Wan Xiuzi’s complexion grew worse and worse.

Just as the third quarter of the hour of Zi’s drum sound was about to ring, a rush of hurried footsteps sounded outside. A Daoist acolyte knelt outside the door, reporting, “Reporting to the Cult Leader, Master Dujun requests an audience outside the branch headquarters! The Xinzhou army shows no abnormal movement. Along the way, no one followed. He has indeed returned to Tianjiao alone!”

CONTENT END 225

chapters.title: Staging a Good Show
chapters.content:
In Luoyang at midnight, cold stars hung in the sky, with no bright moon to be seen.

Outside the gates of Guiyi Manor ahead, not a single soul could be seen.

However, the two people guarding the gate had thick hands and feet, broad shoulders, and thick waists. With their arms crossed and holding swords and blades, their icy gazes swept over Xie Wei, revealing thick vigilance, and also…

A hint of undisguised surprise and curiosity.

Throughout the Tianjiao, not many had seen him; even fewer had seen him and also knew he was the legendary “Master Dujun.”

Yet these past days, rumors about him had spread everywhere.

They all said that Mister Gongyi’s death was full of suspicious points; this person had not only betrayed the Tianjiao but also intended to repay kindness with enmity, creating friction with the Sect Leader. This trip to Luoyang was finally when the Sect Leader would display his divine might, emerging from seclusion to deal with him.

But who could have imagined that the legendary Master Dujun would be like this?

Wearing plain, simple Daoist robes, though bearing some traces of a dusty journey, his ink-painted brows and eyes carried a kind of calm indifference, unperturbed by waves. Though he came alone, he showed not the slightest trace of fear.

More importantly, he was not some wretched old man…

Compared to Gongyi Cheng, whom they had often seen before, Xie Ju’an was truly too young, to the point where they could hardly believe it.

However, soon the Daoist acolyte who had gone inside to report came back out.

Upon reaching the gate, he was still respectful.

He actually bowed to Xie Wei, though with an unavoidably insincere smile, saying, “The Sect Leader and that Second Young Lady Jiang have been respectfully waiting for quite some time. Master, please enter.”

The street was completely empty and desolate. Wind blew from the deserted street, brushing past Xie Wei’s robes, making them flutter and sway.

Yet his expression remained steadfast.

Without saying much, he lowered his eyelids, showing not the slightest trace of fear. Rather than appearing like an unlucky wretch being constrained by others and about to become a prisoner, he displayed a composure and calmness in facing changes, as if entering his own home, following the acolyte through the gate.

In his twenty-plus years with the Tianjiao, he had rarely issued orders or devised strategies under the name “Xie Wei” but instead used the title “Master Dujun” to represent himself. This was so that in the future, when infiltrating the court, the name “Xie Wei” would remain clean and pure, avoiding the court’s suspicions and revealing too many traces.

Thus, he rarely visited the various branch altars.

He was unfamiliar with this Luoyang branch altar. As he followed the acolyte, he looked around unobtrusively. Finally, after twisting and turning through seven or eight corners, they reached a courtyard within the manor.

Outside hung bright lanterns. Below the lanterns, a dark mass of Tianjiao followers stood.

The acolyte announced, “Master Dujun has arrived.”

In that instant, everyone’s gaze turned toward him, landing on him. Then, the surrounding crowd slowly parted like a receding tide, making way for him, though their gazes followed him all along, eyeing him like tigers stalking prey.

But Xie Wei acted as if he saw nothing.

He did not even glance at these followers. He walked straight through the parted path into the courtyard and then saw the open door inside.

Wan Xiuzi had gone through such great efforts and scheming to capture Jiang Xuening, believing that Dujun held this woman in special regard, thinking Heaven had granted him an opportunity, perhaps allowing him to grasp his weakness.

However, this was speculation from beginning to end.

If Xie Ju’an, upon receiving the letter he left behind, disregarded this woman’s life or death today and did not come, he actually would not be surprised in the least. Therefore, when he personally heard that Xie Wei had come and personally saw him walk in from outside, Wan Xiuzi, sitting in his chair, unconsciously tightened the grip of the hand that was clutching the young woman’s shoulder, feeling greatly invigorated.

The young woman had not expected this and let out a soft cry of pain.

However, Wan Xiuzi had already pushed her aside with one motion. His eyes blazed with intense light, carrying a somewhat chilling coldness, quickly locking onto Xie Wei as he laughed, “Good, such boldness! You actually dare to come!”

Xie Wei stood there without offering any courtesy.

He did not even look at Wan Xiuzi first, but instead looked toward Jiang Xuening.

From the moment she heard the acolyte come to report that Xie Ju’an had already arrived, her heart had begun to sink; now, seeing Xie Wei walk in, she felt her heart sink even deeper to the bottom of a valley.

Jiang Xuening was still bound to the round pillar.

For several days, she had been drugged unconscious during the journey and not long ago had been splashed awake with a ladle of water. Her face appeared somewhat pale and haggard, with a few drops of water that had not yet dried rolling down her cheeks. A pair of dark pupils gazed toward him, her eyes flickering lightly, as if she had many things to say, yet all were hidden in silence.

In these recent days, Xie Ju’an had thought countless times about what the situation would be like when he saw her at the Luoyang branch altar.

With the big picture at hand, he should control himself.

So after imagining all sorts of circumstances in his mind, even the worst ones, he thought that when he saw Jiang Xuening again, he would be as calm as still water, revealing not the slightest flaw. Moreover, the situation was far from as bad as he had imagined. Yet just this one hesitant glance, containing a worry as light as threads of smoke, struck hard against his heart, nearly causing him to lose control in that instant and reveal the deeply buried malice and murderous intent in the depths of his heart.

Wan Xiuzi watched him with great interest, saying, “So you really do care about this little girl?”

Only then did Xie Wei turn his gaze.

With just one glance at the pitiful, disheveled young woman at Wan Xiuzi’s feet, he knew nothing good had happened in this room earlier. Thinking again that Jiang Xuening had been watching in this room just now, the frost in his eyes deepened by several degrees. Yet he said, “The Sect Leader summoned me; how dare I not arrive? However, Jiang Xuening is the daughter of a court colleague and had once saved my life. By sentiment and reason, she should not be implicated because of me. She’s merely an unimportant outsider and not a daughter highly valued in Jiang Boyou’s household, either. I am afraid she has no value for exploitation.”

This was to distance himself from any relationship with her.

However…

A trace of suspicion suddenly arose in Jiang Xuening’s heart. For some reason, seeing him calmly and composedly answer Wan Xiuzi’s questions, she felt inexplicably much more settled: Xie Ju’an was someone bearing a blood feud; his revenge not yet complete, he surely would not truly place himself in a perilous situation with no way to turn things around. He must have come prepared. Just these few sentences distancing their relationship were worth deep consideration.

Sure enough, if Jiang Xuening could think of this, so could Wan Xiuzi.

How could he believe such nonsense?

Immediately, he laughed coldly, saying mercilessly, “You were thriving in Xinzhou with excellent momentum. For a person with ‘no value for exploitation’ and who is an ‘unimportant outsider,’ you risked danger to come to Luoyang. To then distance the relationship, do you not think you are protesting too much? I still have some sense of what kind of person you are. Since you dared to come alone, you must have thought about how I would deal with you. You’ve personally witnessed the Tianjiao’s methods for dealing with traitors.”

Xie Wei said nothing.

Wan Xiuzi stared at him, his eyes revealing a vicious quality. “Back then, it was I who saved your life, sparing you from dying under Prince Pingnan’s blade. People say that even a drop of kindness should be repaid with a gushing spring. But you! All my careful cultivation over these years has actually raised a great calamity for myself. Repaying kindness with enmity; truly worthy of being Xiao Yuan’s son, carrying on the tradition!”

Jiang Xuening’s heart jumped.

Xie Wei’s face became expressionless. He raised his eyes to look directly at Wan Xiuzi; his hands, tucked in his sleeves, clenched tightly for an instant.

However, he was not someone who could be provoked to anger.

Facing such provocation, he only said, “You saving me was merely wanting to keep a good weiqi piece, to one day make the Imperial clan and the Xiao family look bad. If so, over these many years, working for you in court and passing information to the Tianjiao, I’ve already repaid you cleanly. We came together for mutual benefit from the start, neither owing the other anything. How can you speak of repaying kindness with enmity?”

Wan Xiuzi flew into a great rage, slapping the armrest of his chair with one palm. He suddenly stood up, raising his hand to point at his nose and began cursing, “What a fine ‘neither owing the other’! If you had worked diligently and conscientiously for my Tianjiao all these years, that would be one thing. But do you think that because I do not concern myself with Tianjiao affairs, I am blind? Every underhanded thing you’ve done in secret, which one am I unclear about? Openly for the Tianjiao, secretly for yourself! Ever since going to the capital, when have the northern branch altars ever taken me, this Sect Leader, seriously? Every one of them has become your lackey! In your eyes, is there still me as Sect Leader, me as your adoptive father?!”

Young Xie Ju’an had truly been a dazzling talent.

Throughout the Tianjiao, who could compare with him?

When Wan Xiuzi initially brought this child bearing a blood feud back to Jinling, he had not thought he would have such great abilities. Seeing that he was exceptionally intelligent with meticulous thinking, he thought the Tianjiao had gained great assistance. He bestowed favors everywhere, even letting him assist with Tianjiao affairs, placing him on equal footing with Gongyi Cheng, wanting the other party to therefore obey his every word. How could he expect this person to have great ambitions? On the surface, his conduct was faultless, but secretly, he was wildly ambitious, gradually growing into a massive force, to the point where even he had to be wary of him!

Someone he originally thought he could control and who would serve him faithfully had, in the blink of an eye, become a blade hanging over his own neck. Who could endure such hatred?

Wan Xiuzi hated him to the extreme.

It was just that now, having first lost Gongyi Cheng and then losing Xie Ju’an, Tianjiao’s followers were somewhat scattered in morale. Moreover, raising troops in rebellion was no simple matter. He was old now, and no matter how much he valued health cultivation, he could not recover his former glory, gradually feeling his energy and spirit exhausted.

By comparison, he hated Xie Wei even more to the bone.

These words were spoken with tremendous anger and carried a condescending, stern questioning.

However, those two words, “adoptive father,” fell into Xie Wei’s ears and only stirred up the surging malice in his heart. He even recalled that blood-filled palace, the corpses piled like mountains, that revulsion carved into his every limb and bone surging upward.

He actually laughed.

He coldly reminded him, “Sect Leader has forgotten; over twenty years ago, Xie Wei already abandoned his old name and shed his old surname. Having a mother but no father, and if there is a father, he should be dead. Your adopted son is surnamed Xiao and named Dingfei, currently enjoying wealth and honor in the capital.”

Throughout the Tianjiao, who did not know Young Master Dingfei’s great name?

The followers all felt their hearts pounding thinking of him.

At this, a few acolytes seemed to recall that devil incarnate’s behavior and could not help but shudder, burying their heads lower.

Wan Xiuzi, hearing these words, nearly had a surge of blood rush to his head, feeling dizzy and seeing stars!

That damned Xiao Dingfei! Over these years, his lack of proper learning had caused him much trouble and had led to many problems for the Tianjiao!

He suddenly realized, “That bastard; you deliberately picked him! Good, very good!”

Xie Wei did not deny it, only saying, “I have come as agreed. If the Sect Leader wishes to judge my crimes, do as you will. You’ve also kept Jiang Xuening for several days now. Should you release her now?”

Wan Xiuzi looked toward Jiang Xuening. “Why the rush?”

He laughed coldly and actually raised his hand to signal the nearby acolyte, “Since you’ve come all this way, my Tianjiao is no dragon’s pool or tiger’s den. Please have her stay here for a few days to accompany this poor Daoist in reading scriptures and playing weiqi to relieve boredom!”

The acolytes stepped forward.

Jiang Xuening’s heart filled with great alarm. Though she knew this wretched old Daoist was using her to threaten Xie Ju’an, seeing the acolytes walking toward her still made her hair stand on end. Finally unable to suppress the fire in her heart, she cursed aloud.

Through gritted teeth, she said, “Old demon Daoist, speak plainly! You’ve been standing there talking for so long without ordering anyone to beat the one surnamed Xie. I see it is not him being threatened by you, but you who have something to ask of him! Putting on airs like some great turtle! If you dare let people lay hands on me, this young lady’s temper is not good; if I am not careful and bite my tongue to kill myself, see what you will use as leverage!”

Wan Xiuzi had not expected this girl to expose everything with one statement. His face immediately became covered with a layer of darkness.

The acolytes went to gag her mouth.

Xie Wei’s form finally wavered, but he held back from moving, saying coldly, “Do not touch her!”

These acolytes all served at Wan Xiuzi’s side. The outer followers did not know Xie Wei’s methods, but they were crystal clear about them. Hearing this voice, they nearly froze and shuddered, instinctively stopping and looking toward Wan Xiuzi.

Wan Xiuzi’s eyebrows raised.

He smiled with satisfaction. “Your heart aches for her?”

Xie Wei did not answer but said, “I killed Gongyi Cheng.”

His voice was calm.

To the point where, at first hearing, one would think he was saying something ordinary.

However, when everyone was a beat slow and finally realized what he had actually said, they felt as if a thunderbolt had been thrown down on level ground, stunning them dizzy and dazzled, hardly able to believe what he had said!

Even Wan Xiuzi was stunned for a moment. Immediately after, recalling that battle in Tongzhou from two years ago, his heart continuously emitted cold air, accompanied by a towering rage!

His entire being was about to explode!

Gongyi Cheng had been his right-hand man, utterly loyal to him, and even the key to restraining Xie Wei!

“You actually dare to admit it!”

Wan Xiuzi’s voice was almost squeezed out from between his teeth.

“I knew it, I knew it!”

Xie Wei seemed completely unconcerned about the shock his words caused and continued dropping thunderbolts. “I’ve devoted considerable effort to the Tianjiao, as everyone can see. When Gongyi Cheng came to the capital, he immediately began pointing fingers and did not know his place. You cannot blame me for being ruthless with him. After killing this person, from the capital to Zhili, all Tianjiao branch altars fell into my hands. I only pretended to obey the main altar, but in truth, they listen to no orders but mine. Now that you are raising troops, from south to north, if you have the northern followers cooperating from within, conquering the Imperial City would be but a matter of days. However, unfortunately, I anticipated the Sect Leader would not let this go easily, so I left word that, without my orders, when war breaks out, they should pledge allegiance to the court. With a great battle imminent, even if you want to settle accounts, now is not the time. I believe that with Shen Lang’s methods, he will first incorporate these followers into the military and slowly settle accounts later.”

Wan Xiuzi said, “What scheming! To oppose me, you even borrow the strength of the court and the dog Emperor, completely forgetting your blood feud.”

Xie Wei said, “Though I have ambitions to stand independently, I have not reached the point where I must rely on my enemy’s favor to survive. Originally, I planned to raise troops myself, but now being under someone’s roof, I have no choice but to bow my head. I do not wish to threaten the Sect Leader; I only want to exchange this for the Sect Leader to release Jiang Xuening. Revenge is the most important matter in my heart. Raising troops myself or joining with the Sect Leader in raising troops makes no great difference to me. I ask the Sect Leader to show mercy. Though Dujun lacks talent, I am willing to offer the court’s military deployment maps for nine major fortified cities in Hubei and Anhui provinces to assist our Tianjiao’s uprising.”

As they say, the enemy of my enemy is my friend.

Wan Xiuzi had trusted Xie Wei so much in earlier years precisely because he knew Xie Ju’an’s background and knew how deep the hatred in his heart was. Such a person, abandoned by his own clan and made a weiqi piece by the Imperial family, could by no means possibly stand on the court’s side. And to one day achieve revenge, he would necessarily exhaust his heart and effort for the Tianjiao.

Although he later grew powerful, he had not really done anything to particularly obstruct or weaken the Tianjiao.

Even at this very moment…

Wan Xiuzi had sufficient reason to believe that Xie Wei hated the court to the bone and would use any means to achieve his goals. When unable to raise troops himself, yielding to join the Tianjiao was absolutely not an impossibility.

The Tianjiao’s main forces were all in the south. Though the north had secretly developed followers because Xie Wei entered the court as an official, they were all ultimately grasped in Xie Ju’an’s hands. After Gongyi Cheng’s death, he, the Sect Leader, had even more lost control over the north.

Now, having just raised troops, it seemed like an overwhelming force.

But he knew clearly in his heart that the further north they fought, the harder it would be. Hubei and Anhui provinces were especially hard bones to crack, yet were extremely important to the Tianjiao. Occupying these two provinces meant occupying the lower Yangtze River region. Especially Hubei’s Jiangcheng, the thoroughfare of nine provinces; it truly was a rich prize.

To say he was not tempted would be a lie.

However, if he released Jiang Xuening, he would lose the leverage to threaten Xie Ju’an. Though he still did not know exactly how much space this woman occupied in his heart, under no circumstances could he release her first.

Moreover…

Xie Ju’an had come; that was not beyond Wan Xiuzi’s expectations. But if everything was truly as he anticipated and things developed smoothly, he could not help but be suspicious and distrustful: Without even trying, the border troops at Xinzhou remained inactive—such an excellent situation? Could Xie Ju’an really bear to give it up, actually risking danger alone, just for a woman?

Inside the room, silence reigned.

Wan Xiuzi stared at Xie Wei, apparently considering.

Jiang Xuening had not expected that this person would come to such a dangerous place alone, and word by word, actually had a somewhat guest-taking-precedence-over-host posture. And he actually claimed he wanted to cooperate with the Tianjiao? How could she quite believe this…

Xie Wei also did not rush him, waiting for Wan Xiuzi to consider.

After a long while, Wan Xiuzi finally clapped his hands and laughed, saying, “They all say heroes have trouble passing the beauty barrier. Even you, Xie Ju’an, have a time of flying into a rage for a beauty! Not bad. However, this is a major matter. This seat still needs to consider it. After all, you two are both here, and currently raising troops is going smoothly; there’s no rush. On the contrary, you two…lovers…have finally met, yet you’ve only accompanied this old man in talking for so long. That is really not good.”

Jiang Xuening rolled her eyes internally.

However, Wan Xiuzi suddenly became like a good person. He waved his hands at those around him, signaling everyone to leave. Then he said to Xie Ju’an, “Dujun, this seat will not make things too difficult for you. I will trouble you to rest here with this girl for a while, so you can talk. Wait until tomorrow, and this seat will give you an answer.”

Having finished speaking, he actually walked out with a smile.

Everyone followed and withdrew.

Though his words said he was asking them to stay here and rest for the night, when the last acolyte walked out the door, he showed no mercy whatsoever, directly locking the door. The followers in the corridor also did not leave, obviously guarding against the two of them escaping.

Inside the room, only Xie Ju’an, standing in place, and Jiang Xuening, bound to the pillar, remained.

Only at this moment did Jiang Xuening discover her back was cold with sweat; apparently, while listening to Xie Wei and Wan Xiuzi go back and forth earlier, she had unknowingly broken out in a cold sweat.

Now that people had withdrawn, that tense energy also relaxed.

If she were not still bound by ropes, her entire body would probably have gone soft.

Xie Wei said nothing and walked toward her, reaching out to help untie the ropes.

Jiang Xuening turned her head to gaze at his coldly handsome face. In this instant, she could not describe what she felt. When things quieted down, a deep silence enveloped her, making her eyes sting with tears.

This person actually dared to risk himself for her…

She said, “You really are insane.”

Xie Ju’an, with lowered eyelids, paused for a moment and said, “Did you not know that long ago?”

The rope was tied too tightly. The slightest movement made her wrists hurt.

Jiang Xuening laughed and said, trying to sound casual, “I thought being abducted by the Tianjiao was an opportunity. They’d threaten you, you would not come, keeping me would be useless, and then I’d use some underhanded tricks, feeding that old demon Daoist some intelligence from the capital; maybe a blessing in disguise, I’d escape your control and gain my freedom like that. But you…following me to the ends of the earth, never letting me go.”

At this moment, both were trapped in a cage. She did not want the atmosphere to be too heavy, which was why she said this.

However, Xie Wei did not pick up the conversation at all.

He was untying the rope knot, but could not immediately untie it. So at this moment, he noticed that his fingers working at the rope knot actually had an imperceptible trembling.

After a long while without hearing his response, Jiang Xuening thought this person had gotten angry. However, when she turned her eyes to look at him, her gaze followed downward and saw Xie Wei slowly clenching his hand into a fist.

He just did not say anything.

As usual, not responding, wanting to continue untying the rope.

Jiang Xuening’s eyes wandered. After watching him for a while, she suddenly said, “Xie Ju’an, there’s something I am very curious about.”

Xie Wei glanced at her.

Jiang Xuening coughed, then bit her lip with an expression of wanting to laugh but trying to hold it back. “I saw you were quite skilled that time. Turns out you’ve never slept with a woman; you are still a virgin?”

“…”

At first, Xie Wei did not react.

However, after realizing what Jiang Xuening had actually said, his face almost instantly darkened.

Seeing his expression, Jiang Xuening finally could not hold back and burst out laughing.

Her appearance was exactly like someone who had finally exposed another’s shortcoming, with that kind of unrestrained, swaggering, arrogant attitude; simply detestable!

A vein jumped at Xie Wei’s temple.

He ultimately could not hold back. His thin lips pressed tightly together, he directly kicked her, signaling her to restrain herself and be more obedient.

This kick was actually neither light nor heavy and did not hurt.

However, seeing his expression, which looked like he wanted to kill someone, Jiang Xuening ultimately still did not want to go too far. She suppressed her laughter several times, forcibly restraining it considerably, though the expression on her face still appeared teasing and playful.

Only then did Xie Ju’an lower his head again to untie the rope for her.

However, this time, that slight trembling from before had already disappeared.

He suddenly froze.

Looking at the mottled, crisscrossed marks on Jiang Xuening’s wrists from the bindings, Xie Ju’an recalled her outrageous joke from just now. In this moment, he finally perceived her unspoken thoughtful consideration.

Was Xie Ju’an the kind of person who was clear as a mirror in his heart?

In a flash of thought, he already knew she had deliberately made such a joke to divert attention and ease his emotions.

However, Ning’er, do you know that it is not because of being trapped in danger, but the lingering fear after seeing you safe and sound…?

Xie Wei finally untied the rope binding her.

Jiang Xuening’s hands had almost lost all feeling, sore and numb throughout. Moving them even slightly was painful. In her heart, she could not help but curse Wan Xiuzi’s ancestors back eighteen generations.

However, Xie Wei lowered his voice and said, “Wait for me here.”

Jiang Xuening was startled. “Where do you want to go?”

Xie Wei did not answer. His gaze looked toward the tightly closed window facing north, and his footsteps followed, moving over. He only looked outside through that narrow crack.

Jiang Xuening also became nervous, not daring to make a sound.

Xie Wei seemed to want to push open the window and do something.

However, just as he raised his hand, his gaze wandered, and he frowned again. He turned around and walked back in front of Jiang Xuening. He actually raised his right thumb and touched it to her lips. The warm pad of his finger used some force, as if wanting to leave some mark on them.

Jiang Xuening was first startled, then confused.

The corner of her mouth hurt somewhat from the rubbing.

She could not help but say, “What are you doing?”

The soft lips, once pressed by his fingertip, moved accordingly. Using just his finger, it was not as easy as he thought to leave a mark. Moreover, this momentarily moist sensation suddenly awakened the surging intensity within his heart.

His finger paused at the corner of her lips.

Xie Ju’an, without warning, lowered his head and pressed down with an overwhelming kiss. Sucking and lightly biting, half cherishing, half fierce, after a thorough ravaging, slightly out of breath, he finally released her.

Those originally cherry-pink lips then took on a shade of bright color, even showing slight redness and swelling from his excess.

Jiang Xuening stared at him with wide eyes.

After quite a while, she finally reacted. She raised her hand to touch her lips, anger surging up. But fearing her voice would be too loud and heard by people outside, she asked through gritted teeth in a low voice, “What’s wrong with you?”

Xie Wei pressed his lips together, his earlobes slightly red, yet his words came out seemingly forthright: “Staging a good show.”

Jiang Xuening was completely confused.

Xie Wei, being stared at by her, felt somewhat uncomfortable. He turned and walked toward the window again. As he walked, he asked, “Did Wan Xiuzi tell you about my past?”

Jiang Xuening felt unhappy, thinking him inexplicable.

So she laughed coldly, “He did, quite a lot. Something about cultivation or not cultivating.”

Xie Wei’s fingers, pressed on the windowsill, suddenly paused. He turned back to look at her. “How did you respond to him?”

Jiang Xuening instinctively said, “I did not respond.”

Xie Wei looked at her. “If he tests you again about cultivation matters next time, just say yes.”

Jiang Xuening: ??????????!

CONTENT END 226

chapters.title: Scream
chapters.content:
What on earth was this person trying to do?

Right now, Wan Xiuzi clearly wanted to use her to coerce him, but not only did he not want to distance their relationship, he even wanted her to say next time that the two of them had cultivated together.

Jiang Xuening really could not figure it out.

After Xie Wei finished speaking, he no longer concerned himself with her reaction. He returned his gaze to the window crack, watching for a long while. After thinking briefly, he actually lifted his wide sleeve and untied the thin, short blade that was always bound to his wrist.

Jiang Xuening: “…”

She lowered her head to look at the ball of rope that had just been untied and fallen at her feet, then raised her head to look at the blade Xie Wei was inserting into the window crack. The corner of her eye twitched slightly. “Since you had a knife, why did you not use it when untying the rope earlier?”

Since he had brought a knife, why go through the trouble of untying it? Would it not be better to just cut it open with one slash?

Xie Wei had already gently pushed open the wedge fastened in the window crack. When she asked him this, his form froze for a moment. After a long silence, he replied, “I forgot.”

Jiang Xuening: “…”

How can you forget that? You are really something!

Xie Ju’an had not lied. Earlier, when untying the rope for her, he actually had not thought of anything else. Only after untying the rope, when he wanted to act according to his predetermined plan, did he naturally remember the knife at his wrist.

Throughout the Tianjiao, everyone said he was someone who relied on his brain.

Seeing him enter with nothing on his person, they had not been vigilant when searching him. Moreover, this blade was extremely thin. Bound to his wrist, he only needed to clench his fist forcefully, making the muscles on his arm hard, and no great difference could be felt.

That was why it was so easy to bring it in.

This window was not large. Pushing it open slightly to create a narrow crack, one could see that even behind the building, there were people visible.

However, this room was already in the side courtyard, with the courtyard wall at the northeast corner.

After thinking briefly, Xie Wei said to Jiang Xuening, “I will go out first. No matter what commotion you hear, do not panic. Wait a moment for me to return.”

Jiang Xuening was startled. Before she could answer, he had already silently pushed open the window and flipped out with remarkable swiftness and silence. Immediately after, a sharp cry came from outside, as if someone were shocked and panicked, but before it could be completed, it had already been cut off, stopping abruptly.

Faintly, there was a sound of spraying.

Very quickly, the Tianjiao followers guarding outside had already discovered the abnormality. A loud shout rang out, “He came out! They are escaping!”

Jiang Xuening’s heart immediately began pounding with alarm.

Outside, however, Xie Wei was methodical and orderly. After flipping the blade and killing one person first, he quickly seized the unfortunate follower’s sword, then slashed another cut across that person’s neck, covering up the wound previously made by his thin, short blade.

Someone chased after him.

But these Tianjiao followers knew his identity was different and had some scruples. They only wanted to capture him, not act decisively when they moved. On the contrary, this gave him an opportunity; with one slash each, he cut them down to the ground.

He hid toward the small bamboo grove by the courtyard wall, flicking the blood on his blade over the eastern courtyard wall and leaving a footprint on the wall. However, he himself did not cross over the wall from this spot. Instead, he turned back and climbed over the wall from beneath the tallest locust tree at the northeast corner.

This Tianjiao branch altar was loose on the outside but tight on the inside.

The interior was extremely strictly guarded, but the outside, being the authorities’ territory, they did not dare station too many guards, also fearing exposure.

But this precisely became his opportunity.

“Where is he?!”

“There’s blood on the wall! And footprints!”

“Quick, he must have escaped outside. Chase him toward the north street!”

…

Inside the manor, torches immediately blazed brightly. Everywhere was in chaotic commotion, with followers shouting back and forth, and people quickly running to report to Wan Xiuzi.

At this moment, Xie Wei had already followed the outer northeast corner wall, calmly and unhurriedly circling to beneath the north wall. After walking about twenty steps, he pressed against the wall to listen to the movements inside.

Everything was exactly as he had predicted.

Learning that someone had run away, the inside immediately panicked. Immediately, someone in charge ordered others to take the key and open the door to check the situation, saying, “Only one ran away! That woman is still inside!”

Who could have imagined that Xie Ju’an, coming alone with an air of disregarding life and death, would now abandon Jiang Xuening and escape by himself?

It could be said that no one was prepared.

Some were even completely baffled: If he was going to run, why take such risks in the first place?

But in any case, someone had escaped. If they did not quickly catch and bring him back, when the Sect Leader became enraged and held people accountable, no one could bear the responsibility. Therefore, these people below could not spare time to think further. They quickly mobilized manpower; most went outside the wall to chase, and quite a few followed along the north wall searching. The number of people originally guarding in front of that room in the side courtyard decreased.

Xie Wei listened as those chasing him gradually moved farther away. After calculating briefly, he held his breath and flipped over from the north wall.

This way, he landed right at the front of the building.

Only a few followers remained to guard Jiang Xuening. Moreover, no one took Jiang Xuening inside the room seriously; a man with his strength could run, but a weak, delicate woman, even if you gave her both hands, probably could not escape. Thus, they were somewhat lax and distracted, with two still puzzling over Xie Wei’s sudden escape, when the knife Xie Wei was holding fell on the backs of their necks.

With two thuds, the people had already fallen to the ground.

The person killed first, blood flowing freely, struggled to turn his head and saw it was Xie Wei. His eyes immediately widened in terror. However, how could the blood from the wound be staunched? Without making a single sound, he collapsed to the ground.

The remaining few people were even more directly stunned.

Did they not say he escaped toward the north?

How had he come back!

Those with quick reactions had instantly thought of the feint strategy, deliberately luring the tiger away from the mountain, then turning back for a counterattack to rescue the woman inside the room.

However, it was still too late.

Fighting against them, Xie Wei ultimately had the advantage. The wound at his waist and abdomen had mostly recovered. Though it still imposed some constraints on his movements, he killed people so cleanly and decisively, going straight for vital points. Before they could make too much commotion, he had already ended their lives.

The lock hanging on the door had already been opened earlier.

Xie Wei’s snow-white robes were covered entirely in blood. He directly kicked open the door and strode inside.

Jiang Xuening looked at him in disbelief.

But he could not spare time to explain. He pulled her along and headed outside.

At this moment, the followers who had gone far to chase him had not returned, and the nearby guards had not yet understood the situation. As long as he could take Jiang Xuening and flip over that nearest north wall he had crossed earlier, they would be halfway to escape.

Xie Ju’an’s face was calm, but his feet moved quickly.

However, just as he gripped Jiang Xuening’s hand tightly and stepped one foot out of the courtyard gate, a sharp, gleaming sword tip suddenly appeared, precisely blocking his path. If he took even half a step forward, this sword tip would pierce through his brow!

Jiang Xuening’s palms were covered in sweat. Alarmed, she gasped, and following the sword tip upward with her eyes, she saw clearly that the one holding the sword was a Daoist acolyte with a stern, cold expression. Behind this acolyte, a group of Tianjiao followers had already surrounded the front of the side courtyard, holding torches.

Wan Xiuzi slowly walked over from that end of the crowd.

Xie Wei looked at him.

Wan Xiuzi stopped with his hands behind his back. He swept a glance at Xie Wei, then looked toward Jiang Xuening behind him. His gaze paused on Jiang Xuening’s lips, which bore some slightly ambiguous red marks, then fell on their tightly clasped hands. With an expression somewhere between mockery and pity, he laughed coldly, “I knew it; you, Xie Ju’an, have always had your own ideas. You are definitely not someone who would submit without resistance. I was on guard against you early on. If you had not made a move tonight, I would have been unable to sleep peacefully instead! As for the young married couple’s deep mutual affection, she’s truly placed at the tip of your heart. When disaster strikes, you do not fly your separate ways!”

Hearing this, Jiang Xuening suddenly recalled Xie Wei’s earlier phrase “staging a good show.” Though she did not know what plan he had or what purpose, somehow she seemed to understand a bit.

Her thoughts immediately turned, and she said, “What young married couple?! Old demon Daoist, do not speak nonsense and ruin people’s reputation!”

Though she said this, her gaze appeared guilty and evasive.

Seeing her like this, how could Wan Xiuzi truly believe she and Xie Wei were completely innocent?

The more she dared not admit it, the more suspicious it was.

He knew it in his heart, but could not be bothered to deal with this insignificant little girl. He only looked at Xie Wei and said, “Feint east, strike west; lure the tiger away from the mountain; it is a good plan. Unfortunately, most of your intelligence and strategy were taught by me. Did you think you could deceive me with such small tricks? Do you really take this seat for a senile old fool?”

Xie Wei seemed to know his plan had failed. He gently released his grip and threw the knife he had been holding to the ground, assuming an attitude of submitting to punishment. Yet he said calmly, “If my injury had not healed and my movements were slightly slower than usual, even if you could see through my stratagem, I am afraid you would not have had time to react. By the time you brought people here, I would have long escaped. Strategy is certainly important, but timing also cannot be lacking. It depends entirely on how it is used, when it is used, and who uses it. This time, I was one move behind in the game. However, if I did not make such an attempt, I would not be reconciled in my heart.”

These words were reasonable and logical.

To blink and become a prisoner, yet still had to serve him; how could this be something Xie Wei would do?

He had to try it before giving up; only then could he be obedient.

Hearing this, Wan Xiuzi was not angry. Instead, he laughed heartily, “Now the Tianjiao is flourishing. Having you assist me again would not be wronging you! However, you are also not some easy person to deal with.”

His face suddenly turned cold.

Though he had spoken politely just now, after tonight’s incident, he would not be lax in the slightest. He sternly rebuked those around him, “Someone, come! Confine them in Lingxu Pavilion. Guard them day and night. If even a fly escapes, I will have your heads!”

“Yes!”

The followers had long been frightened into a cold sweat by tonight’s incident. Fortunately, at the critical moment, after hearing about the situation, the Sect Leader immediately saw through Xie Wei’s scheme, preventing the escape.

At this moment, they had already tensed their nerves, fearing blame, and responded in trembling unison.

This time, they had even less goodwill toward Xie Wei and Jiang Xuening.

Very quickly, they were escorted out of the side courtyard and locked in the second floor of a small building at the center of the manor.

Up, down, left, right, front, and back—the guards were impenetrable.

Jiang Xuening was pushed and shoved inside. Looking down from above, she could not help but sigh in her heart: This time, there really was no escape, even with wings!

The room upstairs was not large.

But compared to where she had been held before, it was somewhat more refined.

There was a table, chairs, a bed, a bathing tub, a screen…

The people who escorted them in harshly berated them for a few sentences before closing the door and withdrawing.

The door was once again heavily locked from the outside.

Jiang Xuening did not take that scolding seriously at all. She only glanced at the room’s sole bed and could not help but silently curse Wan Xiuzi’s ancestors back eight generations again.

Xie Wei, however, was very composed.

The failure of that escape plan just now seemed to have no effect on him whatsoever.

He removed the outer robe stained with blood.

This revealed the waist bound tight with leather straps and the straight spine up to the nape of his neck. Compared to when wearing loose outer robes showing elegant detachment, he now displayed a bit more upright coldness.

Jiang Xuening finally had a chance to ask her question, “What exactly are you planning?”

Xie Wei said indifferently, “Wan Xiuzi has a suspicious temperament. If I behaved properly and caused no trouble, he would become suspicious instead.”

Jiang Xuening said, “But having dispelled his doubts, what then?”

Xie Wei glanced at her. “I have my own plan.”

Jiang Xuening: “…”

This person really had not been beaten in his past life, had he?

She took a deep breath and simply did not ask further. In any case, when he needed to use her, Xie Ju’an would not fail to speak up. She only said, “Then…that cultivation thing, why is that?”

Xie Wei lowered his eyelids. Thinking of Wan Xiuzi, he slowly said, “To make him believe you are extraordinarily important to me. However, people are always willing to believe what they already believe, but maintain doubt about things they cannot understand. If one firmly believes that everyone living in this world fears death, how could one believe someone would sacrifice their life to save another? Wan Xiuzi is precisely like this.”

He believed in profit, not righteousness.

He believed in desire, not emotion.

If one wanted to gain someone’s trust, naturally, one should cater to what they believed.

Jiang Xuening finally understood. However, she vaguely felt something was not quite right, but thinking it over carefully, she could not pinpoint what exactly was wrong.

It was already late. After the earlier ordeal, it was even deeper into the night.

There was only one bed in the room.

Jiang Xuening had no choice but to share the bed with Xie Wei.

The two lay flat on the bed, fully clothed, extremely close together, shoulder against shoulder, hand next to hand, heads each resting on one end of the pillow.

Inside the room was pitch black.

Neither moved chaotically nor spoke.

Jiang Xuening could hear Xie Wei’s subtle, steady breathing. For a moment, she actually felt it was very strange: something as intimate as sharing a bed seemed to mean nothing to them. After all, it was not as if they had not slept close together before, just not on a bed like this.

Having faced death twice, with everything said and revealed.

The rapids had returned to deep stillness; the vast sea stirred no waves.

For that brief moment, it even gave one an illusion of plain tranquility stretching far into the distance.

Jiang Xuening had thought that after experiencing such a bloody storm earlier, she would need a long time to calm down before falling asleep. Unexpectedly, after lying down, her heart was completely at peace, as if life and death were not such momentous matters after all.

She fell asleep quickly.

However, while sleeping soundly until midnight, in a daze, she was actually pushed awake by someone.

Jiang Xuening had almost forgotten she was currently imprisoned.

Opening her eyes drowsily, she only saw Xie Wei propping up half his body, sitting at her side, his hand still resting on her shoulder and arm.

Clearly, it was he who had pushed her awake.

She had not slept enough yet. Having just woken, her head was simply a complete muddle. Somewhat annoyed, she complained in a sleepy, dream-like tone, “What are you doing now?”

Xie Wei asked, “Can you scream?”

Jiang Xuening had not reacted yet and instinctively said, “Scream what?”

Xie Wei saw her eyelids heavy, about to close again. His thin lips pressed together. He simply did not bother explaining to her. His hand resting on her thin shoulder moved downward, and at her slender, soft waist, he squeezed with a bit of force.

The waist area was most sensitive.

A sensation, both itchy and painful, came from where Xie Wei squeezed. Jiang Xuening was pinched until she curled up, and a cat-like, delicate moan with a trace of hazy nasal tone overflowed from deep in her throat, lazy and lingering.

His breathing stalled for a moment, hearing it.

But at least now she had opened her eyes again.

Xie Wei glanced toward the tightly locked door, then turned back to gaze at her, repeating once more, “Can you scream?”

If there was still confusion just now, in this instant, Jiang Xuening recalled the sound she involuntarily made when he pinched her, and hearing his meaningful question, she finally became completely and thoroughly frightened awake!

Scream…

What kind of screaming did Xie Ju’an want from her?!

CONTENT END 227

chapters.title: Until the End of Time
chapters.content:
She stared at him, almost dumbstruck.

At this moment, she finally belatedly realized what was not right.

To put on a show in front of Wan Xiuzi, to make people think they had something going on: in the middle of the night, a man and woman alone were locked together, and they were lovers who had “cultivated” together. A brief separation was better than a new marriage. Even though they were in such a dangerous place, they were still lying on the same bed. If nothing happened, could it still be called “having something going on”?

So this act had to be performed convincingly!

That “screaming” was naturally the kind of screaming…

Jiang Xuening lay on the bed, the quilt covering half of her. Thinking of this, her entire body stiffened.

Being stared at by her like this, Xie Wei inevitably felt somewhat uncomfortable. However, in the darkness, it was not very clear to see. Just listening to his voice, one could not detect anything unusual. It seemed as if he had only said something ordinary, still saying in a low voice, “Scream for a while.”

Jiang Xuening felt inexplicably nervous.

She raised both hands to grip the edge of the brocade quilt. Her throat had become somewhat dry, her voice tight. “Do we…do we have to act this realistically? And it is already nearly the second half of the night. Would it not be rather inappropriate…”

Xie Ju’an’s hand still rested on her waist and had not moved away. Hearing this, he only said indifferently, “Be obedient. Do not force me.”

Jiang Xuening immediately cursed in her heart.

When two people were mutually in love, screaming a couple of times during intimate pleasures was nothing much; it was not as if she could not do it. But when nothing was actually happening, yet she still had to scream in front of others—such a shameful thing! She had not done it even in her previous life! Never mind doing it, just thinking about it gave her the impulse to dig a hole and bury herself. Her whole body turned as red as a cooked shrimp.

She sensed Xie Wei’s unyielding attitude. But no matter what, she could not bring herself to do it. She bit her lip slightly, showing some resistance.

Though Xie Wei was calm and self-controlled, he had ultimately lived many years. From the marketplace to the court, even if he had not personally experienced such things, he at least knew the general idea and had heard some things.

Naturally, he knew it would not be easy to get her cooperation.

He gazed at her for a moment, only asking, “Really, you will not scream?”

Hearing this sentence, Jiang Xuening immediately felt something was amiss.

But when she wanted to dodge, it was already too late.

There was only so much space on the bed. Moreover, Xie Ju’an’s hand had been resting on her waist all along. Without even waiting for her to react, that hand used a bit of force again to pinch her.

The waist area was truly both soft and ticklish.

She could not bear his pinching. In rapid succession, she said, “Don’t…do not do that anymore,” with gasps she absolutely could not control mixed in between, broken and intermittent. Wanting to laugh yet wanting to escape, like a fish struggling in his hand, yet unable to avoid it.

After all that commotion, even her forehead was covered in sweat.

Jiang Xuening finally knew what fate awaited those who fell into Xie Wei’s hands and did not obey. Having finally gotten a chance to catch her breath, she hurriedly grabbed that mischievous hand of his. Panting heavily, she yielded. “Fine, fine! I will scream. Is that not enough?”

This voice was truly full of grievance.

Her eyes were moist, pupils containing a trace of hazy mist.

Xie Ju’an only felt that her entire person under his hand seemed to have melted into a pool of water, soft and tender, reminding one of the bright apricot blossoms on tree branches.

Hearing her agreement, he paused for a moment before withdrawing his hand from her waist.

Jiang Xuening had also figured it out.

Xie Ju’an was decisive and resolute. If he said to act, then they would act. Rather than being held down by him on this bed and tormented for ages, ending up half-dead, breathless and weak all over, it would be better to be sensible and scream readily and openly.

However, when it came time to actually open her mouth, there was still some embarrassed awkwardness. She bit her lip and said to him, “Can you turn around?”

Xie Wei glanced at her and turned sideways away.

Only then did Jiang Xuening feel somewhat better. She relaxed her body and let out a vague and ambiguous sound from deep in her throat, as if both uncomfortable yet pleasured, as if floating on water’s surface, already unable to quite bear it.

Xie Wei could not see the scene behind him and could only hear her voice. His body almost instantly tensed up.

Though he clearly knew things were not really like that, if one only listened to this voice and closed their eyes, what emerged in one’s mind would be an entirely different unspeakable scene, making one’s blood surge and heart restless.

Her voice was delicate and soft.

Deliberately pitched somewhat through her nasal cavity, it had an indescribable sultry quality, as if wanting to struggle yet being powerless, wanting to escape yet sinking deeper. The faint gasps vaguely tinged with a crying tone gave even more of a feeling of being bullied. Though naturally arousing pity, it also more deeply stirred a certain unspeakable desire for cruel domination in one’s heart, both wanting to cherish her and also wanting to go deeper, deeper…

His hand, resting on his knee, suddenly clenched tightly.

At first, Jiang Xuening was not quite used to it, but after screaming a few times, she gradually became proficient. It was nothing more than making some sounds to deceive people; naturally, she would make them sound as good as possible. Moreover, she could vary the pitch from time to time, pondering over the emotions and sensations carried in the sounds.

However, inadvertently, from the corner of her eye, she caught a glimpse of Xie Wei.

He was sitting cross-legged with his back to her on the outer side of the bed. His entire back presented a kind of tense straightness. The fingers that should have been loosely resting on his knees were pressed down forcefully, as if enduring something.

Her eyes rolled, and Jiang Xuening suddenly understood.

But in this moment, she actually wanted to laugh.

He was the one who told her to scream. Now he was the one with an appearance of being unable to bear it. If this was not asking for trouble, what was it?

Perhaps it was because this person had teased her earlier, or perhaps she resented him for coming up with such a terrible idea and making her scream here. The bit of mischief in Jiang Xuening’s belly gradually rose to the surface.

Not only did she not restrain herself, but she cried out even more lingeringly.

She even quietly moved closer, right next to the back of his neck, and blew a breath of air. Her voice carried a bit of fake sobbing, “Don’t…don’t…”

Xie Ju’an trembled all over from that breath she blew. Hearing this sound, even the mental state he had been struggling to maintain was thrown into chaos. He instantly turned his head back to stare at her. But he only saw Jiang Xuening looking as if her scheme had succeeded, with a hint of smug satisfaction, laughing behind him.

Even the delicate moans that followed carried a flavor of pleasure.

As if she had found some amusement.

Because she had just been pushed awake from sleep by him earlier, her hair and collar were somewhat disheveled. At this moment, the corners of her eyes and tips of her brows carried a kind of charm that made one’s heart race. Her fragrant lips slightly parted, her breath light as orchids, and her soft neck slender; truly, her alluring beauty was overwhelming, stirring up fires.

How could he not hear that she was doing it on purpose?

Originally, he thought he could control himself, remain calm and self-possessed, and cultivate an unmoved heart.

But at this moment, he truly could not endure it any longer.

Even the corners of Xie Wei’s eyes twitched slightly. Finally, he reached out a hand and pressed her back down onto the bed, covering her trouble-making mouth, saying through somewhat gritted teeth, “Enough! No need to scream anymore!”

But she had not finished yet…

Jiang Xuening blinked, wanting to speak.

However, as soon as her lips moved slightly, they touched Xie Wei’s palm.

He only felt a slight tickle in his palm. For a moment, it was like being burned by a hot iron; he immediately withdrew his hand.

Jiang Xuening’s eyes were clearly black and white as she looked at him. After hesitating a moment, she asked tentatively, “Is that enough already?”

Xie Wei said nothing.

Jiang Xuening naturally knew Xie Wei was a normal man. Anyone who heard a woman beside them screaming like that would probably find it difficult to endure; hearing each sound was a kind of torture. But for some reason, she wanted to laugh a little.

But she did not dare to in front of Xie Wei.

Jiang Xuening bit her lip once, forcibly holding it back. Out of kindness, she asked supplementally, “Screaming for just this short while, will the time not be too short…”

Hearing this, Xie Wei’s face almost instantly darkened like the bottom of a pot!

Having asked this question, Jiang Xuening felt extremely pleased inside. However, at the same time, she also sensed a bit of danger. Deeply aware that if she provoked him further, she would be asking for trouble, she forcibly suppressed a bellyful of laughter and slowly pulled up the quilt, covering even her entire face and whole head.

Then Xie Wei heard muffled laughter.

The lump raised in the quilt beside him seemed unable to suppress itself as it trembled. Faintly, there were even sounds of pounding the bed.

Xie Wei restrained himself again and again, but had never had such an infuriating moment before.

His sagely temper—in the end, she had provoked his anger.

With one hand, he reached in and hauled the person out.

Jiang Xuening, covered in the quilt, had nearly laughed herself to death. Being suddenly caught out, before she could react, lips carrying some warmth had already descended overwhelmingly, entangled with some anger that was difficult to dispel, combined with some turbid desire, completely and entirely blocking up her vexing little mouth.

At first, it was only meant as punishment, to make her also know fear.

However, after just sucking and playing for a couple of moments, the flavor changed. Intense, scorching, burning hot; wanting to possess her, conquer her, and make her entirely his own. Just like how she had moaned and cried out just now, even more excessive than that.

Xie Wei’s kiss gradually took on a forcefulness that could not be refused.

She opened her mouth, wanting to resist.

However, this only allowed him to take advantage and pry open her white teeth. Lips and tongues finally met. All the soft fragrance in her mouth became delicacies for him to savor. The sudden storm thus mixed in some lingering entanglement that was difficult to sever. Even the tip of her tongue went numb, almost becoming his captive. Dazed and confused, her hands and feet also lost strength.

When their lips finally parted, her dark pupils were already full of misty vapors.

In the dim light, their eyes met.

In the silence, it seemed one could hear each other’s violently beating hearts and unsteady breathing.

In this moment, it was as if time stretched until the end of the world.

Xie Ju’an ultimately did not do anything more to her. He only stuffed her entire person into the quilt, wrapped her up, and tossed her to the inner side against the wall. He himself also turned around with his back toward her, saying, “Sleep.”

CONTENT END 228

chapters.title: The Height of Shamelessness
chapters.content:
That night, neither of them slept well.

That Xie Wei could not sleep was nothing unusual.

But Jiang Xuening, wrapped in the quilt and lying facing inward, found that even after quieting down, her emotions were difficult to calm. Perhaps having already slept in the first half of the night, she truly was not tired in the second half. She kept her eyes open until the sky grew dimly bright before finally feeling her eyelids grow heavy, dozing off for a bit.

When she woke in the morning, Xie Wei had already risen early.

From his face, one could not tell that anything had happened last night. He was calm and ordinary with no unusual signs. Even the blood-stained Daoist robe had been changed for a clean one.

The Tianjiao now treated him rather like a guest, sending over everything needed for washing up, all proper and regulated.

If not for the group of people below watching day and night without rest, one might think he was still the Master Dujun of former days, rather than a prisoner as he was now.

Jiang Xuening blinked her eyes.

She naturally knew that, being held hostage by the Tianjiao and having no freedom, she should not be lazy. However, having not slept well in the latter half of the night, she really had no energy and even had some headache and felt weak.

Struggling to sit up, within moments, she collapsed back down again.

Seeing this, Xie Wei inexplicably found the scene somewhat amusing. The person was in the quilt with only a messy head poking out, lacking the spirit from last night when she had teased him. He only asked her, “Awake?”

Jiang Xuening nodded while in the covers.

Then added, “Tired.”

Though only one word, her voice sounded somewhat different from usual, carrying a bit of hoarseness that revealed some decadent laziness. As soon as it came out, even she herself was startled. Immediately realizing something, she clenched her teeth slightly and looked at Xie Ju’an with some annoyance.

Hearing her voice, Xie Wei was also stunned momentarily. But then he looked away, lightly brought his hand to his lips to cover it, and said, “Then continue sleeping?”

Jiang Xuening laughed coldly, “You even need to say that?”

Too lazy to bother with him, she huffily twisted her body and turned her head back around, wrapping herself up like a large caterpillar. Closing her eyes, she paid no attention to the situation outside.

Outside, daylight had already brightened. Through the snow-white, slightly aged window paper, it shone on her. Her waterfall-like black hair was spread beside the pillow. Looking at her, Xie Wei only felt that the flowing time had become slow upon that soft hair.

Clearly, this was a dangerous situation, yet it gave one a feeling of tender warmth.

He stood there for a while before slowly smiling and walking out.

Wan Xiuzi had sent someone to invite him early in the morning.

Throughout the manor, guards were stationed every three steps, every five steps; it was more strictly guarded than last night. All along the way, led by a silent acolyte, every Tianjiao follower he saw cast wary, watchful gazes at him without exception.

They stopped at a waterside pavilion by the lake.

Inside was not only Wan Xiuzi. Besides him and a few attending acolytes, there were also several Branch Altar Masters of varying heights and builds. Some were dressed as Daoists, others merely as ordinary martial artists from the rivers and lakes.

But without exception, none of them looked like easy people to deal with.

Yesterday, Wan Xiuzi said he would give an answer today, which was why he summoned him now. Seeing Xie Wei enter, he set down the teacup he had just raised, saying, “After killing people last night, did you sleep well?”

Xie Wei had always been rigorous and self-disciplined. He was not one of those profligates who indulged early and had been hollowed out by wine and women. Whether in the past studying music by lamplight or reading at night, or later entering court as an official urgently discussing affairs, occasionally going one or two nights without sleep was nothing much. Naturally, nothing could be seen on his face.

Xie Wei did not pay attention to the barbs in Wan Xiuzi’s words.

He only said, “Very well.”

Very well?

Wan Xiuzi was not without ears and eyes.

Last night, when he probed with words, that girl had become angry and embarrassed, rebutting him and claiming she had no relationship with Dujun. Yet sleeping in the same room at night on one bed, she showed no resistance. When people went in this morning to deliver basins and water, though Dujun had already risen, they could not tell whether the two had slept together.
