Xie Wei recalled that back in Tongzhou, when he had Dao Qin and Jianshu search everywhere for the secret correspondence he had written to the Tianjiao under the identity of Dujun but could not find it, only to turn around and find it in Zhang Zhe’s hands; yet he had not used this thing to make an issue of it, only returned it to him.

Now he brought up the matter of Shen Zhiyi again…

The incompatibility between him and Zhang Zhe was something both were well aware of. He would not think this kind of solitary and aloof person, who did not fit in with groups, would form cliques and stand on his side. In fact, when Zhang Zhe returned that secret letter to him, he had harbored killing intent.

Only, at that time, he was, after all, the person in Ning’er’s heart…

Thinking of this, Xie Wei pressed his thin lips even tighter, his face covered with frost. Ultimately, he suppressed all the churning emotions and said, “No need.”

What he feared was not the matter itself.

What he feared was not knowing about this matter.

Watching the sky grow dark and heavy with impending rain, he felt increasingly stifled. He simply flicked his sleeves and left, leaving behind the words, “After he finishes seeing Shen Zhiyi, tell him to leave quickly. Do not let him stay in the city even one moment longer!”

Dao Qin and Jianshu had followed him for many years. Moreover, they’d been handling matters since this morning; how could they not know what he truly feared beneath these words?

With great difficulty, they had sent Second Young Lady Ning away.

If these two people were to meet face-to-face…

The two exchanged glances, understanding without words.

Xie Wei returned to his room. Because his heart was not very settled, he took out a scroll of Daoist scripture to read. After calming down somewhat, he heard the pattering sound outside the window; it had actually started raining.

Autumn leaves drifted, yellow, desolate, and cold.

Only after reading for a while did it wash away that agitation in his heart. At this time, he thought that Ning’er would still need to practice zither when she returned in a bit. So he put down the Daoist scripture in his hand, took down a zither hanging on the wall, untied the zither cover, and carefully tuned the strings.

Yesterday, when he was listening to Ning’er play, one string had loosened slightly. Though the sound it produced differed only by a hair’s breadth if not tuned for one day, and it differed by a hair’s breadth each day, then who knew how far off it would be?

His slender fingers tightened the zither string bit by bit.

Xie Wei thought, since it was raining outside, that little swindler and Wei Liang would not continue busying themselves in the fields and should return early. His fingers stopped, and he instructed Jianshu, “The wind is cool, and the rain is heavy outside. Have the kitchen prepare a bowl of ginger soup to dispel the cold.”

Jianshu went once on this errand.

However, when he returned, his expression was somewhat wrong.

Xie Wei stood beside the zither table, one hand diagonally supporting the zither, having just finished tuning that string from before. He casually plucked it lightly, the trembling sound rippled, and several points of a smile floated at the corners of his lips.

Only, after all, this was a purchased zither, not as satisfying as one he had made himself.

Later, when he had leisure, he should craft one for Ning’er.

Seeing Jianshu return, he casually asked, “Has she returned?”

Jianshu immediately knelt on one knee. “Second Young Lady Ning returned a bit early because of the rain. The carriage was at the city gate and happened to run into Minister Zhang. She…It is all because we subordinates were incompetent in our work!”

He kept his head lowered, not daring to raise it.

He did not even dare to say the exact words.

The arc at the corners of Xie Wei’s lips froze for a moment, then slowly, bit by bit, faded away, like a colored painting placed in water, gradually losing its color, becoming completely calm yet extremely frightening black and white.

He surprisingly did not blame them.

His gaze stopped on that string still lightly trembling. He asked softly, “Ning’er went to find him, did she not?”

Jianshu only felt an unprecedented oppression. “Master…”

As if a sharp pain stabbed straight in, Xie Wei’s fingers resting on the zither body gradually darkened and tightened. In the end, he could not hold back that deeply buried malevolent energy. Eyes lowered, he grabbed that zither and smashed it against the corner of the table.

A crash sounded.

The zither scattered, and the strings broke.

He only stood there silently, expressionlessly watching.

His slender fingers hung at his side, a thread of fresh blood winding and dripping down from the wound cut by the broken wood.

Outside the window was pattering rain and gusting wind.

CONTENT END 238

chapters.title: World-Weariness
chapters.content:
The sky had already darkened, and the ginger soup prepared in advance had already gone cold.

Yet Jiang Xuening still had not returned.

Yan Lin’s side sent someone to invite him to discuss the next course of action. Xie Wei simply lowered his eyelids, picked up a snow-white handkerchief to wipe away the bloodstains on his fingers, and said indifferently, “I will come shortly.”

He set down the handkerchief, had someone clean up the mess in the room, and instructed the back kitchen to keep the ginger soup warm before leaving the room.

The front hall for deliberations happened to pass by Jiang Xuening’s courtyard.

He actually encountered Shen Zhiyi along the way.

This former Imperial princess no longer loved wearing her old palace attire. She wore only a deep red and white wide-sleeved immortal dress. Judging by her direction, she had just come from Jiang Xuening’s courtyard, but seemed not to have seen anyone. Her brows were lightly knitted, her expression not particularly relaxed.

She had a faint scar at the corner of her eye.

That was the injury left on her cheek when the Tianjiao and Prince Pingnan’s faction attacked and broke through the capital over twenty years ago. Back when she was in the palace, she had always cared greatly about a woman’s beauty and charm, to the point where she brooded over this scar. Now, having experienced a thousand-li marriage alliance, frontier wind and sand, and twists and turns as a puppet, she no longer cared about outward appearances. She had not even applied any covering makeup, actually gaining a bit of frankness in facing reality.

Because with some things, turning a blind eye and glossing over peace was merely deceiving oneself, like covering one’s ears while stealing a bell. What should be there would not change because of hypocritical pretense.

In the afternoon, she had seen Zhang Zhe. Her emotions had originally been churning. Though there were many people in this vast residence, she could not think of anyone else she could talk to. So after sitting listlessly for over an hour, she still decided to go find Jiang Xuening.

Unfortunately, she was not there.

After turning around the corridor for just a few steps, Shen Zhiyi looked up and saw Xie Wei. At this moment, both their footsteps oddly stopped. Though the twilight rain around them had not yet ceased, the air suddenly filled with a stagnant atmosphere.

Some things need not be said to others; between them, it was crystal clear.

What armies to rescue the Emperor, what princess’s decree, what respectfully escorting Her Highness back to court…

All of it was false!

Shen Zhiyi had neither issued any decree nor said she wanted to return to court. Everything was merely a large hand behind the scenes, manipulating the overall situation, using her as a puppet pushed onto the stage to find a suitable and proper reason for all the things they wanted to do, allowing everything to continue in an upright and dignified manner.

And the so-called noble princess…

Could not even freely cross that city gate.

Shen Zhiyi felt several points of irony in her heart but ultimately did not show it, only asking first, “Ningning said she was going outside the city this afternoon to find Wei Liang. It is so late now; has she not returned yet?”

She had only recently seen Zhang Zhe.

Xie Wei stood with his hands behind his back and did not answer, but instead asked, “When she should return, she will naturally return. At noon, she had already gone to visit Your Highness. For Your Highness to come looking in the evening, do you want to tell her that Zhang Zhe came to inform her to go see him?”

Having informants among the servants attending her, with her every move reported upward; for Shen Zhiyi, who grew up in the palace, this was truly commonplace, no longer anything unusual.

But when she actually knew that Xie Wei had complete knowledge, she still could not help feeling cold.

Even disgusted.

Her countenance cooled several degrees, but she said, “I merely have some words I want to say to her. Now that Teacher Xie holds power and has already taken most of the realm into his grasp, there’s truly no need to be so wary of me, this puppet about to be discarded. After all, the reason you still dare let her see me is it not precisely because you are certain I would never speak too much in front of her and make things difficult for her?”

Although Jiang Xuening had rushed to the frontier and rescued her, the Xinzhou and Huangzhou armies were truly and genuinely treasonous rebels. For a princess of the Imperial clan to be saved by rebels, her position was already extremely awkward.

If it were only that, it would be one thing.

But the person she truly cared about had intimate connections with the mastermind behind the rebels, threads upon threads.

You Fangying had already passed away.

Shen Zhiyi also knew all this was for her sake. In her heart, even if there were ten thousand difficulties, even if the surface was far from reality, she would absolutely never reveal or complain even half a word to Jiang Xuening.

Only because she was her only friend.

She was unwilling to add any troubles for her or push matters toward an unsolvable abyss.

Regarding this, Xie Wei knew it clearly and did not deny it. He only gazed at Shen Zhiyi, his calm voice without fluctuation carrying a particularly ruthless flavor. “Since you know I am wary, you should not always come looking for her.”

Where was this the Junior Tutor Xie from Fengchen Hall of days past?

Shen Zhiyi almost could not believe he could say such words.

In an instant, anger surged.

She coldly demanded, “Is this your way of liking someone? Have you asked whether she knows and whether she’s willing? Under heaven, there has never been a wall without cracks, never a fire that can be wrapped in paper. She’s forthright and kind-hearted, naturally free in spirit, yet you are hypocritical and cunning, calculating at every step, scheming everywhere, not letting her know anything! What do you take her for? A captive bird you’ve caged?!”

Xie Wei said, “What should she know?”

Shen Zhiyi laughed coldly, “Regarding the Tianjiao, you first captured them and then released them, allowing them to wreak havoc on the world, to devastate living beings! Along the way, how many people have been displaced and suffered in the flames of war! Even if you want to rebel, this realm has always been at the mercy of those in power, but what wrong have the common people done? If you said your abilities were insufficient and you truly could not prevent it, that would be one thing. But you deliberately have the capacity yet do not act, intentionally indulging evil deeds, only to fulfill your personal desires! If you want to destroy the court and seize the realm, you could openly fight your way there, but you need not use such despicable means that treat human lives like grass!”

What deeds he had done, Xie Wei knew himself.

He was unmoved, and regarding the so-called lives and deaths of people under heaven, he was also indifferent, only saying, “So what?”

So what?

Along the way, devastation met the eye everywhere: merchants whose life’s work had been plundered, wives whose husbands had been killed, children without homes…

Voice after voice crying, voice after voice shouting!

Shen Zhiyi traveled with the army, unlike Jiang Xuening and Wei Liang, who always lagged a few days behind. Everything she saw and heard entered her heart, often keeping her awake at night.

At this moment, looking at Xie Wei was like looking at a monster.

What kind of cold-blooded person could say such words?

She blinked, ultimately still calmed down, only saying with extreme clarity, word by word, “Jiang Xuening’s whole heart treats people with sincere devotion. She deserves everyone to forever treat her well, but you are not worthy of her.”

Having said this, she flicked her sleeves and left.

Those words “not worthy of her” were truly rather sharp.

Xie Ju’an lowered his eyelids, equally unwilling to speak more with her, only after walking a few steps out; too many things from the past surfaced, too many, too many, so much so that the malevolent energy originally lingering in his heart became increasingly heavy and difficult to suppress!

At this moment, his footsteps suddenly stopped.

He turned around, his voice seemingly mixed with cold malice, actually saying cruelly, “The weak are prey to the strong. The foolish masses of this world deserve only to be slaughtered! Her Highness the Grand Princess stands beneath a dangerous wall and should speak cautiously. Even if one day I kill everyone under heaven, I’d only blame them for willingly being fodder!”

Having said this, he did not look at Shen Zhiyi even once more, going directly toward the deliberation hall.

Shen Zhiyi watched this person’s back disappear among the layered corridor pillars, only feeling that beneath that calm shell hid a ferocity and madness about to lose control.

A gust of wind blew, and only then did she feel cold all over her body.

She gently opened her palm. The military tally pieced together from two fragments lay quietly in her palm. Looking at it for a long time, she actually felt a kind of absurd sorrow. Closing her eyes, bit by bit, she forcefully clenched her fists, letting them press painfully into her flesh.

Jiang Xuening did not know how she had returned, dazed as if walking through a dream spanning two lifetimes. The shadows of surrounding flowers and trees overlapped as they passed, suddenly seeming to transform into those people she had seen and known across both lifetimes, making her head heavy and feet light, actually unable to distinguish where she was.

Until a hand suddenly grabbed her arm from the side.

Only then did she come to her senses.

The rain had already lessened. Yan Lin was not holding an umbrella.

He wore a fitted outfit. Seeing her lost and dispirited appearance, he could not help but furrow his handsome, sword-like brows. Only a strange emotion was surging in his chest, preventing him from speaking immediately.

Jiang Xuening looked toward him.

His gradually maturing features were covered by the descending night, actually carrying an indescribable heaviness. He should have asked, “Where did you go?” but when the words came out, they became, “Ningning, I had a nightmare last night.”

Jiang Xuening froze.

Yan Lin’s hand still gripped her arm, his deep black eyes gazing at her. “I am a bit afraid. In that dream, I was so bad to you, so very bad…”

Dream…

If she had still been somewhat confused and dazed just moments before, at this moment, she was shocked awake.

A kind of fear left over from her previous life almost instantly seized her heart.

The face of Yan Lin before her actually overlapped for a moment with his expression in her previous life when he gazed deeply at her in her bedchamber. Jiang Xuening’s heart trembled violently, and she almost could not control her instinctive reaction; she broke free from his hand, grasping hers, and stepped back!

Watching this, Yan Lin felt like his heart was cut by a knife.

Before saying these words to Jiang Xuening, he had even been thinking; it was just a dream, just a dream.

But why was she truly so afraid?

The young man’s voice vaguely carried a bit of hoarse choking. “The dream you mentioned, the dream I had; they are all real, are they not?”

He was still this lifetime’s Yan Lin.

When Jiang Xuening looked at him and realized this, she immediately knew her action just now had hurt him, but she had no way to control it.

Could such strange things exist in the world?

Or was it that after hearing what Zhang Zhe described today, she had developed an illusion where past and present lives converged, making it difficult to distinguish truth from falsehood?

No…

She shook her head, actually feeling a splitting headache, unwilling to stand here and say even half a sentence more with Yan Lin.

Only after she walked several steps away did that young man, who had shed his old naivety, still stand in place, as if abandoned.

That guilt then surged forth.

Jiang Xuening thought that they were ultimately not the same person.

Standing frozen for a long time, she finally turned her head and said to him, “It was just a dream. Once you wake up, it all scatters away. Do not take it to heart.”

Yan Lin stood beneath the wall covered with withered yellow vines, watching her walk into the distance.

Her graceful and delicate figure was lit by lantern after lantern.

But falling into his eyes, entering his heart, only desolation remained.

By the time she reached Xie Wei’s courtyard, the rain had stopped.

There were truly too many things weighing on Jiang Xuening’s mind, so much so that she was unwilling to think about what Yan Lin’s words just now actually meant. Even arriving at the courtyard gate and hearing Dao Qin say Xie Wei was still waiting for her, she still carried an unresolvable emptiness.

She walked into the room.

On the table were actually placed exquisite bowls and plates, several dishes prepared, a pot of wine set out, and two wine cups already filled. But the liquid inside no longer swayed; clearly, they had been filled long ago and left for quite some time, so much so that the surface in the cups was smooth as a mirror.

A new zither was placed on the zither table.

The original mess in the room had already been cleaned up. Xie Wei sat at one end of the table. Seeing her walk in, his face showed not the slightest abnormality. He only picked up a cup of wine to hand to her, asking, “What did you chat about with Wei Liang that you came back so late?”

Jiang Xuening and Wei Liang had encountered rain and naturally finished early; only on the road back to the city, she had actually seen Zhang Zhe and chased after him, speaking for a long time before returning.

But she did not want to tell Xie Wei.

Taking the wine cup he handed over, she lowered her eyelids, avoiding his direct gaze, smiling and saying, “I was kept by a farming family who talked for a very long time. I was not paying attention and forgot the hour.”

Xie Wei sat at the table, quietly watching her.

Her state of mind was indeed more chaotic than usual. She did not even think about why Xie Wei had prepared a table of dishes and wine. Once the wine cup was handed to her and she finished speaking, she raised it to drink.

Xie Wei’s gaze fell on her fingers holding the cup.

However, just as the wine cup was about to touch her lips, he suddenly stood up abruptly, snatched it away with one hand, and directly threw it to the ground, where it shattered with a “crack” into pieces!

At that moment, his countenance held an indescribable coldness.

Not knowing whether it was more anger or more hatred, he cursed her without mercy: “Jiang Xuening, are you an idiot?!”

The splattered wine had two drops fall on the silver chopsticks, dyeing them somewhat black.

Only Jiang Xuening did not see it.

She even looked up at him with several points of bewilderment, not reacting.

Rain had fallen in the afternoon and evening. She came back from outside, her crow-black hair ends stained with dampness. When Xie Wei’s hand reached over to grasp her shoulder, his palm was also completely cold.

Thus, that anger burned even more fiercely.

He directly pulled her into the inner room, had someone prepare hot bathing water, and, with a cold face, stripped off all her clothes, penetrated by rain and cold air, throwing her entire person into the bathtub.

Jiang Xuening tumbled in, sitting down, almost entirely submerged by the hot water. Her dampened hair immediately came loose, falling over her fair shoulders, draping across her rising and falling curves.

When her head emerged from the water, water droplets hung on her thick, long lashes.

She only felt this person had suddenly become unreasonable. Just as she was about to open her mouth to ask what was going on, Xie Ju’an had already pressed down on the back of her neck with one hand, his lips covering hers, tightly controlling her. That invasion carried several points of venting desire. Following his tongue, exploring her mouth, he restrained her thoroughly.

He made Jiang Xuening drenched.

But the water droplets clinging to her body also soaked his originally neat outer robe. She whimpered, actually having an illusion of suffocating.

This time was clearly more intense than any previous time.

Yet Xie Wei’s eyes were calmer than at any previous time.

He said, “I want you.”

Jiang Xuening looked at his obsessive, mad appearance. For some reason, she actually felt the heart beating in her chest being cut open by a knife, fresh blood flowing steadily from the wound, making her feel immense desolation, yet she could not say a single word.

It was hard to imagine she would actually feel distressed for this person.

Xie Wei suddenly detested her eyes looking like this. He raised his hand to cover her eyes, then buried his head to kiss deeply the scarlet lips below, finally suppressing her, bit by bit, slowly penetrating deeply.

An almost ultimate pleasure.

But what remained afterward was desolate emptiness, that could not be filled, and fear, along with a kind of self-loathing.

She lay on her side beside him.

Xie Wei was quiet for a while before asking, “Shall we get married?”

Jiang Xuening did not answer.

She bit her lips tightly, one hand pressed against her heart, clenched tight, forcefully suppressing something. Tears had already dampened the pillow; she feared that once she loosened her mouth, she would cry out loud.

Xie Wei waited for her for a long time.

But did not dare ask a second time.

Rising and putting on clothes, the room had toppled wine remaining, and the window had clear moonlight spilling everywhere. What came to mind was actually what Lu Zhaoyin had once jokingly said to him.

Xie Ju’an certainly will not always win, but will never lose.

But what if…

What if this time, no matter what, he wanted to win?

CONTENT END 239

chapters.title: Battle at the Capital
chapters.content:
The next morning, Xie Wei had already vanished without a trace.

The side of the bed was empty.

When Jiang Xuening opened her eyes and sat up, she discovered that her hair, which had been dampened last night, had already been carefully dried by someone. After talking with Wei Liang outside the city for several hours, encountering Zhang Zhe at the city gate, and then coming back to attend to that ancestor, her state of mind had been troubled and oppressed. She had even forgotten how she fell asleep.

This was originally Xie Wei’s room.

Only, presumably, he had given instructions. The two maids, Tang’er and Lian’er, were waiting outside the door to serve, and there was even Jianshu present.

After eating porridge and rice in the morning, Zhou Qihuang came to take her pulse.

She found it strange, “What’s this for?”

Jianshu bowed and said, “When the master left, he instructed that you had come back yesterday after being in the wind. Fearing you might catch a cold, he asked Physician Zhou to come take a look.”

Jiang Xuening then recalled, “Where is your master?”

Jianshu did not even dare look at her more, saying quietly, “There was an urgent report from the front lines before dawn. The master went to the army before daybreak.”

He left before dawn?

How truly “clean and efficient”!

Jiang Xuening was stunned for a moment. Having lived two lifetimes, for the first time, she actually felt like someone had taken advantage of her for free. She was somewhat angry from all directions, nearly rolling her eyes. What she had originally thought was that she would wait until this morning, when she was calmer and had considered things more thoroughly, then discuss with Xie Wei future matters, including marriage; that would be more proper.

Who could have thought this person would run away early in the morning?

She pondered for a long time but truly could not figure out whether she was at a loss or whether Xie Wei was at a loss.

In any case, it was one muddled account she could not understand.

Jiang Xuening laughed in anger and raised her slender fingers to press her temples. As her gaze flowed, she inadvertently noticed Jianshu’s posture of lowered brows and downcast eyes actually seemed like he knew something. Her thoughts thus stirred slightly.

Last night, Xie Wei’s whole person had been strange.

At the time, her head had been empty with no leisure to think much, but now, recalling it, she discovered the clues.

She suddenly asked, “He knows I went to see Minister Zhang last night?”

Jianshu never expected Jiang Xuening would directly ask this. He was nearly scared into breaking out in cold sweat all over his neck. He opened his mouth, not knowing how to answer all at once.

But Jiang Xuening no longer needed him to answer.

Just looking at Jianshu’s flickering gaze and not daring to speak, what did she not understand?

Calling him Xie Ju’an a vinegar jar would be giving him too much credit.

This person was an entire sea of vinegar.

Even without wind, he could stir up waves, making things difficult for himself.

Only when she calmed down to think did she feel she actually seemed to understand him.

Xie Wei was different from her.

Though they had similar experiences, she had never possessed anything from the moment of birth. In the previous life, she yearned to possess things, but when those things truly came into her hands, she discovered they were nothing special. In this life, she did not deliberately chase after things anymore, but whatever she was fortunate enough to possess, she was grateful for. But Xie Wei had originally possessed everything; only a calamity in his youth caused him to lose it all.

Thus, everything became scars.

He lived in this world yet did not have the slightest sense of security, so he would rather never possess anything again. But what about once he possessed something?

A faint sourness rose in the bottom of Jiang Xuening’s heart. After having her pulse taken by Zhou Qihuang, she only instructed Jianshu with one sentence, “When your master returns, inform me. I have something I want to say to him.”

Hearing this, Jianshu’s scalp went numb.

But he did not dare rashly speculate what kind of words this “something to say” referred to. He could only lower his head and acknowledge with a sound.

Ordinarily, for deliberations or going to the army, it was only half a day’s effort.

Jiang Xuening thought she could see Xie Wei in the afternoon.

But unexpectedly, forget about the afternoon; even on the second day, the third day, she had not seen his shadow!

Only upon asking did she learn that in this short span of two or three days, Xie Wei, who originally would arrange to stop and rest for ten days to half a month upon reaching each city, this time had actually acted completely contrary to usual. Together with Yan Lin, he swiftly reorganized military forces, apparently unwilling to delay even one day. At dawn on the third day, he directly sent troops toward Baoding Prefecture, where the Tianjiao currently were!

Upon first hearing this news, Jiang Xuening almost thought Xie Wei had lost his mind.

However, calming down to think…

If the Tianjiao knew of the movements on the Xinzhou army’s side, what should they do? Perhaps stop and clash head-on with the Xinzhou army, but Wan Xiuzi, encountering Xie Wei, had long been like a bird startled by a bow; he probably would not be willing to undertake this certain-death action and let the court profit like the fisherman. Or perhaps, like a wild beast driven by hunters, he would have no choice but to exhaust himself fleeing for his life, sending troops to attack the capital before Xie and Yan could…

Xie Wei was not going mad.

He clearly was too lazy to wait any longer and was forcibly compelling Wan Xiuzi to attack the capital!

On this side, Jiang Xuening had just figured out the thread. On that side, Xie Wei, who had not shown his face for three whole days, finally appeared again.

The carriage had already been prepared.

Yan Lin was at the front lines.

He entered the room and extended his hand toward her. “Let’s go.”

Jiang Xuening was still looking down at the zither score. Seeing him extend his hand toward her, she instinctively first placed her hand in his before asking, “What for?”

Xie Wei gazed at her and pulled her to her feet.

His voice was calm, but the meaning within was earth-shattering. He only said, “Taking you to kill someone.”

CONTENT END 240

chapters.title: Killing Zhou Yinzhi
chapters.content:
When they heard that the Xinzhou Army in Zhending Prefecture had made unusual movements, the Tianjiao’s Righteous Army, which had only rested for a few days in Baoding Prefecture, nearly went insane with fright!

Over these past months, they had almost grown accustomed to the pursuing troops behind them.

After all, the enemy seemed to deliberately calculate something; each time, though they chased and attacked them, they also left them sufficient time to rest and reorganize, not pushing them so hard as to exhaust too much of their combat strength.

So when this news arrived, they simply could not believe it.

What followed immediately was a sense of overwhelming crisis: Could it be that the Xinzhou Army was finally going to get serious with them? Now that they’d reached the capital, did the enemy think they no longer had any use?

Ever since Wan Xiuzi had been released by Xie Wei, both his hands were practically useless. No matter how many famous physicians he consulted, they could not be healed. At his advanced age, still having to fight alongside the army, no amount of health preservation techniques could sustain him.

After several months of this, where was his former vigor?

However, being driven all the way back to the capital reminded him of the glorious momentum when he led troops northward in the past. This ultimately stirred up some of his fighting spirit; even if he were to die, he would die on that supreme dragon throne!

So he immediately gave the order to break camp and march, not caring whether wolves or tigers pursued from behind, attacking the capital with manic fervor!

How could Baoding Prefecture’s city defenses compare with the capital’s?

If he could capture the capital first and hold the city with heavy troops, he might not be unable to keep Xie Wei and Yan Lin’s great army outside the city walls, winning for himself that single thread of survival!

The Sect Leader above was driven mad by obsession, while the sect followers below, because of the pursuing troops about to arrive, surged with an intense will to survive. Knowing they had no other choice, they instead gritted their teeth and displayed astonishing combat power in attacking the capital!

The capital had four main city gates.

The Tianjiao Righteous Army did not divide its forces in the slightest. Upon arriving at the city, they went straight for the southern gate, attacking fiercely and rapidly, clearly willing to take it at any cost in the shortest time possible!

Wan Xiuzi had thought it might take considerable time, but unexpectedly, what he had assumed would be solid city defenses now seemed as fragile as paper, breaking at a single thrust!

So vulnerable they could not withstand a single blow!

The moment the city gate was opened, everyone showed expressions of wild joy, including Wan Xiuzi. A boiling excitement pervaded, and no one even thought to consider whether this victory had come too easily.

If Xie Wei, who was sufficiently familiar with the capital, had been here, he would certainly have spotted the irregularity at a glance: If the court truly intended to defend, with the Tianjiao’s capabilities, even if they could win through numerical superiority, opening the city gate would take at least three days and nights; it absolutely would not be this easy.

In warfare, deception was the way.

The real trap likely was not at the city gate but inside the city!

The rising sun broke through the darkness before dawn, golden-red light spilling across the golden-glazed tiles of the Imperial Palace. The white frost condensed on them quickly melted, reflecting only a dazzling color.

Before the Taiji Hall, an expanse of open space.

Shen Lang, wearing dragon robes, stood barefoot at the very top of the steps, hair hanging loose, his eyes staring unblinkingly at that gradually brightening sun, as if waiting for something.

*

Zhou Yinzhi did not know whether the Emperor’s plan could succeed.

Or rather…

It no longer had much to do with him.

As the newly appointed Commander of the Nine Gates, he had not been assigned to ambush the Tianjiao inside the city, but rather to defend the eastern gate. The troops he commanded numbered less than ten thousand, with few real experts from the army. If anyone chose to break through the city from here and struck ruthlessly, they could practically annihilate his entire force!

Beside him, a young soldier’s hand trembled as he gripped his spear.

Zhou Yinzhi, however, picked up a water pouch filled with strong liquor and tilted his head back to take a drink, as if also trying to dispel the icy cold that invaded his body along with the autumn chill.

No one knew that he had secretly sent three letters of surrender to the Xinzhou Army.

But they had all sunk like stones into the sea, without response.

Ever since discovering Yao-niang’s disappearance, he knew that misfortune would sooner or later descend upon him.

But he had not expected it to come so quickly.

A lifetime of restless striving, always calculating, climbing upward to become one of those above others; yet as he changed masters one by one, it was only lowering his head to one after another.

Half a lifetime of scheming, ultimately the wrong choice!

News came from the southern gate that it had been breached.

The entire army felt a collective dread.

Zhou Yinzhi’s gaze, however, remained fixed ahead. Finally, two quarters of an hour later, a scout’s swift horse galloped back from the front, shouting in panic, “They are coming, they are coming! The Xinzhou Army is also here!”

The young soldier immediately asked, “My…My Lord, what should we do?”

Zhou Yinzhi said, “Why panic?”

He grabbed the Embroidered Spring Blade resting on the gate tower and fastened it at his waist. His cold, stern face showed no emotion as he actually turned and walked toward the city below, merely saying, “Yan Shizi and Minister-Tutor Xie lead a loyal army that serves the sovereign. They’ve come pursuing the Tianjiao rebels; what’s there to worry about?”

Those around him exchanged glances.

Zhou Yinzhi descended from the gate tower and raised his arms in a shout, calling loudly, “Open the city gates!”

The defending soldiers knew in their hearts how many troops guarded the eastern gate.

Who in this world did not fear death?

If they had not yet heard the news that the Tianjiao had already attacked through the southern gate, they might still have hesitated, wondering whether to stake their lives on a desperate fight. But now that the southern gate was breached and Zhou Yinzhi, as commander, had given such an order, that bit of hesitation was forcibly dispelled.

They were only following orders and would not bear responsibility.

So the soldiers on both sides finally pulled the city gates open with force!

Rolling dust and smoke approached from ahead.

The three armies arranged their formations below the city.

Zhou Yinzhi did not know whether this gamble of his was right or wrong, but in the end, he had no other choice. When he saw that carriage arrive before the city gate from afar, he closed his eyes briefly, then actually planted his blade on the ground and declared in a clear voice, “This official, Zhou Yinzhi, respectfully welcomes the Minister-Tutor and the Shizi back to the capital to serve the sovereign!”

Xie Wei lightly lifted the carriage curtain. Hearing his voice, a trace of a smile appeared at the corner of his lips. He first stepped down from the carriage but did not immediately acknowledge him, only extending a hand back into the carriage.

Jiang Xuening had not heard this voice in a very long time.

The scene of You Fangying falling in a pool of blood that day suddenly flashed through her mind again. She took Xie Wei’s hand and also stepped down from the carriage.

When Zhou Yinzhi saw Xie Wei descend from the carriage, he felt it was within expectations. However, when he saw that Xie Wei did not respond to him but instead extended a hand into the carriage, his heart suddenly sank. Immediately after, when he witnessed his former master Jiang Xuening emerge from the carriage with Xie Wei’s support, a chill that had previously been dispelled by the strong liquor suddenly returned to his heart, making him feel as if he’d fallen into an ice cellar!

Dao Qin and Jianshu stood at attention to the side.

Xie Wei did not speak.

Jiang Xuening looked at him, came before him, then glanced at the wide-open city gate behind him and suddenly laughed, “Worthy of Lord Zhou indeed; able to bend and stretch, able to risk your life for the Emperor, and also able to sell the Emperor for your life!”

Zhou Yinzhi had thought that people in this world ultimately unite for profit.

As long as he still had use value, he would not be immediately discarded.

When the time came, he would first submit to Xie Wei and Yan Lin. Even if he had to suffer some hardship, it did not matter; as long as he could preserve his life, there would always be opportunities to maneuver and scheme afterward. But with a thousand calculations, how could he have calculated that at this critical moment of two armies facing each other, Xie Wei would actually bring Jiang Xuening along!

What this meant, he understood all too clearly.

His fingers hanging at his side were clenched tightly from intense unwillingness. In this instant, too much flashed through Zhou Yinzhi’s mind.

However, the more desperate the situation, the more one would want to struggle before death.

A strange glint passed through his eyes. He raised his head to look at Jiang Xuening, putting on an appearance of remorse, and said, “The matter at Xinzhou: this official harmed Young Lady You. But at that time, this official’s wife and children were all in the capital, and every interest, large and small, was controlled by the court. I truly had no other choice! Today, with the young lady and the Minister-Tutor returning to the capital, this official reflects on past errors with deep regret. Therefore, I opened this city gate, hoping to make some small amends, only asking that the young lady, in consideration of past ties…”

At this point, his words suddenly turned fierce!

The Embroidered Spring Blade that had been planted on the ground shot directly from its scabbard. Where was even half a trace of remorse left on Zhou Yinzhi’s face? He actually took advantage of Jiang Xuening standing closest to him, using the pretense of speaking in repentance to relax her guard, and struck at her with his blade, attempting to take her hostage in this desperate situation to exchange for a way out for himself!

However, Dao Qin’s blade was faster than his!

“Clang!”

In a flash, with a sharp ringing sound, Dao Qin, his face cold without a trace of a smile, was clearly standing even farther from Jiang Xuening, yet he managed to block Zhou Yinzhi’s blade heavily before it reached her neck!

His wrist turned again, taking advantage of the momentum to slash downward.

The sharp blade tip instantly tore a long, bloody gash on Zhou Yinzhi’s arm!

On the other side, Jianshu took the opportunity to strike Zhou Yinzhi’s leg with his sword sheath, then kicked out with such force that it accurately shattered his kneecap, causing Zhou Yinzhi to immediately lose his footing and fall heavily to his knees!

His blade flew from his hand!

Zhou Yinzhi could hardly believe that these two, who had been standing on either side, could have such quick reactions, as if they had anticipated he would strike and had been guarding against him all along!

Dao Qin had witnessed him attack You Fangying, such that despite his exceptional martial arts, he could only watch helplessly as that living young woman met her tragic end.

Because when he arrived, You Fangying had already been taken hostage.

But now, face-to-face, with Zhou Yinzhi’s meager skills, to try to attack Jiang Xuening before him was simply a fool’s dream!

Seeing Zhou Yinzhi’s expression of shock and fury, of disbelief, Dao Qin only said coldly, “Earlier on the road here, Young Lady Ning already warned us, saying your nature is hard to change. If you knew you could not escape death, you certainly would not submit quietly but would take desperate risks. Now, it has proven true indeed.”

Zhou Yinzhi never would have expected this.

Recalling his entire life, Jiang Xuening did count as one of his former masters, but altogether, he had only handled a few matters for her. Their actual interactions were truly not many. How could she understand his conduct so thoroughly?

And moreover…

He clenched his teeth, glaring at her fixedly, his voice seeming to drip blood as it emerged from his throat, “Young lady promised! That letter! You clearly pledged that as long as I was willing to be an inside agent and help, you would not hold the past against me, would spare my life, and would also let Yao-niang and the child in her belly go!”

Jiang Xuening looked at him with pity. “So you actually believed it?”

In this instant, Zhou Yinzhi’s face turned ashen.

But Jiang Xuening only raised her head to look at the already wide-open city gate, thinking how absurd people were, and said slowly, “But yes, a person like me in Lord Zhou’s eyes must seem kind and easily deceived, so when such a person turns bad and deceives others, it is all the less believable.”

She thought the hour was not early anymore; best not to delay the great army behind from entering the city.

So she extended her hand toward Jianshu at the side.

Jianshu passed the sword to her.

She had almost never held a blade or sword. That sharp, long sword drawn from its sheath seemed to press the weight of a person’s life onto the blade edge, heavily pulling down her wrist. When light struck it, cold radiance shot in all directions!

Zhou Yinzhi tried to struggle.

But soldiers on both sides had already come forward to pin him down firmly.

Jiang Xuening held the sword with some difficulty.

Xie Wei then stepped forward, his palm covering hers, helping her grip the sword tightly, only directing it toward Zhou Yinzhi’s neck, and smiled lightly. “I will teach you.”

The blade edge instantly pierced through the skin.

Zhou Yinzhi’s eyes had already turned red.

As death approached, he felt only an intense unwillingness, loudly roaring like a cornered beast making its last stand, “So what if I killed You Fangying? This was an Imperial command! You raise armies in rebellion, engage in power schemes and plots, and even have souls dead by your blades; in what way are you better than me, Zhou Yinzhi?! What right do you have to kill me!”

Jiang Xuening had never killed anyone before.

She was almost being guided by Xie Wei’s hand to thrust this sword forward.

However, the instant this questioning arose, a fierce anger suddenly grew within her!

Her originally trembling fingers actually gripped the sword tightly and forcefully pushed it toward his throat!

Blood immediately spurted out, even gushing from Zhou Yinzhi’s mouth.

He opened his mouth wide, wanting to say something, but his pierced windpipe could only emit blurred hissing sounds; he could not say anything!

He could only stare with wide eyes!

Jiang Xuening yanked the sword out abruptly. Her eyes had already turned red as she said each word coldly, “I once said that if you commit evil, do not let me know. Many in this world engage in power schemes and plots, but you are the lowest of them all! Not a single one of your methods is presentable. You do not even count as an ambitious hero; you only deserve to be a petty villain worse than an ant! No one wanted to kill you; you brought this death upon yourself.”

Zhou Yinzhi finally remembered that many years ago, she had indeed said such words…

But it was already too late.

As blood flowed more, the people pinning him from behind released him. He fell face down to the ground, tears actually welling up in his eyes. He struggled desperately to reach his hand toward Jiang Xuening, opening his mouth, trying to say something, “Yao…Yao…”

Jiang Xuening heard that he wanted to ask about Yao-niang.

But there was not a trace of mercy in her heart. Exceptionally cold, she only looked down at him once from her superior position, did not acknowledge him, threw down the sword, and walked past him.

For a person, the most painful way to die was to not know the safety of the one you cared about until you breathed your last!

Whatever You Fangying suffered that day, she would have him experience it in full today!

CONTENT END 241

chapters.title: Return of the Departed Soul
chapters.content:
At the wide-open city gate, Zhou Yinzhi’s body, which had gradually stopped bleeding, lay collapsed in the road. Amidst the swirling yellow dust clouds, it faintly opened a bloody curtain.

Yan Lin waved his hand, and the great army entered the city.

As Jiang Xuening walked from outside the city gate to inside, those familiar streets appeared before her eyes once again. From her previous life to this one, they remained vaguely the same. But there was not a single shop that was open; either doors were tightly shut, or buildings were broken down and desolate. Where was the prosperous scene of this former dynastic capital?

Long ago, it was on this very long street that Yan Lin, full of high spirits, had galloped with her through the lantern festival on horseback; where You Fangying, clumsy and awkward, wanting to look at a pouch, had knocked over someone’s stall; where when Shen Zhiyi went to marry into the Tatar lands, that procession that seemed joyful but was truly sorrowful had wound its way through the city; where Xie Ju’an had still been biding his time, walking from his residence with hands behind his back to the Youhuang Pavilion to find Lu Xian for a zither string or some good wood…

Everything began here, and would ultimately end here.

She had thought that killing Zhou Yinzhi and avenging herself would feel very satisfying.

But it did not seem to be the case.

Standing on this long street, watching those rows upon rows of soldiers marching forward, what arose in Jiang Xuening’s heart was actually a sense of emptiness, as if she suddenly did not know what to do next or where to go.

Xie Wei stood right beside her, accompanying her as they watched, but he did not say a word.

Jiang Xuening suddenly asked him, “What about you?”

Xie Wei turned back. “What?”

Jiang Xuening said, “After you’ve finished avenging yourself, what will you do?”

Xie Wei looked at her for a long time without answering.

Over twenty years of heavy obsession, the blood feud of an overturned life story; if it were avenged one day, would he feel gratification?

Or perhaps, like that feeling that came over her so suddenly…

Jiang Xuening truly could not fathom it.

Deep autumn leaves were swept by the wind and scattered across the corners of the long street. The sound of marching footsteps extended all the way to the end of the street. Scouts rode swift horses ahead to gather intelligence, while at the other end, Lu Xian frowned as he spoke with Yan Lin about something. From the far end of the long street, a young monk in blue robes came running hurriedly, only to be stopped by soldiers along the way. He struggled to explain something until he suddenly spotted Xie Wei at the other end, then pointed with his hand, his eyes brightening…

Xie Wei suddenly felt a moment of disorientation.

He said to Dao Qin beside him, “Let him come over.”

Dao Qin complied, walked over, spoke to the soldiers there, and brought the young monk over.

Jiang Xuening watched with some curiosity.

The young monk was clearly somewhat fearful of Xie Wei, but when he reached him, he still very politely pressed his palms together and bowed his head before saying, “Some days ago, a patron surnamed Meng came seeking refuge, covered in blood. After the abbot inquired, he said to inform Benefactor Xie. Hearing that the Xinzhou Army has entered the city, he specially sent this young monk to report.”

Xie Wei knew who he was referring to. He only lowered his eyes slightly and said, “Thank you for your trouble.”

Jiang Xuening looked at this monk with much confusion.

But Xie Wei suddenly turned to her and asked, “Have you been to Baita Temple?”

Jiang Xuening’s heart suddenly trembled.

She had heard the name Baita Temple before, but had never been there.

The words caught in her throat, too bitter to emerge.

But Xie Wei took her hand and smiled. “There’s an old acquaintance there whom you also know. I need to make a trip. Will you come with me?”

Jiang Xuening could not say words of refusal.

So Xie Wei pulled her onto the horse, directly circling her in his embrace, and they rode away. They passed through several streets and soon saw from afar a white pagoda built tall.

The desolate city was filled with bleakness everywhere.

The ground had originally been covered with fallen leaves, with no one to sweep them. In the marketplace, not a single common citizen could be seen. Even if some people had not left the city, at this time they all kept their house doors tightly shut, hiding from calamity.

However, the road ahead was actually clean and tidy.

On the ancient stone slabs covered with moss, fresh marks left by broom strokes remained, without a single fallen leaf. At the end stood an ancient and secluded temple. The maple leaves in the temple had long since turned red, and in this deep autumn season, there was a bit of brilliant splendor like rosy clouds.

Xie Wei reined in his horse here.

He extended his hand to Jiang Xuening again, helping her dismount.

In front of the temple gate, a young monk was just coming out carrying a water basin, sprinkling water on the ground that had just been swept. He seemed not to have expected anyone would come to worship Buddha at this time. When he first saw the two of them, his eyes revealed some surprise.

However, when he saw Xie Wei, his eyes instantly widened.

Xie Wei knew the monk had recognized him, but he did not waste words, only asking, “Where is Abbot Wangchen?”

The young monk began to stammer. After standing there for a long while, he quickly set down the water basin in his hands at the corner of the nearby wall and said, “The abbot is meditating in the meditation room. This young monk will go inform him right away!”

Having said this, he ran inside very quickly.

Xie Wei did not mind him and only led Jiang Xuening together into the temple.

Under the wall grew quite a few bodhi trees.

The abbot’s meditation room was further back, an ordinary, simple, small structure.

When they reached the front, Xie Wei said to her, “Wait here for me a moment.”

Jiang Xuening nodded.

Xie Wei walked straight inside. His figure was, in the blink of an eye, blocked by the door panel. From within the meditation room with its yellowed paper windows came the sound of a Buddhist chant, followed by calm conversational voices.

Everyone knew that although Xie Wei was in court, he both read Daoist scriptures and understood Buddhist teachings, which was why he could get along well with scholars and also match wits with the former National Preceptor, Monk Yuanji.

However, this was the first time she had seen him truly have any connection with a temple.

A patron surnamed Meng, whom she also knew…

Was it Meng Yang?

Thinking about it, Jiang Xuening found that she did not seem particularly curious about this. She only raised her eyes to survey her surroundings and then saw that stone pavilion not far ahead.

At that moment, she clearly had not seen the name of this stone pavilion, yet mysteriously, there was a strange sensation that made her heart suddenly jolt. So she lifted her feet and walked toward it.

When she drew near, she could see it clearly.

It truly was the Chaoyin Pavilion.

Seven stone steps raised the pavilion higher. Inside was placed an old wooden table with an incense burner resting on it. It seemed incense had been burned just this morning. Though there was no wafting incense smoke now, one could vaguely smell from the empty air the faint scent of agarwood that had already dissipated.

Beside this stone pavilion was a vast forest of stone steles.

Each one was six feet tall and one foot wide.

Names upon names were carved on them.

Further back, some did not even have names.

One could see they had stood here for a very long time. The edge of each bore traces of wind and rain erosion, even covered with dust and grime.

Jiang Xuening slowly walked among them to look. Zhao, Qian, Sun, and Li—all surnames were present. Some had full given names and surnames, completely intact. Some, however, seemed to not yet have formal names, with only a childhood name carved on the stele. Further back, there were quite a few without any names at all…

The tomb of three hundred righteous children.

In her previous life, she had never seen it, because it had seemed after all to be something unrelated to her. If it had not been for later hearing You Fangying mention it when under house arrest in Kunning Palace, she might never have known that the ultimate upheaval of her previous life’s fate was actually tied to this bloody event from over twenty years ago.

Today, she finally saw it.

She did not look quickly. Each time she saw a name, she would pause for a moment, as if wanting them to leave some trace in her memory.

However, when she walked to the corner in the southeast, Jiang Xuening suddenly stopped for a very long time and did not continue forward.

Before her eyes was also a stone stele.

But it was especially different from those around it.

On other steles, either clear names and surnames were carved, or there were no characters at all. But on this one, a name and surname had originally been carved, but it seemed not to have been completed before being forcibly scraped away by someone, leaving only a few mottled indentations and several chaotic carved marks.

A voice suddenly sounded from behind her, “This one is me.”

Jiang Xuening turned around.

Xie Wei had at some point already emerged from the meditation room. In the distance, by the steps below the Chaoyin Pavilion, stood an old monk, with Meng Yang standing beside him with a pale face, but they only watched and did not come over.

At first, Jiang Xuening did not understand what Xie Wei meant.

But he came to her side.

The dust accumulated on the dark stone stele was gently brushed away by his extended hand.

Xie Wei looked at her and smiled. “Originally, a name and surname were to be carved here as well, but she refused to believe, no matter what, that that pile of withered bones and filth after the snow melted was me. When the craftsman was carving the name on it, she snatched away the carving knife and destroyed the name carved on it. Then she told others that her child might not necessarily be dead, and even if misfortune had already befallen him and he was to be buried in the earth, he should no longer bear the surname Xiao.”

These were clearly words spoken with a smile.

But for some reason, as Jiang Xuening listened, her eyes grew hot with moisture, and she felt a choking sensation in her throat.

But Xie Wei said quietly, “I was originally someone who should have died over twenty years ago.”

Jiang Xuening reached out to grasp his hand and shook her head at him. “No, you are not.”

Her palm was sweaty and even trembling.

So Xie Wei smiled. “What are you afraid of?”

Jiang Xuening could not tell him. She only said, “No matter what, she hoped you would live.”

Xie Wei’s Adam’s apple moved slightly. For a long time, he said nothing, his fingers hanging at his side clenched tightly. In the end, he did not respond to her words, only saying, “Do not come here alone in the future. It is time to go.”

He pulled her toward the exit.

As they passed beneath the Chaoyin Pavilion, Meng Yang glanced at them, while Abbot Wangchen pressed his palms together and recited a Buddhist chant to them: “Amitabha, all dharmas are empty of characteristics!”

Jiang Xuening had no Buddhist enlightenment and could not understand.

Xie Wei did not respond.

He led Jiang Xuening out of Baita Temple again. Outside the gate, Yan Lin led a mass of soldiers waiting quietly. Lu Xian stood at the bottom of the steps. Seeing them emerge, he first glanced at Jiang Xuening, then walked forward.

Xie Wei stopped.

Lu Xian came up and said something to him in a low voice.

Xie Wei seemed rather unconcerned. “Let her come. No need to stop her.”

Lu Xian gazed at him for a long time and asked, “Do you truly still want to win?”

Xie Wei said, “I do.”

So Lu Xian said, “But if what you want changes, your winning will be losing to others.”

Xie Wei said flatly, “I will not lose.”

He did not speak further with Lu Xian.

During the time he was in Baita Temple, Yan Lin and the others had already led troops to investigate the situation in the city. After the Tianjiao’s righteous army entered the city, they had clearly encountered a long-premeditated ambush. Throughout the western and southern districts of the city, there was flowing blood everywhere, spreading all the way along Chang’an Street to the Forbidden City.

Fallen by the roadside were some from the Tianjiao, some from the court.

There were even those who were wounded but had not yet died.

When the Xinzhou Army passed by along the blood-stained road, they cried out and pleaded, “Save us, save us…”

Most people who saw this felt sympathy in their hearts.

However, when Xie Wei’s gaze swept over them, it only stirred up memories of the past. He did not linger long and continued all the way with Yan Lin and the others straight toward that excessively quiet Forbidden City ahead.

The palace gates had long been broken through by the Tianjiao.

Corpses that had not yet been collected could be seen everywhere.

The originally brilliant golden Taiji Hall had now been covered with a layer of blood red.

Wan Xiuzi surveyed his surroundings, almost unable to believe it.

Following at his side were now only a few thousand remnant soldiers, each with bloodshot eyes and wounds on their bodies. Even on his own waist and abdomen, a feathered arrow that had not yet been removed protruded. Only the arrow shaft had been broken off; the arrowhead remained in his body, but he temporarily did not dare extract it.

The situation before the great hall was hardly any better.

Several thousand elite troops were arrayed before the hall, guarding the Emperor in their midst. But with Shen Lang’s disheveled hair and bare feet, how could he still look like the ruler of a nation?

He laughed in a neurotic manner.

All the civil and military officials of the court, those who had not defected to the enemy and had not fled, who remained loyal to their sovereign, now all sat paralyzed in the great hall, trembling with fear, looking with lingering dread at the Tianjiao righteous army that had pressed forward to stand before the hall and now faced them in confrontation.

Prince Linzi Shen Jie, Dingguo Duke Xiao Yuan, Minister of Justice Gu Chunfang, Vice Minister of Revenue Jiang Boyou, and even Xiao Dingfei were mixed among them…

Only Zhang Zhe was nowhere to be seen.

Xiao Shu, who had already attained the rank of Imperial Noble Consort, stood at this moment in a corner, watching the laughing Shen Lang, feeling only an icy coldness throughout her body and utter bleakness in her heart.

If judging only by cunning, Shen Lang was undoubtedly a qualified Emperor.

He had actually deliberately withdrawn troops from the city gates and instead had people lie in ambush at the narrow passages of the marketplace. When the Tianjiao thought they had achieved victory, he dealt them a devastating head-on blow, truly catching the enemy completely off guard.

Fighting all the way, they had actually won miserably by a narrow margin!

Though now people had fought their way into the Imperial Palace, he showed not a trace of panic and even had an indescribable sense of satisfaction, making people suspect: Did this Emperor still have other cards up his sleeve?

Wan Xiuzi’s gaze looked toward him darkly. For a moment, he actually could not quite make up his mind.

Regardless of what came after, that dragon throne sat there at the heights of the Taiji Hall.

Over twenty years ago, he had been only one step away from this position. It was only a pity that Prince Pingnan had been entangled in Imperial family grudges, insisting on exterminating the Shen bloodline completely, ultimately leading to the arrival of reinforcements and falling short at the last moment!

Over twenty years later, he once again stood beneath this dragon throne!

Before the Taiji Hall, the sunlight blazed intensely. Over ten thousand people on both sides faced each other in confrontation, yet among the formations, only the sound of the wind howling past could be heard. Not a single person dared to make the slightest sound.

So the sounds from afar became clear.

It was the orderly footsteps of many people, striking one by one on the solid stone-paved ground of the Imperial Palace, gradually drawing nearer, as if each step trod upon people’s hearts, controlling the beating of their hearts!

Both the Tianjiao and the court sides showed a commotion.

Shen Lang and Wan Xiuzi both looked toward the palace gate.

When they saw from afar the raised banner of the Xinzhou Army, the remnant soldiers on the Tianjiao side only felt a wave of panic, while among the officials on the court side, a small portion almost immediately became energized, even with a flavor of weeping tears of joy!

“It’s Minister-Tutor Xie and Yan Shizi’s Xinzhou Army!”

“They’ve finally arrived!”

“An army serving the sovereign! Heaven aids our dynasty! These Tianjiao rebels will certainly meet their end here today!”

…

However, in contrast, Shen Lang’s face suddenly turned ashen.

Wan Xiuzi even seemed to have heard the greatest joke in the world. He raised his hand, pointing at these foolish incompetents, and laughed loudly, “Rescue troops, you still think rescue troops have arrived! Hahaha…”

Xie Wei, in his snow-white Daoist robes unstained by dust, slowly approached in the fiercely blowing wind.

Almost everyone’s gaze turned toward him.

Jiang Xuening, at his side, looking at this scene of tragic confrontation before her eyes, felt the entire world turn pale and experienced a strange, dizzying sensation.

The great army in overwhelming force, black and dense like tidewater, arrayed itself before the Taiji Hall, almost surrounding everyone.

Those people in court, hearing Wan Xiuzi’s great laughter, became noisy with confusion.

Wan Xiuzi only thought himself already pitiful and tragic, yet he had never imagined that in this world there were people even more tragic and pitiful than himself. He laughed even more wildly, actually raising his hand to point at Xie Wei and loudly shouting, “He’s served as an official in court for seven or eight years! Right under your noses! Yet you actually did not recognize him! This is hardly the Prince’s Junior Tutor who devoted himself wholeheartedly to your court; this is clearly a demon who at any moment will demand your lives and make you repay your blood debt!”

Xiao Dingfei, hidden in the crowd, sighed softly, thinking to himself: “My days of swindling food and drink were finally coming to an end…”

Xie Wei walked up the steps without speaking.

Dingguo Duke Xiao Yuan looked at him, then at Wan Xiuzi, suddenly thinking of something. An indescribable terror suddenly spread through his heart!

Immediately after, that ominous premonition was confirmed.

Under the anxious and uneasy gazes of everyone, Wan Xiuzi’s voice, carrying boundless malice and even a bit of smugness, rang out before this vast Taiji Hall, yet it carried an extremely sinister flavor: “If we go back over twenty years, at that time and place, he was not called Xie Ju’an; he should be called Xiao Dingfei!”

Many people in court and country immediately heard a “buzz” in their heads.

But Xie Wei only stood still, looking at everyone with extraordinary calm, and said indifferently, “With such liveliness, it seems I’ve arrived a bit late.”

CONTENT END 242

chapters.title: Slaughtering All Blood Relations
chapters.content:
What did Wan Xiuzi’s words mean?

Many people did not understand at first.

How could Xie Wei be Xiao Dingfei?

The Shizi Dingfei, who survived that great calamity, was standing properly in the corner right now, was he not? If Xie Wei was actually Xiao Dingfei, then who was this Xiao Dingfei? And how could he have known so clearly about those events from back then?

It was clearly a simple sentence, yet in an instant, it scrambled their minds.

Over twenty years ago, when the Tianjiao rebel faction colluded with Prince Pingnan’s rebels to attack the capital, the story of that precociously intelligent Shizi Dingfei sacrificing himself to save his master by substitution had already spread through every street and alley over these years.

But who had ever considered the truth within?

After all, everyone in this world had been taught since childhood to be loyal to the sovereign and serve the nation. Not a single person would think about whether having one child die in place of another child was reasonable, whether it was justified, or even whether it was actually true.

They were accustomed to it.

A sovereign was a sovereign, a subject was a subject. A sovereign could demand a subject’s death, and a subject should die for the sovereign!

A person’s status, high or low, was determined by heaven.

For common people to climb even a single step upward, they needed those lofty nobles to look favorably upon them, either by becoming someone’s slave or someone’s subject, selling their talents, selling their lives, or selling everything they could, all just to obtain a bit of leftover scraps casually bestowed by those in power!

People throughout the world lacked sufficient awareness.

So today, Xie Wei stood here.

Those who did not know the truth from back then felt bewildered and uneasy.

Those who did know the truth from back then instantly turned deathly pale!

In their eyes, at this very moment, Xie Wei standing before the Taiji Hall was hardly a living person at all, but clearly a ghost revived from the grave, staring at them with that gaze from the netherworld!

“No, how is this possible…”

Dingguo Duke Xiao Yuan had already been injured in the earlier battle with the Tianjiao and could not move easily. At this moment, he looked at Xie Wei as if looking at a monster. His wide eyes were clearly filled with terror, yet, as if telling others or telling himself, he began shouting aloud.

“No! Absolutely impossible! Not alike at all, not alike at all…”

Shen Lang’s pupils also suddenly contracted. That the Xinzhou Army of Xie Wei and Yan Lin would arrive first had already greatly exceeded his expectations, not to mention the thunderbolt from clear skies that Wan Xiuzi had suddenly dropped!

Xie Ju’an, Xiao Dingfei…

Even though he had already anticipated today’s chaos and thought he could remain composed, he was still struck by this sudden news, such that his mind went blank for an instant. Immediately after, his heart felt as if it had sunk into an abyss, icy cold throughout!

Because after hearing Wan Xiuzi’s words, Xie Wei just stood there without the slightest intention of refuting them!

Xiao Shu’s gaze fell on Xie Wei and also on Jiang Xuening, not far from his side, before turning with some confusion toward Xiao Dingfei.

This “Shizi Dingfei,” who had been idle and accomplishing nothing since “returning to the capital,” seemed to also notice her attention. At this moment, he actually threw her an especially bright smile.

Heaven knew what kind of mess he’d made of the Xiao clan these past two years!

Chaos and cacophony, not a single day of peace!

The already not particularly good reputation of the entire great Xiao clan had, under his debasement, fallen even further. People in the marketplace cursed them universally!

However, at this moment, he stepped forward with a beaming smile, pretending to be refined and elegant as he bowed to everyone, saying sheepishly, “I am truly sorry. Actually, I really am also called Xiao Dingfei now. It is just that, well, many years ago, when I met Teacher, he did not want this name anymore and gave it to me. I figure you actually did not find the wrong person. However, these past two years, I’ve eaten your food, drunk your drink, enjoyed your entertainment, and spent quite a bit of your silver. I really am very embarrassed!”

Xiao Yuan nearly vomited blood from anger upon hearing this!

The young Xiao Ye was even more dumbstruck.

Xiao Shu’s refined face turned alternately pale and flushed, ugly to the extreme!

All the civil and military officials of the court were shocked.

This Xiao Dingfei was actually a fake!

This Shizi Dingfei then sauntered over to Xie Wei’s presence, grinning. “How about it? This young master has not disgraced this name, has he? Said I’d teach these bastards a lesson, and I taught them a lesson. Too bad you were not in the capital these past two years; you missed so many great performances! But even without an audience, this young master was conscientious and diligent and performed wonderfully!”

Xie Wei smiled faintly. “You have not disgraced it.”

The corner of Jiang Xuening’s mouth twitched slightly.

But Xiao Dingfei had long since noticed her. With a beauty before him whom he had not seen in a long while, truly stunning, he got carried away and forgot himself. His pair of frivolous peach blossom eyes could not help but wink at Jiang Xuening.

However, before Jiang Xuening could react, Xie Wei had already looked at him flatly.

Xiao Dingfei immediately felt a shiver run through his entire body.

He quickly retracted his gaze, straightened his posture, and obediently retreated to the side, not stopping until he reached Lu Xian.

Lu Xian was speechless.

Seeing this scene, who among those present still did not understand?

Xiao Yuan, recalling the grievances he’d suffered these past two years, could not help trembling with anger. He raised his hand, pointing at Xie Wei and rebuking, “So all of this was calculated by you! Even this human trash bastard was deliberately arranged by you! You, you…!”

Xiao Dingfei rolled his eyes at him.

For an instant, he wanted to say, “Who the hell are you cursing?” but, catching a glimpse of Xie Wei from the corner of his eye, he reluctantly swallowed back his belly full of profanity and only cursed the eighteen generations of the Xiao clan’s ancestors in his heart.

But Xie Wei appeared calmer than anyone.

He walked forward.

With each step forward he took, the arrayed soldiers below the Taiji Hall would suppress their fear and cautiously retreat one step backward.

Xiao Yuan’s gaze was fixed on him.

Xie Wei examined this person. There was actually no excess emotion stirring in his heart; he even smiled and said, “Indeed, not alike at all, is it?”

Everyone’s gaze fell on his face.

Without question, this former Imperial Preceptor possessed an incomparably handsome appearance, with the reclusive air of a mountain hermit and the transcendent quality of an immortal banished from heaven. If paired with such an extremely faint trace of a smile, who in the world would not feel goodwill toward him?

He truly was not alike at all.

On the contrary, that imposter who had already shrunk to the side actually resembled Xiao Yuan by three or four parts in features; simply incredible!

But who said a son must look like his father, or a daughter must look like her mother?

In an instant, Xiao Yuan’s face became like dead wood!

Xie Wei looked at him and said, “I do not resemble her, and I do not resemble you either. So I am neither kind like her nor worthless like you. As things stand now, it is actually just right.”

Not kind, then vicious.

Not worthless, then terrifying.

Everyone who heard these words felt a chill run down their spines!

Seeing such a scene, Wan Xiuzi laughed heartily from behind, clapping his hands. “Wonderful! Absolutely wonderful!”

Back then, why had he not killed Xie Wei?

Was it not precisely for a scene like today?

To take revenge on the court, to scheme against the Imperial family, and to tear off the hypocritical mask of this so-called Imperial clan before everyone’s eyes, letting the world know just how much filth these people concealed within and whether they were worthy of ruling the world!

Unfortunately, Xie Wei was not an easily manipulated puppet.

His plan ultimately could not be fully completed, but now being able to witness half of it already brought him immense satisfaction!

Xie Wei did not want to acknowledge the mad Wan Xiuzi behind him, letting him live a bit longer for now. He only said, “The sage says the debt of giving life should be repaid.”

A glimmer of hope suddenly surged in Xiao Yuan’s eyes.

He immediately said, “Yes, yes! Back then, when Empress Dowager pushed you out to substitute for His Majesty, that was also a method of last resort! She is your aunt; how could she not care for you? Our Xiao clan, and even the Imperial family, are all your blood relatives!”

When he spoke, he was not careful enough. Just those two words “pushed out” in that one sentence had already allowed the surrounding officials to easily realize the truth lurking behind this, and their expressions suddenly changed!

Even Shen Lang’s face turned completely dark.

Xiao Shu looked toward Xie Wei, but unlike Xiao Yuan, she did not sense the slightest trace of mercy from this person’s face. On the contrary, only an ominous premonition crept into her heart!

At this moment, hearing Xiao Yuan’s words, Xie Wei actually laughed and even echoed, “Well said. All blood relatives; some consideration should be shown.”

Xiao Yuan nearly wept tears of joy.

However, Xie Wei looked down at him condescendingly and added in a light and breezy manner, “What kind of death would you prefer?”

What kind of death would you prefer?

With these words, that illusion of being reasonable from before was almost immediately shattered!

Not to mention the court officials; even the soldiers from the Tianjiao and Xinzhou Army behind him could not help but shiver coldly, chilled by the certain killing intent contained in those light and breezy words!

Xiao Yuan froze.

What followed immediately was the terror of approaching death.

He was closest to Xie Wei and could easily see that in his eyes was such an indifference, they held not a trace of emotion, making him felt a coldness from the depths of his heart, as if the souls of those three hundred righteous children buried in the snow back then were all attached to his body, and, moreover, there was a pair of eyes looking down at him through the void!

“No, no, do not kill me…”

Xiao Yuan had never been any kind of strong-willed person. Upon realizing that Xie Wei truly intended to kill him, he could not help but retreat backward.

He wanted to flee.

But the steps before the Taiji Hall had never seemed so long. The distance that could normally be covered in just a short while now seemed endless, no matter how long he walked.

Xie Wei did not have anyone pursue him. He only extended his hand backward.

Dao Qin took down the bow and arrows he carried and placed them in his hands.

Xie Wei looked at that panicked, stumbling figure, took the bow and arrow, then drew the bow and nocked an arrow. The arrowhead of the carved feather arrow glinted with a dim, cold light, aimed from afar at Xiao Yuan’s retreating back. He only said, “On such a fine day as today, how can the Empress Dowager not be present? Jianshu, take people to find her.”

Whoosh!

His fingers gently released, and the bowstring violently trembled!

The carved feather arrow flew from the string!

Xiao Yuan’s figure, hurrying down the steps, suddenly shuddered. An arrow, just like that, shot into his back. His body swayed, but he did not immediately fall.

What followed was the second arrow, the third arrow!

The first arrow only pierced his back, the second arrow had already shot through his heart, and the third arrow directly penetrated his skull!

The blood-stained arrowhead drilled out from between his brows.

Xiao Yuan, whose hair had already turned gray, still had the terror in his eyes before it could dissipate when he gradually lost all expression. With a “thud,” his entire body pitched forward face-down. Blood gushed from his front, staining the white marble steps red.

Patricide!

Everyone in court and country was shocked speechless.

Shen Lang, standing among the crowd, was even more blazing with fury.

However, what made him even more uneasy was not Xiao Yuan’s death, but rather what Xie Ju’an had said to those few people beside him when he released that arrow!

Xiao Shu never would have expected that Xie Wei would dare to act so brazenly in public!

Xiao Ye stood stunned for a long while. He had a straightforward temperament that was not good at concealment, and his eyes immediately turned red. He charged straight at Xie Wei. “You killed my father; I will fight you to the death!”

However, Xie Wei only glanced at him.

He did not even need to act himself.

Dao Qin had his blade in hand. Before Xiao Ye could even get close to Xie Wei, he had already stabbed the blade directly into his chest, then withdrew it without changing expression.

Xiao Shu’s face turned pale with shock as she cried out, “Little brother!”

Xiao Ye looked down.

A bloody hole had opened in his chest. Blood almost instantly stained half his body red. He touched it with his hand, still showing some confusion in his eyes, then retreated two steps just like that and fell to the ground.

His young eyes remained wide open, never to close again.

Before the entire Taiji Hall, there was almost a deathly silence!

Dao Qin and Jianshu, besides Xie Wei, had been seen by quite a few people in court and country. On ordinary days, they ran errands and handled some trivial matters. Everyone had thought they were merely two attendants with some martial arts skills.

Dao Qin spoke little and had higher martial skills.

Jianshu was smooth and worldly-wise.

But who could have imagined that now, acting without a word, they would be so cruelly efficient, not even blinking an eye before taking a person’s life!

And this person should also have been Xie Wei’s brother…
