When everyone now looked at Xie Wei, what echoed in their minds was only that sentence from earlier when Wan Xiuzi had been at the height of madness: This was hardly any sage or Imperial Preceptor; this was clearly a demon demanding lives and blood debts!

Two people from the Xiao clan had died in succession, yet for Xie Wei, it seemed to have no effect whatsoever.

He only looked toward Shen Lang.

As if sensing his unease and fear, after shooting Xiao Yuan dead with three arrows and watching Dao Qin kill Xiao Ye, he appeared perfectly ordinary, turned back, and said to him indifferently, “Do not be anxious.”

Do not be anxious; your turn will come soon.

And truly, everyone did not have to wait long.

From the direction of the rear palace, before long came terrified shouts, “Who are you, people? What do you want to do? How could you know the location of the secret chamber?! Release this dowager, release this dowager!”

Empress Dowager Xiao was dragged over.

Her phoenix hairpin had toppled askew, her hair bun was disheveled, and on her face, which had already shown some signs of age, there was nothing but terror.

She had originally been hiding in that secret chamber in the Imperial Palace that only the Imperial family knew about, attempting, as twenty-some years ago, to conceal herself within and survive the calamity, waiting for the rebellion to be quelled.

But who would have thought?

Just moments ago, the stone door had opened, and a group of people she completely did not recognize had actually walked in, treating her with no respect whatsoever, like a criminal, dragging her all the way here!

Jianshu threw the person before the Taiji Hall and bowed to Xie Wei. “Teacher, the person has been brought.”

Only then did Empress Dowager Xiao see Xie Wei. “Xie Wei?”

Confusion still remained in her heart, but when she turned her eyes and saw Xiao Ye’s blood-covered corpse, she cried out in fright. When she instinctively sought Xiao Yuan, she discovered there was no sign of him among the officials.

The originally lofty Dingguo Duke was now inferior to even a corpse in the wilderness, collapsed at the bottom of those long steps.

Empress Dowager Xiao searched for a long time before she saw him.

Her gaze swept past Shen Lang, looked toward Wan Xiuzi, and then toward Xie Wei. She finally realized an unprecedented danger and shrieked, “Someone come, protect His Majesty, protect His Majesty!”

Over these years, Xie Wei had, after all, been an outer minister.

He had not seen the Empress Dowager many times, but this face was always branded in the depths of his memory, not a trace forgotten.

However, in the blink of an eye, twenty-three years had passed.

Things changed, stars shifted, people and events transformed.

Now, he was the one holding the blade, and they were the prisoners.

Xie Wei did not look at her. He only returned the bow in his hand to Dao Qin, then took a blade instead, and actually gazed at Shen Lang, saying, “While the person you are waiting for has not arrived yet, choose now.”

Hearing these words, even the corner of Shen Lang’s eye twitched.

But Xie Wei acted as if he had not said anything that penetrated heavenly secrets.

He tossed that blade before Shen Lang and Empress Dowager Xiao, his voice light and gentle like clouds drifting across the sky. “You personally kill her, or she personally kills you. Or perhaps I will help you choose…”

Back then, the Imperial family had forced him to make a choice between substituting for Shen Lang and protecting Yan Min. Today, he threw the same choice before this most noble mother-and-son pair in the world!

All the civil and military officials of the court were already too terrified to speak a word.

What a ruthless heart Xie Ju’an had; he was actually going to forcibly stage a tragic human ethics case of mother and son killing each other right here in the Forbidden City!

CONTENT END 243

chapters.title: Kill All Who Bear the Surname
chapters.content:
Since ancient times, the Central Plains have governed the world with “filial piety.” For him to commit patricide and kill his own relatives was one thing, but now, in such a time of crisis, he was actually forcing the Imperial mother and son to kill each other! The ethical principles and moral order of the world were completely trampled beneath his feet!

Some conservative officials were already flushed red with anger.

Voices of rebuke were endless.

However, Xie Wei remained unmoved, as if he had not heard a thing.

He had always done what he wanted to do, without needing to explain to anyone and completely without needing others to understand the reasons behind it.

Even if everyone saw him as a demon.

Watching him from afar in the crowd, Jiang Xuening actually felt a faint aching pain in her heart.

Xie Wei looked at them and only gently urged, “Is it difficult to choose?”

Those who did not know the details from back then called him deranged and mad. However, those who had some understanding or some speculation vaguely realized that behind this action of his, the secrets from back then must be hidden!

Had there been such a choice placed before Xie Wei over twenty years ago?

No one could confirm it.

Ever since being dragged here, Empress Dowager Xiao had suffered one shock after another.

Hearing these words now, she finally reacted.

She clearly did not think Xie Wei resembled Xiao Yuan or Yan Min from back then very much. However, thinking of the location of the secret chamber that should not have been known by others, and this familiar impossible choice before her eyes, that terrible conjecture in her mind that she originally had not dared believe, surfaced.

Empress Dowager Xiao’s eyes nearly split with rage.

As if seeing an evil ghost, she trembled as she pointed at him, her voice tearing and ferocious. “It’s you! So it is you!!!”

However, her emotions were truly too agitated. Almost all her attention was focused on Xie Wei, so much so that she did not see at all that, less than five steps away from her, the disheveled Shen Lang, with a sinister gaze, had already picked up that blade Xie Wei had thrown on the ground earlier.

A trace of mocking pity flashed through Xie Wei’s eyes.

Xiao Shu, from behind, let out a cry of alarm.

That blade was tightly gripped by one hand and easily pierced through Empress Dowager Xiao’s body, penetrating from her back to her chest. When she lowered her head to look, she could even see on that blood-stained blade surface the reflection of her own face bearing some confusion.

The court officials who had been continuously berating suddenly seemed to have been slapped across the face. All words came to an abrupt halt without another sound!

In the Taiji Hall, only the sound of the blade slowly withdrawing from a body could be heard.

Empress Dowager Xiao staggered two steps.

The blood from her chest and back could not be stanched at all, flowing outward like a spring. She finally turned around and saw clearly what was behind her.

What a familiar face it was!

It was the legitimate eldest son she had personally raised, for whom she had fought against many favored consorts in the palace, for whom she had forced the then not-yet-seven-year-old Shizi Dingfei to substitute for him and go to his death, and for whom she had even agreed to send her own daughter far away to marry into the Tatars…

“Lang’er…”

Empress Dowager Xiao saw him holding the blade, standing there silently, yet she did not dare to believe what had just happened. However, the pain in her body was so clear and obvious that she could not comfort herself that this was only a nightmare.

A moment of reluctance flashed through Shen Lang’s eyes, but in an instant, it became that kind of coldness and ruthlessness unique to Emperors. All people under heaven were nothing but grass and trees in his eyes!

Even if this was his birth mother!

He held the blade and said sternly, “The nation is in peril; I must impose upon Mother this once. However, the matter from back then truly had nothing to do with this son. It was Mother who acted on her own authority, forcibly using the Yan family’s lives as a threat to compel the still-young Shizi Dingfei to take my place! I did not understand worldly affairs back then, but over these years, whenever I recall it, I toss and turn, constantly reflecting on my faults! Now that he has returned, it should be time for Mother to repent and realize her wrongs!”

Xie Wei himself had not mentioned it, but with Shen Lang and several others speaking one after another, they successively revealed seventy to eighty percent of what happened back then.

The court officials could already deduce from this the truth from over twenty years ago.

There had never been any loyal service to save the sovereign. Back then, the young Shizi Dingfei had not gone willingly but rather, for the safety of the Yan family, had been coerced by Empress Dowager Xiao to substitute and go to his death in the rebel army!

However, these words were all a fog to Shen Jie as he listened.

He had no idea what Shen Lang was talking about.

When he witnessed Shen Lang’s blade pierce through Empress Dowager Xiao’s body, his head had already “buzzed,” and he was almost unable to believe what was happening.

Shen Jie had always known that he and his Imperial Brother and his mother were not the same kind of people. But he had thought that blood kinship ties meant that no matter what, they would not commit fratricide!

Even when Xie Wei had just spoken those words, he did not believe what he said would actually happen.

But now…

He only felt that the Imperial Brother standing before him had become a bloodthirsty beast. For a moment, it actually stirred up the little courage in his chest. He stepped forward and pushed him away. “What are you doing?!”

Empress Dowager Xiao was already on her last breath.

Shen Lang’s high-sounding words simply made her feel tremendous irony!

Shen Jie half-knelt and gathered her into his arms, calling again and again, “Mother, Mother!”

Two lines of tears fell from Empress Dowager Xiao’s eyes.

At the moment of death, she actually laughed out loud miserably, not knowing whether she was laughing at this absurd heaven, or at the so-called affection of the Imperial family, or at her own pitiful and tragic self. “Hahaha, retribution, retribution; no one can escape it! No one can escape.”

That voice, at its most shrill and high-pitched, suddenly stopped.

Warm blood from her throat gushed from her mouth. She struggled feebly twice before finally collapsing limply.

Shen Jie cried out, “Mother, Mother.”

But he was only a weak person.

He had neither the courage to question his Imperial Brother, who had killed their mother, nor the courage to take revenge on Xie Wei, who was the instigator. He could only hold Empress Dowager Xiao’s corpse and weep bitterly.

Who could have imagined that in less than half a moment, Shen Lang had already made his choice!

The court officials only felt their hearts palpitating with fear.

Even the Tianjiao righteous army, which had killed its way here, found it unbearable to watch.

Wan Xiuzi stood stunned for a long while, but then immediately clapped his hands and laughed loudly. Not even minding the wound on his abdomen, he raised his hand, pointing at the pool of blood spreading before the Taiji Hall, saying excitedly, “Did you see? Imperial nobility! This is the Imperial nobility sitting high in the Forbidden City! Even marketplace rats might not commit such inhuman atrocities! Imperial nobility? Bah! More like worse than pigs and dogs! Hahaha…”

As he spoke, he actually spat on the ground.

His contemptuous attitude overflowed beyond words.

Only Xie Wei sighed softly, as if with some regret, “She died too easily…”

After the silence, quite a bit of discussion arose.

Almost everyone’s gaze fell on Shen Lang’s face.

He still held the blood-stained blade in his hand and could roughly guess what everyone was discussing about him. However, the temperament of this former Imperial Preceptor had already been displayed thoroughly just now!

If he did not make a choice, two people would die!

Since that was the case, he might as well give Empress Dowager Xiao a quick end first.

Shen Lang looked toward Xie Wei. “As for the matter from back then, you know it was all Mother acting on her own authority. You were originally my study companion, yet over these years, I actually did not know you. Why did you need to hide it from me? If you had informed me earlier, I would certainly have issued an edict of self-reproach to the world and sought justice for you.”

Truly, the manner of one who acted as an Emperor.

Xie Wei looked at him. A trace of a smile appeared at the corner of his lips, but he actually did not answer. He only raised his hand and pointed, “What about her?”

Wherever his hand pointed, everyone’s hearts filled with terror.

But in the end, most people experienced only a false alarm.

That slender finger ultimately pointed toward Xiao Shu in her splendid palace attire, but with a deathly pale face at the rear!

On the ground already lay her father, her younger brother, her aunt…

Now, it was finally her turn!

At this moment, without saying another word, everyone already understood: Xie Wei clearly intended to completely exterminate the Xiao clan, leaving no room for mercy! All who bore this surname would be killed!

Xiao Shu was different from Empress Dowager Xiao. Empress Dowager Xiao was the Emperor’s birth mother, but she was merely the Emperor’s favored consort.

To Shen Lang, she was only a tool for venting desires and scheming.

She knew that if Xie Wei wanted her to die today, she absolutely would not live past tomorrow…

But all she had done in this life was to avoid being manipulated by others.

Why was it that, climbing up step by step in pursuit, what she gained in exchange was not even control over her own life?

As Shen Lang walked toward her step by step, holding the blade, tears filled Xiao Shu’s eyes. She raised her head, but neither looked at Shen Lang nor at Xie Wei. Instead, at this moment, she looked toward Jiang Xuening, gazing at her from afar!

That sense of absurdity from being toyed with by fate had never been so intense.

The first nineteen years of her brief life had been almost perfect, and she had not even committed any major errors. However, all the changes stemmed from being a study companion at Yangzhi Study. She had been wary of Jiang Xuening and framed her in connection with the jade ruyi case, but failed and, from then on, formed a deep enmity.

Now, she was Xie Wei’s beloved, while she had become the Emperor’s favored consort; however, she was worse than even a prisoner!

One wrong step, and every step after was wrong.

That was all there was to it.

When the blade pierced through her body, Xiao Shu felt endless cold. But she finally withdrew her gaze and looked at this heartless Emperor before her. In the end, she no longer had her former docility and spoke almost like a curse, “Do you think you can escape?”

Shen Lang had not cared about this woman’s life or death to begin with.

Hearing that she actually uttered such malicious words, malevolent energy surged in his heart. He actually pulled out the blade and slashed another cut across her throat, making her unable to make another sound, and she fell.

By now, the most important people of the Xiao clan had almost all died cleanly.

Jiang Xuening remembered that in the previous life, it had also been like this. Though not the same manner of death, the outcome seemed not much different.

She had fought with Xiao Shu for so many years.

But actually, neither had prevailed over the other.

Xiao Shu had died first under the rebels’ blade, and the entire Xiao clan had been slaughtered by Xie Wei. Not long after, in her lingering existence, she too had taken her own life in Kunning Palace…

Only in this life, she had given up striving relentlessly, while Xiao Shu had walked a path even more twisted than in the previous life…

Watching Xiao Shu fall, she could not say what she felt in her heart.

She only felt it did not seem wrong either.

Karmic retribution; in the end, it would spare no one.

At this moment, standing before everyone’s eyes was not just Xie Wei as a demon, but the one who more closely resembled a demon was clearly that Emperor who had originally sat high on the golden throne!

Shen Lang said, “I can give the order to raze the Xiao clan completely, without mercy!”

Xie Wei only smiled with his hands behind his back. “No need to be so duplicitous with me. Let’s see whether the person you are waiting for arrives. The time is almost here, is it not?”

Shen Lang had already felt that he knew something. Now hearing him state it so clearly, his heart was already three parts panicked.

Killing Empress Dowager Xiao, killing Xiao Shu—he did not feel anything about these.

As long as Xie Wei did not immediately act against him, there might still be a chance to turn the tables. So he swallowed his humiliation and shame and, conversely, spoke many words trying to win over Xie Wei. But who would have thought Xie Wei also knew his intentions!

At this moment, Shen Lang almost thought the other would immediately act against him.

But it was also at this moment…

The sound that everyone had heard when the Xinzhou Army arrived earlier rang out once again from the distance of the palace grounds, approaching from the Shunzhen Gate in the northeast corner all the way toward the Taiji Hall.

There were no banners, and their origin could not be discerned.

Soldier after soldier wore only black armor. The army was well-disciplined and advanced very quickly. Just those visible numbered over ten thousand, not knowing how many more remained outside the palace, unable to enter together!

And at the center of this army, surrounded by troops, was clearly a woman.

Deep purple palace attire was worn on her body, but her face bore no powder or rouge. The scar at the corner of her eye was almost the first thing everyone noticed, along with her face.

Jiang Xuening suddenly froze.

She called out, “Your Highness!”

However, just as she was about to step forward to meet her, a hand forcefully pulled her back from the side.

Jiang Xuening turned around; it was actually Yan Lin.

He would not let her go forward. A few traces of dark radiance flowed through his eyes as he asked in a low voice, “Do you still remember what I told you before?”

CONTENT END 244

chapters.title: Leave Him An Intact Corpse
chapters.content:
Before?

There were truly too many things Yan Lin had said to her before. Jiang Xuening could not recall which particular sentence it was, so she could only look at him with confusion.

But Yan Lin only smiled and said no more.

Just with this delay, and this army that no one had ever seen before had already arrived near. They easily formed a confrontational stance with the Xinzhou Army. If one were to compare military strength, they might not actually be inferior!

Lu Xian’s eyelid twitched as he looked toward Xie Wei.

Xie Wei only watched without making a sound.

However, Shen Lang was overjoyed, no longer maintaining that posture of compromising before Xie Wei. That Imperial bearing suddenly returned to him, making him raise his arms and laugh loudly, “I knew it! In the end, this is the blood of my Imperial family! They absolutely will not disappoint my painstaking efforts!”

The entire Xinzhou Army immediately became highly alert as if facing a great enemy.

But Xie Wei did not seem surprised.

He stared at Shen Zhiyi, only smiled, and lightly raised his hand to wave it behind him.

Yan Lin glanced at him, then said to the entire army, “Make way for Her Highness the Princess.”

This order was simply baffling.

However, from the border to the capital, fighting all the way as their commander, Yan Lin had already established sufficient authority. Without needing to explain a single word, although everyone had doubts, they still quickly parted like a receding tide.

In the area before the Taiji Hall, which had originally been surrounded like an iron barrel, a path was thus opened up.

Shen Zhiyi looked toward Xie Wei and also saw Jiang Xuening in the corner, looking at her with some confusion. At that moment, her steps paused briefly, then she lowered her eyes. Without the slightest trace of fear, she led a contingent of black-armored soldiers and walked through the Xinzhou Army formation like a sharp arrow.

Now that reinforcements had arrived, what did Shen Lang have to fear?

This was all a contingency left behind by the late Emperor after he had suffered Prince Pingnan’s rebellion, to prevent such betrayals from happening again!

Using the Emperor’s private treasury, they had secretly raised an army at the border between Zhili and Tianjin!

For generations, they only heeded commands from the Imperial family. They could not be mobilized without an Imperial bloodline bearer holding the military tally!

He felt victory was assured and found this younger sister, whom he had always looked down upon, to be unprecedentedly pleasing to the eye. So he sneered coldly at Xie Wei, “Did you think I would truly submit without resistance? As soon as I learned of the changes in Xinzhou, I had plans in mind. I had Zhou Yinzhi send half of the military tally to Leyang. Three days ago, I carefully selected from among many court officials and sent Zhang Zhe to deliver the remaining half of the military tally. Zhou Yinzhi is crafty; I promised him great benefits. Zhang Zhe is upright; I appealed to his sense of righteousness. Those two could absolutely keep the secret and accomplish these two matters right under your nose!”

Zhang Zhe was upright and could keep secrets?

Xie Wei agreed with the first half of that statement, but as for the latter half…

He recalled how that Minister of Justice had straightforwardly revealed his purpose that day without any concealment, suddenly laughed, and actually glanced at Jiang Xuening.

Shen Lang knew nothing of this. When his gaze swept over those corpses lying on the ground, a look of humiliation appeared in his eyes, twisting his face.

At this moment, he directly gave the order.

He pointed his blade at Xie Wei and proclaimed loudly, “The Tianjiao and Xinzhou Army have colluded in rebellion. All of you, quickly capture this rebel leader and quell this revolt for me!”

There had originally been quite a few soldiers before the Taiji Hall.

When the Emperor said reinforcements had arrived, everyone became energized.

Almost as soon as Shen Lang gave the order, they picked up their swords and spears and charged forward!

The Xinzhou Army and Tianjiao side instinctively thought the situation had turned against them and had long been taut like arrows on bowstrings, ready to be released!

Those holding blades and swords were filled with rage.

The archers at the rear shot several thousand carved feather arrows down like rain!

How could that small force at the Taiji Hall compare with the Xinzhou Army?

Much less when the opposition held the advantage of archery.

In an instant, a swath fell behind Shen Lang. An expression of disbelief suddenly appeared on his face.

Because when he gave that order, Shen Zhiyi, standing on the steps, only closed her eyes and remained completely motionless!

Shen Lang was stunned. “Leyang, what are you waiting for?!”

An ominous premonition rose within him.

He flew into a rage, shouting hoarsely and cursing at the black-armored army behind Shen Zhiyi, who also had not moved, “You lot, are you all good-for-nothings?! I am ordering you to suppress the rebellion!”

Those black-armored soldiers’ faces also showed signs of hesitation, but Shen Lang had just killed his own blood relatives and was in such a deranged state; it made one’s scalp tingle.

Their gazes all turned toward Shen Zhiyi.

As long as Shen Zhiyi did not give the order, they all endured the cursing, remaining motionless and silent!

Xie Wei observed coldly from the side with great interest.

Shen Lang finally realized something was wrong. He changed his form of address. “Zhiyi, what do you want to do?”

Shen Zhiyi saw the corpses on the ground.

And her elder brother held a blood-stained blade in his hand.

It was not difficult to guess what had just happened here.

Even on the day of her marriage alliance, she had never felt such despair and disappointment. “What have you done?”

Shen Lang said, “It was I who had someone deliver the military tally to you! Imperial blood flows through your veins; you should shoulder your responsibilities! Would you watch this realm fall into outsiders’ hands?”

Shen Zhiyi laughed coldly. “Have I not shouldered them?!”

When she was in the palace, though her temperament was willful, she had always been considered docile.

This sudden retort almost stunned Shen Lang.

His face turned ashen. “What do you mean?”

Shen Zhiyi looked at him with some sorrow. “You’ve harmed loyal subjects, the borders are in turmoil, yet the one who went to the Tatars for the marriage alliance was me! Though Imperial blood certainly flows through your veins, and you even sit high on this supreme position, which thing you’ve done is worthy of your status? Master of all under heaven, sovereign of ten thousand people; are you even qualified?”

She had changed.

This Imperial Sister had changed.

Shen Lang finally realized belatedly: perhaps everything he had done before was not enough to bring about his eternal damnation, but this one thing before his eyes might bury everything he had originally planned!

He said, “Do you know what you are saying?”

Shen Zhiyi loudly shouted, “I know!”

Shen Lang’s eyes turned bloodshot. “Have you forgotten the words I had Zhou Yinzhi and Zhang Zhe bring to you?”

Shen Zhiyi said, “It’s precisely because I have not forgotten that I came today!”

Xie Wei, listening from the side for quite a while, suddenly found their Imperial family rather interesting.

Shen Jie, however, no longer understood what the two of them were arguing about. The corpses of Empress Dowager Xiao and Xiao Shu had already grown cold.

The arrows from earlier had even fallen beside him.

No one paid him any attention. Only Fang Miao, at the edge of the crowd, anxious and taking advantage of the lack of attention, pulled him aside.

Shen Lang looked at Shen Zhiyi without speaking.

Because the situation was almost even worse than the worst case he had imagined!

He had actually handed over the black-armored army for nothing!

But Shen Jie was useless, and he did not trust other relatives. That was when he thought of Shen Zhiyi. At that time, she was in Xinzhou, and with the popular support from her resolute marriage alliance back then, it naturally seemed that, as fellow bearers of Shen blood, Shen Zhiyi should stand on his side.

But he had been wrong.

Shen Zhiyi recalled those words in the letter and the words brought by Minister Zhang from the Ministry of Justice. She felt that her entire previous life had been manipulated by others. For a moment, she had infinite reflections and slowly said, “The words you had people bring were all correct. The strong prey on the weak; if one is meat, one cannot blame others for being the knife and chopping block. So today, I came. However, I did not come for you.”

Shen Lang’s jaw clenched tightly.

Shen Zhiyi looked at him and said, “I came for myself.”

When she spoke this sentence, even that last thread of hope Shen Lang had was extinguished.

Desperation could drive people mad.

He gripped that blade tightly and actually charged at Shen Zhiyi. However, the Xinzhou Army, which had originally been surrounding the area to control the situation, almost immediately reacted. No one knew whose foot was quick, but someone actually kicked him to the ground!

In recent years, alchemists had presented so-called “immortality pills,” and he had continuously consumed Five Mineral Powder. His originally decent body had long been hollowed out by medicines and debauchery. With this kick’s force, his leg bone almost broke. Prostrate on the ground, he simply could not get up.

His face became thoroughly twisted and ferocious.

However, all his fury was directed at Shen Zhiyi. “How dare you? Your surname is Shen; Imperial blood flows through your veins. How dare you kick someone when they are down at this time?!”

Tears rolled from Shen Zhiyi’s eyes. She only asked, “When I went for the marriage alliance, it should naturally be my duty as a princess of this nation; I went willingly. But when you all committed evil first and were incompetent after, when you placed me under house arrest and forced me to go to the borderlands thousands of li away, to barbarian territories, did you ever think that my surname is also Shen and Imperial blood also flows through my veins?!”

This sentence ultimately revealed several parts of hatred.

Shen Lang’s blade fell to the ground. Though he could not get up, he cursed incessantly. Where was there even a trace of his arrogant attitude from moments before?

Xie Wei walked over, picked up that blood-stained blade, and sighed, “It seems no one can save you now.”

Shen Lang shouted sternly, “Shen Zhiyi!”

Shen Zhiyi closed her eyes, as if restraining something. But what she had witnessed over these two years had already made her clearly understand that some people should live, while others only deserved to die.

But Shen Lang was, after all, her elder brother.

At this moment, she slowly opened her eyes, looked toward Xie Wei, lowered her posture, and requested of him, “I beseech you, Teacher, in consideration of past ties, to leave him an intact corpse.”

Xie Wei gazed at her, actually laughed, and agreed, “Very well.”

However, the next moment, his hand rose, and the blade fell!

Blood like a waterfall splattered red into everyone’s eyes. A head suddenly fell, rolling while stained with still-warm blood until it reached Shen Zhiyi’s feet. A pair of eyes turned upward, their appearance fierce and terrifying!

When everyone came to their senses, Shen Lang’s head and body were already separated.

Some civil officials could no longer bear such a bloody scene and covered their mouths, forcibly suppressing the churning in their stomachs.

Shen Zhiyi’s form stiffened for a moment.

When she lowered her head and saw clearly that face of Shen Lang, who died with eyes wide open, her fingers hanging at her sides, ultimately still clenched, and began to tremble.

She raised her head to look at Xie Wei.

This was what he promised as “leaving an intact corpse”?!

At this moment, even the most obtuse person realized something seemed wrong: clearly, this was not necessarily a situation requiring a life-and-death struggle; why did Xie Ju’an have to be so cruel and absolute?

Even Jiang Xuening was stunned.

It seemed many things she did not know had already occurred in the shadows.

CONTENT END 245

chapters.title: The Imperial Jade Seal
chapters.content:
With Xie Ju’an acting so strangely, who could connect him even the slightest bit to that sage-like Junior Tutor Xie of former days?

Even though his features had not changed in the slightest…

Let alone the court officials; even Lu Xian, who was already sufficiently familiar with him, could not help but twitch his eyelids, frightened by him until a chill emerged from his back!

However, Xie Wei remained as calm as the deep sea throughout, without stirring up even the slightest ripple. He casually and lightly kicked aside Shen Lang’s headless corpse with one foot, as if this were not the exalted Son of Heaven of former days but merely an insignificant object for him to manipulate at will.

Xie Wei gazed at Shen Zhiyi.

He simply said, “You are right. I am hypocritical and cunning, planning every step and calculating everything. The common people are suffering across the land, the masses displaced and homeless; to me, none of it matters. But this is simply who I am. If the Emperor wants me to kowtow, I will cut off his head. Even if I treat human lives like grass and weeds, what can the world do to me?”

Shen Zhiyi felt desolation in her heart and said, “Teacher also suffered greatly in years past and witnessed the tragic fate of the three hundred righteous children. People losing their homes, sons losing their fathers, the realm afflicted with calamity, and the common people wailing in anguish—can this not move even one or two parts of Teacher’s compassion?”

Xie Wei answered her calmly, “It cannot.”

This magnificent Imperial Palace, bathed in the gradually setting evening sun’s brilliant light, was steeped in blood, revealing an intense refinement, yet he did not like it at all.

He even laughed at this moment.

He said, “I once thought, Shen Lang and I are both flesh and blood mortals; why must I kneel to him and sacrifice my life for him? Heaven gave birth to all people, and everyone is its child, so why does only the Emperor dare call himself the Son of Heaven? Clearly, everyone is a Son of Heaven. But everyone is also grass and weeds. When all beings compete, they never show mercy; they kill when they want to kill and destroy when they want to destroy. If one were to ask why, perhaps one should ask Heaven. After all, when Heaven gives birth to people in this world, the only true equality has always been just one thing.”

Complete silence fell over the area as everyone looked at him.

Xie Wei’s brow and eyes relaxed as he continued lightly, “And that is death!”

Yet throughout the ages, the only difficulty had been death itself.

Some people fear death.

So today, he had come especially to send these people on their way.

Originally, aside from the word “death,” this world had no further principles to discuss, and he did not want to reason with anyone either.

At this very moment, Xie Ju’an was clearly calm and rational, yet for some reason, after hearing these words from him, everyone felt only a bone-chilling coldness arise from the depths of their hearts.

Such a mad person…

Even if he possessed intelligence and strategy superior to all others, who would dare let him control the realm?

Shen Zhiyi stood still and silent for a long time.

Meanwhile, Yan Lin seemed to be pondering something.

Before the Taiji Hall, the two armies confronted each other.

The atmosphere suddenly tightened to the extreme, and battle was about to break out!

Yet at precisely this moment, a delighted laugh suddenly rang out from inside the great hall, “Hahaha, the Emperor is dead! The little Emperor is dead too! This Imperial Jade Seal has finally fallen into this seat’s hands!”

Everyone suddenly froze.

Both sides in the confrontation almost could not hold back from attacking each other, but simultaneously turned to look into the Taiji Hall.

At some unknown point, Wan Xiuzi had actually reached the top of that golden throne hall, standing before the high Imperial desk, lifting in his hands that exquisitely carved Imperial Jade Seal!

No one had noticed how he got there.

They could only see that the wounds on his body were clearly still bleeding and the arrow shafts not yet removed, yet he seemed utterly unconcerned. He laughed with particular satisfaction, as if fulfilling a cherished wish, and then even walked toward the highest dragon throne!

When she saw that jade seal, Jiang Xuening was stunned for a moment.

She was all too familiar with this object…

But she did not notice that Yan Lin, standing beside her, was also gazing at this jade seal, with even a trace of unspeakable grief flashing through the depths of his eyes.

At this moment, his face grew solemn, and he actually gripped his sword and strode toward the interior of the hall.

Wan Xiuzi was about to sit upon the dragon throne.

Yan Lin lifted his foot and kicked him down, taking the Imperial Jade Seal that he clutched tightly with one hand, while his other hand reversed the grip on his long sword and thrust downward, directly piercing through his neck from behind!

The wild joy on Wan Xiuzi’s face had not yet completely faded.

His hand was even still reaching toward that dragon throne.

But Yan Lin simply pulled that long sword out mercilessly, and so what little fresh blood remained in his body also sprayed out entirely, submerging even the base of the dragon throne in crimson blood.

No one had anticipated this sudden turn of events.

Many were even confused for a time.

Why had Yan Lin suddenly struck?

Seeing him actually touch the jade seal, a court official could not help but shout angrily, “Treasonous villain, why not quickly put down the Imperial Jade Seal?!”

However, Yan Lin held the long sword in one hand and cradled the jade seal in the other, his deep black martial attire covering him like a layer of heavy shadow.

He completely ignored those people, not even turning back to glance at them once.

He simply looked toward Xie Wei, then toward Shen Zhiyi, but ultimately his gaze fell upon Jiang Xuening.

She still did not understand what was happening.

But a trace of ominous premonition swept through Lu Xian’s heart. His brow twitched as he suddenly realized something, his face abruptly turning cold as he demanded, “What does the Shizi intend to do?”

But his words had barely hit the ground when a “clang” was heard!

The long sword in Yan Lin’s hand actually flew from his grip and was nailed precisely into the ground three feet before him!

A rustling sound!

The Xinzhou Army soldiers around them almost instantly raised their weapons and simultaneously aimed them at Lu Xian in their center!

Before the entire great hall, the situation suddenly transformed!

Though the Xinzhou Army had Xie Wei behind them, he did not lead troops in battle. Even if he planned the overall situation, the one who commanded and directed the army was Yan Lin.

In the military, his word was law.

So at this moment, wherever his sword fell, the blades of the entire army almost all followed.

Lu Xian felt his hair stand on end.

Xie Wei was also somewhat surprised, though he did not react as strongly as Lu Xian. He simply observed him, seemingly wanting to know what exactly he intended to do.

The Imperial Jade Seal was a square block that one could grasp completely with both hands.

Throughout successive dynasties, only the Emperor could possess it.

But at this moment, Yan Lin did not lower his head to look at it even once. His gaze had not even moved from Jiang Xuening as he softly called to her, “Ningning, come here.”

Jiang Xuening was stunned.

Everyone’s gaze suddenly converged upon her.

An indescribable terror made her tremble slightly. Almost instinctively, she looked toward Xie Wei.

Xie Wei suddenly smiled and simply said to her, “Go.”

Yan Lin did not seem to like Xie Wei speaking this way at all. Without waiting for Jiang Xuening to respond, he repeated, “Ningning, come here!”

Jiang Xuening felt as if she’d fallen into a thick fog.

She slowly walked over, lifting her eyes to gaze at Yan Lin at this moment. That indescribable feeling, whether it was strangeness or familiarity, emerged once again.

But the young man before her used an incomparably earnest, even nearly greedy gaze to watch her, as if with every look, there would be one less to come. His moist black eyes were even tinged with traces of tears.

He actually placed the Imperial Jade Seal into her hands!

Jiang Xuening was trembling as she asked him in a shaking voice, “Who are you?”

But Yan Lin acted as if he had not heard, using an extremely gentle voice to coax her, “I was wrong. I will not take it anymore, will not take it ever again. I will give it all back to you, alright?”

Tears suddenly flooded from Jiang Xuening’s eyes.

The pain in that instant pierced to her very heart!

She would never forget; in her previous life, before Shen Jie passed away, he left an Imperial edict placing the Imperial Jade Seal in her hands, asking her to select a suitable Imperial clan member as the new heir apparent. Perhaps that kind and weak man had only wanted to leave her a talisman for survival. He never imagined that after it reached her hands, it would instead become her death warrant.

That day, they came to force her abdication.

She truly could no longer survive and so placed down both this jade seal and the edict…

Now, Yan Lin was saying to her: he would give it back to her…

Jiang Xuening bit down hard on her jaw; only this way could she restrain her trembling. Word by word, as if weeping blood, she asked him, “Who exactly are you?”

He wanted to help her wipe away her tears, but raised his hand only to draw it back again.

Yan Lin stood before her like a child who had done something wrong. After a long time, he finally said, “I do not know either…”

But did it really matter who he was?

It did not matter.

He finally remembered his plan again. Pulling her along, he walked to the entrance of the great hall, raised his hand to point at the silent and standing Xie Wei and Shen Zhiyi, and said to Jiang Xuening, “Come, now you choose everything! I stand on your side! Whoever you want to give this realm to, we will give it to them! How can the Empress be the most honored person in this world? The true person above all others is only the Emperor! If you are unwilling to choose anyone, then I will help you and kill them all clean!”

CONTENT END 246

chapters.title: Now Let Me Teach You
chapters.content:
In the end, was it Zhuang Zhou dreaming he was a butterfly, or the butterfly dreaming it was Zhuang Zhou?

At the very beginning, Yan Lin could still distinguish clearly.

However, when the dreams continuously visited in the deep of night, another set of memories constantly poured into his mind from beginning to end, he gradually began to lose the ability to tell them apart. Dream and reality, converging together, ultimately made it impossible to discern which one was the true self…

Or perhaps the two had already merged into one.

But the only thing he could clearly perceive was now, this time, this very moment!

He wanted her to love what she loved, gain what she gained, have all her wishes fulfilled, all her wounds healed…

Yet Jiang Xuening, who had been pulled to the front of this magnificent hall by him, only had a dreamlike feeling.

The Imperial Jade Seal was cradled in her hands.

Everyone within her line of sight had their gazes fall upon her.

If this were her previous life, she might have laughed aloud; after all, she had not obtained anything she wanted. But in this life, she clearly did not want it, yet others insisted on forcing it into her hands…

Past life and present life suddenly wove together into a strange absurdity.

Jiang Xuening suspected she was in a dream.

Yet the expertly carved dragon scales on the Imperial Jade Seal pressed against her palm, with some pain slowly seeping in; it was not false at all.

But how could this be?

How could she be the one to choose?

Jiang Xuening remembered that in her previous life, she had chosen an Imperial clan child who was only ten years old. Just after he was adopted as heir apparent, before he could even be enthroned, he was killed on the journey to the capital…

How could she dare to choose?

That terror, along with this jade seal delivered into her hands, surged up together. She shook her head, as if afraid of awakening some ferocious beast that would devour people at any moment. Holding the jade seal with both hands, she wanted to return it to Yan Lin.

She said, “No, I do not dare…”

However, Yan Lin did not reach out to take it. He only looked at her like a criminal undergoing punishment, with a gaze so silent it was almost pleading.

A cold laugh suddenly came from ahead. Xie Wei gazed at the two of them with eyes utterly devoid of emotion, though his words were directed at Jiang Xuening, “Do not dare this, do not dare that; when will you grow up a little?”

Jiang Xuening looked at him.

Xie Wei actually had no intention of objecting at all, but his voice grew colder with each sentence: “Either close your eyes and pretend you are randomly selecting a pig, or cut open your heart and look clearly at what you truly want!”

If Yan Lin’s earlier words had only shocked everyone into losing their ability to speak, unable to react for a long while, then at this very moment, Xie Wei’s words summoned back what little rationality remained in those who had been shocked senseless.

“A matter concerning the realm and the nation—how can it be treated so frivolously?”

“Are we really going to let this little woman decide?”

“Have you all gone mad?!”

“Absurd, simply absurd…”

…

Several elderly ministers beat their chests and stamped their feet, nearly becoming so agitated they could barely breathe.

The several thousand remnant soldiers of the Tianjiao were leaderless, and with Wan Xiuzi dead, they were all quite bewildered.

But looking left and right…

What Princess, what Shizi, what Second Young Lady Jiang—they did not recognize any of them!

What to do?

Everyone looked at each other in dismay, and no one knew who was so cowardly and eager to preserve their life that they first ingratiatingly shouted, “Of course, we choose our Master Dujun!”

This was immediately followed by a chorus of agreement.

Lu Xian’s scalp, which had just been made numb by the sword Yan Lin had thrown, had not yet completely recovered. Hearing the voices of these rabble and opportunists, he nearly spat out a mouthful of old blood!

So, without Wan Xiuzi, they were still hoping to preserve their lives by pledging allegiance to Xie Wei!

However, this group of good-for-nothings clamoring really did trigger wave after wave of commotion before, behind, left, and right of the great hall.

Not everyone in the Xinzhou Army necessarily obeyed Yan Lin; they all had their own thoughts. But seeing that Xie Wei seemed to have no intention of opposing Yan Lin whatsoever, they could not do anything for the moment.

Those who followed Yan Lin’s orders naturally remained still.

The numerous Black Armored Army behind Shen Zhiyi had never encountered such a situation either, but they were different from others. Originally established by the late Emperor to protect the Imperial clan, they naturally could not allow the Imperial Jade Seal to fall into other hands.

So at this moment, countless people actually drew their swords!

The sword edges all pointed toward Jiang Xuening, who cradled the jade seal!

They only waited for Shen Zhiyi’s command to charge forward, take Jiang Xuening’s life first, no matter what, and then seize back the jade seal in her hands.

However, what came was not the order to attack.

Shen Zhiyi was even calmer than Xie Wei. “Lower your weapons.”

Several generals behind her were stunned, “Your Highness?!”

Shen Zhiyi’s expression turned cold, her voice finally cooling by several degrees. “I said lower your weapons!”

“…”

The Black Armored Army was bewildered at this moment.

However, Shen Zhiyi’s attitude was firm. Even though they could not fathom it, after being puzzled for a long while, they finally, with some reluctance and unwillingness, put away the weapons they had raised and retreated to the rear.

Shen Zhiyi did not look at Xie Wei, nor did she look at Yan Lin. She only gazed at Jiang Xuening, slowly curving the corners of her lips. This faint smile that emerged softened all her features, making even that scar at the corner of her eye seem overflowing with radiance.

If in this world there was only one person she could trust with her whole heart…

Then, without a doubt, that person was Jiang Xuening.

She gently said to her, “Ningning, whoever you choose, that is who it will be. And I will also forever stand on your side.”

Even if she might choose Xie Wei.

But as long as she was willing, Shen Zhiyi thought, it did not seem like such a big deal. After all, being Emperor did not really mean one could do whatever one pleased.

In this instant, the civil and military officials who still retained some rationality were simply blown away until they could not find north, only feeling that a hole had been punctured in the sky!

One Xie Wei was not enough; add Yan Lin!

Now it was perfect; even Grand Princess herself had gone mad!

Finally, someone’s eyes rolled back, and their head tilted to one side, falling unconscious, causing chaos all around.

Xiao Dingfei, Fang Miao, and others in the corner looked at Jiang Xuening with almost admiring and envious gazes, vaguely carrying some fervor, as if anticipating what would happen next.

However, Lu Xian’s heart suddenly skipped a beat.

His gaze wandered among Xie Wei, Jiang Xuening, and Shen Zhiyi. In just a moment, he suddenly wanted to curse.

Wonderful! So this is what they were waiting for!

He had been wondering why Xie Ju’an had gone mad to this extent, insisting on acting as if he and Shen Zhiyi were incompatible as fire and water, locked in a life-or-death struggle!

What Yan Lin had just done was obviously not within his expectations, but he made no attempt to stop it, which proved this move was exactly what he wanted!

What Xie Ju’an had been waiting for was precisely this moment, wanting exactly this: to force someone into an impossible dilemma!

If one wanted to satisfy both him and Shen Zhiyi, how many choices were left for Jiang Xuening?

Lu Xian almost suspected he could already see the result.

Yet his heart still hung suspended at this moment.

Can Xie Ju’an truly win and have his wish fulfilled?

Jiang Xuening truly did not understand how everything had suddenly become like this.

Was it she who had gone mad, or were they who had gone mad?

Holding this Imperial Jade Seal, for the first time, she felt like a beggar carrying a golden mountain on her back; far from being happy, she felt she was about to be crushed to death, unable to catch her breath at all.

She was clearly nothing.

Yet everyone at this moment was watching her every move, even every glance, every look.

She first looked toward Shen Zhiyi, then looked toward Xie Wei, and memories related to these two people came flooding in.

One was a Princess, and the other was an Imperial Preceptor.

One had a benevolent heart, and the other was mad and obsessive.

One was female, and the other had become a rebel.

One regarded her as a confidante; the other was her teacher.

One had gone far away to the Tatars for a marriage alliance and returned to the palace after many ups and downs; the other had a mysterious background and suffered calamity in childhood, enduring humiliation to seek revenge and clear his name.

One carried in her body the blood of another person’s enemy; the other had just killed the other’s blood relative in front of her.

…

However, after all of this swept past, what remained in her mind was neither Shen Zhiyi nor Xie Ju’an. Rather, it was not long ago, on that rainy evening, when Zhang Zhe had looked at her with an extremely faint smile, so firmly telling her, “Your Majesty, you can.”

The waiting time was drawn out unbearably long.

Yet it was hard to tell whether only a quarter-hour had passed or already half a shichen…

Jiang Xuening, who had stood before the hall entrance for so long, finally moved.

She glanced at Xie Wei, her eyes reflecting a thousand turns and changes, yet she only showed him a somewhat peculiar smile before turning to walk toward Shen Zhiyi!

Yan Lin watched her intently without blinking.

Before the hall, an uproar suddenly arose.

Xie Wei’s hand hanging at his side suddenly clenched tightly with force.

Even Shen Zhiyi could only stare at her in stunned amazement.

Jiang Xuening stopped before her, remembering her first meeting with Shen Zhiyi in this life; she had taken up a brush and drawn a touch of cherry pink on that scar she had been so troubled by. From then on, Shen Zhiyi was good to her, and she was good to her in return.

What in the world could be better than this?

She simply said with a gentle smile, “Actually, welcoming Your Highness back from the Tatars was not my happiest moment. What made me happiest was seeing that Your Highness never again deliberately concealed the scar on your face. You finally accepted yourself. No matter what happens in the future, whether you establish a new Emperor or raise troops to stand independently, in Jiang Xuening’s heart, you will forever be that princess who loved all people despite having nothing and who left me with a promise of homeland.”

Tears suddenly fell from Shen Zhiyi’s eyes.

Yet Jiang Xuening lifted her hand and placed that heavy Imperial Jade Seal into her palm.

She said, “I want to believe in you.”

As her words fell, Xie Wei, standing behind her, swayed slightly. His tightly clenched fingertips dug deeply into his palm; he was nearly crushing his own fingers!

Loved all people despite having nothing!

It was not that he had not anticipated Jiang Xuening would make this choice, but those three words, “loved all people,” were like three extremely long iron nails hammered into his heart. Like a suddenly surging tide, they shattered all the composure and obsession he had been barely holding together!

A faint sweet taste of blood welled up in his throat. Xie Ju’an had never been this exhausted. Unwilling to hear another word, he turned directly and left with a sweep of his sleeves.

The dark gold sun sank in the west, his robes whipping in the wind.

Yet he had only just reached the long stairway when that familiar voice rang out behind him, “Xie Ju’an!”

Xie Wei stopped after all.

A moment later, a warm palm reached from behind him and grasped his hand.

Jiang Xuening gazed at him. “When I came, I already said I had something I wanted to tell you.”

How could Xie Wei not know?

That day, she had seen Zhang Zhe, and early the next morning, she said she had something she wanted to tell him.

Jianshu had secretly come to report it to him.

But…

He turned his eyes to look at her, his prominent Adam’s apple surging up and down, only saying, “I also said I do not want to hear it at all.”

In the carriage, she had wanted to speak several times.

But Xie Wei always told her to be quiet.

At that time, Jiang Xuening thought that perhaps, with their arrival in the capital approaching and the decisive battle imminent, this person might need a calm mind and settled spirit. So after failing to speak, she did not disturb him further, only thinking it would not be too late to speak in a couple of days.

However, seeing this person’s appearance now, what did she not understand?

How bitterly this person must have lived.

She nearly choked up, but she did not let go of him. She simply reached out to take the knife his right hand had been tightly gripping without release, and just as he had coaxed her in the cave back then, she said softly, “Put down the knife. I am right here. I will not leave.”

Xie Wei’s heart was full of deep, heavy violence.

He originally did not want to release it.

But he was also afraid that the knife would hurt Jiang Xuening’s hand, so in the end, he slowly let go.

She threw the knife down to the base of the stairs.

Around the Taiji Hall, where tens of thousands had gathered, for some reason, it suddenly became utterly silent.

That Imperial Jade Seal was pressed in her hand, yet Shen Zhiyi did not look at it. Instead, she looked toward Jiang Xuening, who stood very close to Xie Wei. She asked, “Ningning, do you know what kind of person he is?”

Jiang Xuening said, “I know.”

This person had forced her to her death in the previous life, and even in this life, he had still thought about taking her along to die. He was definitely not a good person; how could she not know?

She could even say she understood more clearly than anyone.

Because she had seen his truest and most insane side.

Shen Zhiyi asked again, “Do you like him?”

Jiang Xuening thought for a moment and said, “I do.”

In this instant, Xie Wei’s palm trembled lightly, yet in his mind it was as if ten thousand rays of light and shadow swept past, ultimately leaving nothing. He could only stare at her in a daze.

Yan Lin stood too far away; no one could see his blurred expression clearly.

Shen Zhiyi also did not speak for a long time.

She did not entirely approve of Xie Wei as a person, afraid that her Ningning would choose wrongly and be hurt. Yet she could not stop her. A thousand worries ultimately transformed into just one sentence: “Then do you truly understand what you are doing right now?”

Jiang Xuening smiled at her. “I understand clearly.”

And not only did she understand clearly what she was doing now, but she also knew what she would do in the future.

So she said calmly and frankly, “I am going to marry him.”

“…”

That evening, he had asked her once, but she had not answered, and he never dared ask a second time.

But now she said she was going to marry him.

Xie Wei suddenly could not distinguish whether this was real or a dream. Was she not supposed to leave him and go find Zhang Zhe?

Jiang Xuening looked at him and suddenly discovered she could actually read this person’s thoughts at this moment, so she could not help but laugh. “A long time ago, you told me that if you liked someone, you should hide it in your heart forever and not let that person know. But Xie Ju’an, if you truly like someone, how could you possibly hide it?”

Xie Wei did not understand.

Jiang Xuening could also see that he did not understand. “You truly are supremely intelligent, but you just do not know how to like people.”

When it came to romance, this person was hopelessly stupid.

At the slightest misstep, he would drill himself into dead ends.

Too afraid of losing what he possessed and also seemingly thinking that what was gained would ultimately be lost, he was obsessive, extreme, and stubbornly refused to show weakness to others or speak those words aloud.

Jiang Xuening suddenly felt this person was far too similar to the her of her previous life.

Not understanding certain things, so crashing into them until bloodied and broken.

She blinked, tears gleaming faintly in her eyes, yet she pulled his hand and stood on tiptoe to kiss his slightly cool, thin lips, saying in a low voice, “Teacher Xie, you taught me to read, write, play the zither, and how to be a person. But from now on, let me teach you; teach you how to properly like someone, alright?”

…

On that day, exactly how Xie Ju’an answered Jiang Xuening ultimately became a riddle in the history books that no one could ever solve.

Because, precisely at this moment when everyone was concentrating intently…

Before the entire Taiji Hall that was shrouded by the setting sun, Lu Zhaoyin’s voice suddenly rang out, gnashing his teeth, filled with bone-deep hatred, finally unable to restrain himself as he cursed loudly, “I knew it, I should have known all along! Using all that brilliant talent and grand strategy just to scheme and trick a young girl! I am done, I quit! This old man is going to change careers and become an official! I must have been possessed to rebel with you! Damn your ancestors!”

CONTENT END 247

chapters.title: Atmosphere of a New Dynasty
chapters.content:
“He cursed, and then what?”

In the gambling house, everyone was concentrating intently, even forgetting to place their bets. Hearing him stop at this point, they could not help but grow anxious and pressed him with questions.

The corner of Xiao Dingfei’s mouth twitched. Rolling his eyes, he forcefully tapped his fingers on the gambling table, loudly reminding this bunch of “idle good-for-nothing” gamblers, “Get this straight; we are here to gamble! Do you think this young master is a storyteller under some bridge? ‘And then what?’ Then hurry up and place your bets! What are you standing around for?!”

This was the capital’s largest gambling house.

All sorts of people from all walks of life came here.

He had originally been a regular here and made friends with a bunch of scoundrels. However, before the Tianjiao and Xinzhou Army fought their way in, the gambling house owner had fled the capital in fear, taking his valuables with him. Only recently, when everything seemed settled and things appeared to have calmed down again, did he return with his family to reopen.

Without a doubt, Xiao Dingfei, who had been cooped up at home bored nearly to death, rushed over at the first opportunity upon hearing the news.

The gambling house thus regained some of its former liveliness.

Everyone here had the kind of friendship with him that came from visiting brothels together, so they paid him no mind and insisted he continue, “But you are the only one who was in the palace that day! Not only did we not witness it, but we did not even dare stay long in the capital. Just tell us; after Lu Xian cursed at people, what happened then?”

Xiao Dingfei looked around and saw that, truly, no one was placing bets.

He now wished he could go back half an hour and slap himself twice:

Serves you right for not being able to hold back from bragging to others about what you know; now look what you’ve done! No money left to gamble!

Helplessly, he could only say impatiently, “What else? Making such a loud fuss at a time like that, he nearly got beaten up. Without even basic fighting skills, he was subdued in two or three moves and dragged out.”

Someone sighed, “To dare curse at that person—his courage is really something…”

Someone else did not quite believe it. “I’ve been to Youhuang Pavilion before. Boss Lu is a money-grubber, a shrewd merchant at heart. By logic, he believes in ‘harmony breeds wealth’; cursing like that does not fit. Is this part not made up by you?”

Xiao Dingfei rolled his eyes and thought about it. Actually, his memory was not particularly good. Nearly two months had passed, and he truly could not remember exactly what Lu Xian had cursed. He just remembered that face filled with indignation, as if he’d been deceived.

When others questioned him, he actually did feel a bit guilty.

But after all, he was a shameless person who had begged for food throughout the countryside and been beaten on every street corner in his younger days. Xiao Dingfei would never admit it. With a few quick words, trying to change the subject, he pretended to be angry. “You want to hear it, yet you do not believe what I am saying. Why are you so difficult to please? I say he cursed, so he cursed. If you do not want to listen, go find someone else to tell you! Do you really think this old man is a storyteller?”

With that, he made as if to leave.

How could the people in the gambling house really let him go?

They quickly pulled him back with kind words of persuasion.

Xiao Dingfei naturally went along with it and, after refusing twice, returned to the gambling table.

This bunch finally started gambling properly.

But while gambling, their mouths were not idle either.

After all, what happened two months ago when the Tianjiao fought into the capital and entered the Imperial Palace had long been spreading wildly among the common folk. However, exaggerated or fabricated information made up the majority. What actually happened that day? Everyone had their own version.

Some said the Emperor was killed by the Tianjiao leader.

Some said the Emperor was personally killed by Xie Wei.

Some even said Grand Princess Leyang had plotted to seize power and had schemed him to death.

But the people in this gambling house had already heard all that. What they were most curious about was not this.

Someone still could not figure it out. “There’s no doubt this Second Young Lady Jiang is a femme fatale, but how is it that Lu Zhaoyin said it was ‘tricking a young girl’?”

Xiao Dingfei thought to himself: “If I knew things that clearly, would I not have become an advisor instead of sitting here gambling with you?”

He was about to find something to say to deflect.

At this moment, a person dressed as a scholar sitting beside him smiled and said, “What Shizi Dingfei said, if true, is not hard to deduce. For Grand Tutor Xie to take this realm would be as easy as reaching into a bag for something. Grand Princess Leyang, at that time, controlled reinforcements and possessed the necessary strength for battle. Second Young Lady Jiang had saved the Grand Princess, so no matter what, the Grand Princess would not repay kindness with enmity and harm her, but with Grand Tutor Xie, it was uncertain. If Grand Tutor Xie controlled the realm, the realm would likely not be at peace. If the Grand Princess controlled the realm, Grand Tutor Xie might not have a good ending. So, did Second Young Lady Jiang not have to make a choice? If she married Grand Tutor Xie, the Grand Princess would love him for her sake. Even if she hated or feared Grand Tutor Xie in her heart, she would know Second Young Lady Jiang’s heart belonged to him and would absolutely not settle accounts after autumn.”

Hearing this, Xiao Dingfei actually thought it made some sense.

This speaking scholar was none other than Weng Ang, who had become the Bangyan74 two years ago. Back then, he had even gotten into a feud with the Xiao clan. He was willful and unrestrained, moving through markets and streets without putting on any airs of Hanlin Academy nobility—quite an unusual character.

However, his deduction was premised on everything Xiao Dingfei said being true.

In fact, the official court statement was: The Xinzhou Army led by Xie Wei and Yan Lin was indeed a loyalist force that chased all the way to the capital and joined hands with Grand Princess Leyang to eliminate the wicked Tianjiao, stabilizing the nation. So Xie Wei became Grand Tutor, Yan Lin was enfeoffed as Great General, and the Grand Princess temporarily ruled as regent.

History books were written by the victors.

Common people buried their heads in their daily lives; who would bother with such things?

This gambling bunch could not recognize many characters, but they practically fawned over scholars like Weng Ang.

After all, that was what you called insight.

So someone looked left and right, leaned in, and asked in a lowered voice, “Then in the future, who will be Emperor?”

Weng Ang held a position in the Hanlin Academy. Hearing this, he glanced at the person but did not answer.

Xiao Dingfei snorted coldly, “The court argues about it all day long; who knows!”

In these past two months, quite a lot had happened in the capital.

For instance, the Xiao clan was raided. From top to bottom, apart from Xiao Dingfei, this imposter who fortunately escaped disaster, everyone with the surname “Xiao” suffered greatly.

For instance, in the mass grave outside the city, they actually discovered the corpse of the former National Preceptor, Monk Yuanji. After investigating extensively without finding who did it, they instead discovered that this Yuanji was not any kind of eminent monk at all. He was involved in many murder cases and had even violated women; he was truly worse than a beast.

For instance…

For instance, the Emperor’s throne in the Forbidden City had been vacant for a full two months with no one sitting on it; it was simply an unprecedentedly rare occurrence throughout dynasties spanning thousands of years.

By logic, with Shen Lang dead and the Imperial Jade Seal in the Grand Princess’s hands, she should support the Imperial clan. Even finding a child from the Imperial family to serve as a child Emperor would be better than leaving the throne empty like this.

But with Xie Ju’an standing in court, who dared?

Many in the Imperial clan had witnessed that bloody scene at Taiji Hall that day and were scared witless, even less daring to make any rash moves. Moreover, with a regent Grand Princess above them, even if they wanted this position, they’d have to ask if she agreed or not.

So they stubbornly could not select anyone.

But every day, countless matters from provinces and prefectures throughout the realm needed the court’s mediation. Having just experienced warfare, the people needed to rest and recuperate. From household registration to taxation to the military, not a single thing did not require handling.

What to do?

The civil and military officials could only sit down together to discuss and handle things. Led by the original Cabinet ministers and including ministers from various departments, they convened daily in the Cabinet duty rooms to deliberate and formulate proposals. But lacking the previous step of the Emperor’s vermilion-brush approval and seal, after formulation, they submitted everything to Grand Princess Shen Zhiyi for review as a formality, then sent it unchanged to all departments and provinces.

At first, the court officials were somewhat unaccustomed to it.

But within a month, they discovered that whether or not there was an Emperor in court did not seem as important as they had thought. Directives were issued from the Secretariat; they were promulgated just fine without an Emperor. In fact, because they no longer needed the Emperor’s approval, memorials that arrived in the morning could be sent back to various localities or lower levels by afternoon—so much faster.

Moreover, when there was an Emperor, no matter how good an idea was, it would always be picked apart. The Emperor always had his own trusted favorites, and everyone had to be mindful of something.

Now it was perfect, completely unnecessary.

Even though there were still differences in official rank, no one truly dominated anyone else. Although factions quickly formed, everyone had the power to debate and contend, so no “one-man rule” emerged.

Furthermore, a month ago, because the Cabinet argued endlessly over “whether to plant potatoes or rice north of the Huai River” until no one would yield, leading to them grabbing “weapons” and fighting, the Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Rites jointly drafted temporary “Cabinet Regulations,” changing “proposal formulation” to “proposal voting.”

Everyone in the Cabinet had voting rights.

All directive formulations required voting. Those with the most votes were issued by the Secretariat to all departments and provinces. Cabinet “brawling” was strictly forbidden, including with rulers, inkstones, tables, chairs, vases, and cups.

Whether the Cabinet still fought now, Xiao Dingfei did not know.

But he figured the Emperor position was probably hopeless.

At the beginning, that bunch of old bastards kept saying things like “the state cannot be without a sovereign for a single day,” urging them to establish one. But this past month, gradually, there was not a peep about it.

After all, if they could handle everything themselves, why keep an Emperor to be their ancestor? What sense did that make?

Would that not just be asking for trouble?

Conveniently, the Grand Princess also did not seem to have any intention of legitimizing her mixed-blood son, so naturally, they turned a blind eye. With perfect tacit understanding, they “forgot” about “establishing an Emperor”; something that originally “mattered more than the heavens.”

Xiao Dingfei had not read many books and did not know what this actually meant, but anyway, however the court tossed and turned, it did not affect his gambling. Thinking about it, he was too lazy to consider it deeply and directly opened his dice cup with a loud laugh, “See that? Four fives and two sixes! Big, big, big; all this money is mine now!”

Everyone immediately cursed.

But a loss was a loss. They could only watch helplessly as he scooped all that pile of money on the gambling table into his arms.

Outside the window, the north wind was cold, and along the street someone was hawking hot wontons.

Hearing this, Xiao Dingfei realized his stomach was somewhat hungry. Sticking his head out the window, he wanted to call over the wonton seller to bring up a few bowls. But just as he was about to speak, his gaze shifted, and he suddenly froze.

He actually saw that Lord Zhang from the Ministry of Justice.

In this bitterly cold weather, he wore casual clothes, hands tucked in his sleeves, walking along the street.

Several barefoot little beggar children holding broken bowls were begging along the way when they reached him. He stopped to look at these children, then reached into his sleeve and took out not much—two bits of broken silver and a small handful of copper coins—and placed them in their bowls.

Then he raised his hand to point them in a direction, seemingly saying something.

The little beggars all showed delighted expressions, bowed to him, and ran hand in hand in that direction.

Xiao Dingfei knew that after recovering from the war chaos, there were many more displaced people in the city. With this cold weather, Grand Princess Leyang Shen Zhiyi had proposed to the Cabinet to establish soup kitchens in various places, providing relief from the national treasury, while simultaneously re-registering household records everywhere and distributing land to settle the displaced.

After some discussion, they formulated detailed regulations and passed them by vote.

Now there was a soup kitchen in the eastern part of the city, while the yamen re-recorded household registrations on-site and issued travel permits, providing settlement for these people.

Only this Lord Zhang…

Now promoted to Minister of Justice, yet still without any airs whatsoever.

Seeing this, he could not help but think back to two months ago…

After all the heart-stopping events in the Imperial Palace, ultimately, the flashing blades and swords returned to formlessness.

That young general watched for a long time, then, as if in a dream, without even smiling, simply turned and walked against the tide of people. He did not call even one personal guard and only carried a kind of weariness and desolation tinged with the vicissitudes of changing times as he slowly walked out the palace gates.

When Jiang Xuening saw him, he had already walked far away.

But she did not go forward to chase after him. She just watched from afar like that, a faint glimmer gathering in her eyes.

To this day, Xiao Dingfei still could not describe his strange feeling at that moment: He felt she did not seem to be simply watching a certain person, but rather watching the gradually receding past and former dust…

The Black Armored Army and Xinzhou Army both withdrew from the Forbidden City.

That bunch of Tianjiao trash was naturally arrested.

Xie Wei, Shen Zhiyi, and a group of court officials remained to deliberate on matters. Other people naturally wished they could leave this blood-stained palace as soon as possible and left immediately when they could. He, of course, greased his heels and fled faster than anyone.

But upon exiting the palace gates and reaching the streets, everything he saw was war-torn chaos.

The prosperous capital had become an empty city.

The high-hanging plaques of inns and medical halls had fallen to the ground, shattered into pieces. The exquisite carved windows of the pleasure quarters had been broken open with large holes, a complete mess. The wine flags that normally fluttered at taverns had been blown by the wind into the street, covered with many dirty and mottled footprints…

It was at this time that Xiao Dingfei saw Zhang Zhe.

In the deserted tavern, with doors and windows wide open, tables and chairs were toppled, and bowls and dishes were shattered on the ground, yet amidst all this devastation, a quiet and orderly space had been carved out.

One square table, one cup of clear wine.

That Lord Zhang sat alone at the table, slowly drinking a pot of wine by himself. After sitting for a while, he rose, placed a few coins for the wine on the counter covered with a thin layer of dust, and then came out.

On the street swept by the wind, not a single pedestrian could be seen.

The desolate city was like a dream.

Yet Zhang Zhe, as ordinary as in former days, walked through all this desolation, turned into a quiet alley, called “I am home” toward the door, lowered his head, pushed open the door, and walked inside.

That day in the capital was clearly one where winds and clouds gathered, danger lurked everywhere, and everything changed in an instant.

Those who valued their lives either scattered and fled or hid in their homes.

What kind of person would, on such a day, find an unmanned tavern, quietly drink a cup of clear wine, carefully leave a few coins for the wine, then return home as if it were any ordinary day?

Xiao Dingfei was truly dazed for a moment.

Someone beside him called, “Lord Dingfei, what’s wrong? Are we still gambling or not?”

Only then did Xiao Dingfei snap back to attention.

Looking again, the street ahead no longer showed any figure, nor the running beggar children, nor the peddler carrying a shoulder pole selling wontons.

He turned back with a smile, “Nonsense, this young master’s luck is running strong today; of course, we are gambling! This time, I will not let you leave until you’ve stripped off your pants!”

Everyone booed him.

He did not care. After happily putting away his money, he prepared to place new bets.

Someone suddenly asked strangely, “Speaking of which, it was one thing when you were called Xiao Dingfei before, but now that everyone knows you are a fake, why do you still use this name?”

Xiao Dingfei froze.

Who was he?

Born without roots, drifting wherever; even his name was picked from someone else’s discards.

The gambling house suddenly quieted.

The person who had just spoken belatedly became uneasy.

Unexpectedly, the next moment, Xiao Dingfei propped up his leg and became cocky, acting shamelessly carefree. “What else? Call myself Zhang Ergou or Li Erdan? Would you not find that tacky! What you are called does not matter; whether you can freeload food and drink is the key! This name of mine, the girls at Cuihong Pavilion call it so nicely.”

The previously tense crowd suddenly burst into laughter.

The topic immediately changed to which girl at Cuihong Pavilion was better.

Xiao Dingfei gambled until dusk was approaching before planning to return home to properly think about what to give the beauty and that Xie fellow for their wedding in a few days. However, his front foot had not even crossed out of the gambling house when his back foot heard the teahouse waiter across the street run back from somewhere, saying with some excitement to those inside, “Just heard news from the court; that Second Young Lady Jiang is moving into Kunning Palace!”

Pfft!

Xiao Dingfei spat out a mouthful of tea.

What kind of joke was this? The Emperor’s successor has not even been decided yet!

CONTENT END 248

chapters.title: The Cabinet
chapters.content:
Near evening, the north wind carried snow. Outside, the sky was darkening but not yet dark, vaguely tinged with an obscure rose color that pressed against the vermilion palace walls and golden glazed tiles. This actually concealed some of the deep heaviness from this palace that had recently been stained with blood, adding a bit of peaceful tranquility in the gradually brightening glow of dim palace lanterns.

In the Cabinet duty rooms, the finest silver charcoal burned.

The little eunuch who came to report was frightened into trembling, not daring to raise his head.

The court officials had already been quarreling incessantly.

Xie Wei acted as if he had not heard or seen anything. He simply sat by the window, holding a cup of tea, gazing at the white snow flying down from the deep, silent heights of the sky, thinking irrelevantly: Shen Zhiyi was deliberately opposing him. With his and Second Young Lady Ning’s wedding date approaching, she was rushing to add to his troubles.

“Absurd, simply absurd! What kind of place is Kunning Palace? Never mind that Jiang Xuening is an outsider, but the Emperor position still has not been settled yet! Empress Zheng just moved out from there, and the very next day, she moved in; what does this mean? What does this mean?”

“But is this not Grand Princess’s intention…”
